title: Staff Systems Engineer, HV Battery Software
description:
About Lucid

At Lucid, we are creating exceptional mobility experiences through innovation to drive the world forward. Built on Lucid’s proprietary technology and software-defined vehicle architecture, our award-winning vehicles bring our “Compromise Nothing™” approach to the global automotive market. That means refusing to choose between performance and sustainability, design and engineering, ambition and integrity. In Lucid Air and Lucid Gravity, we have designed and built vehicles that have redefined their segments, combining exceptional range, performance, design, and expansive space in a single experience.

We achieve this through deep vertical integration, with design, engineering, and production happening in-house across our global offices and manufacturing facilities. Our teams come from industries around the world, united by a shared commitment to excellence. By refusing to settle, you can help redefine what’s possible and shape the future of mobility.

Staff Systems Engineer, HV Battery Software

Role Overview

We are currently seeking a Staff Systems Engineer, High Voltage Battery Software to drive development and integration of Lucid’s proprietary Battery Management System (BMS) software. In this role, you will bridge the gap between early-stage prototypes and global production releases, ensuring our energy storage and powertrain systems operate with maximum safety, efficiency, and performance.

This position sits at the intersection of embedded software, power electronics hardware and vehicle network architecture. You will collaborate with engineers across systems engineering, hardware, controls, and verification and validation to perform complex architecture studies and drive architecture decisions, develop robust system requirements and drive hardware and software improvements for current and future Lucid vehicles.

Our ideal candidate exhibits a proactive, can-do attitude and approaches their work systematically and diligently. Candidates will be expected to demonstrate excellence in their respective fields, to possess the ability to learn quickly and to strive for perfection in a fast-paced environment.

Role responsibilities:

  • Perform functional decomposition to translate complex vehicle-level requirements into clear, verifiable, and traceable BMS and energy storage requirements
  • Perform system analysis and simulations to architect robust, scalable BMS frameworks and propose concept of operations to cross-functional teams
  • Collaborate with safety and reliability teams to perform FMEA, FTA and safety analysis to enable development of fault-tolerant embedded systems capable of real-time, safety-critical execution.
  • Define verification procedure and clear PASS/FAIL criteria for requirement verification and work closely with V&V teams to successfully complete integration testing and guarantee release quality.
  • Leverage large-scale telemetry and fleet-health analytics to proactively monitor battery performance, diagnose anomalies, and triage complex field issues.
  • Develop, validate, and rapidly deploy OTA software mitigations to resolve field anomalies and continuously improve battery safety and longevity.
  • Own configuration management, versioning, and release processes to ensure reproducible, auditable, and compliant deliveries.

What you bring:

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a technical related field is required. Master's degree or higher education is preferred.
  • 7+ years of experience in the field of BMS development or Energy Storage Systems developing embedded hardware and software for safety-critical, real-time systems
  • Deep understanding of Battery Management Systems, including cell modeling, state estimation (SoC/SoH/SOP), cell balancing, and fault diagnostics
  • Demonstrated ability to translate high-level system requirements into low-level embedded hardware and software requirements
  • Proficiency with requirement management process and experience with using at least one requirement management tool such as JAMA, Polarion, or 3DX
  • Proven experience with cross-functional software integration, configuration management, and automated Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) testing frameworks
  • Proficiency analyzing large-scale vehicle telemetry data (Python, SQL, or MATLAB/Simulink) to drive engineering decisions

Ways to stand out:

  • Experience with Model Based Systems Engineering methodology and tools such as Cameo, System Composer, etc.
  • Experience shipping OTA update pipelines for embedded/automotive systems at fleet scale
  • Hands-on experience with MATLAB/Simulink model-based design and auto-code generation for real-time targets
  • Familiarity with functional safety standards (ISO 26262/ASIL) and automotive cybersecurity (ISO 21434)
  • Experience with vehicle communication protocols and measurement data (CAN, CAN-FD, UDS, and isoSPI)
  • Familiarity with AUTOSAR architecture and its application in modern automotive software platforms
  • Experience with data pipelines and fleet-analytics tooling for anomaly detection and root-cause analysis
  • Proficiency in git tools and CI/CD for embedded software and automated regression testing

title: STNA
description:
The State Tested Nursing Assistant (STNA) provides essential care and support to residents in a healthcare, long-term care, or assisted living facility. Under the supervision of a licensed nurse, the STNA assists residents with daily living activities, such as personal hygiene, mobility, and feeding, while ensuring their comfort and well-being. This role is vital in promoting resident safety, dignity, and quality of life through compassionate and attentive care.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Resident Care:

    • Assist residents with activities of daily living (ADLs), including bathing, dressing, grooming, toileting, and oral hygiene.
    • Help residents with mobility, including turning, positioning, transferring, and ambulating using assistive devices as needed.
    • Feed residents or assist with meals, ensuring proper nutrition and hydration, and monitor food and fluid intake.
    • Monitor and report changes in residents’ physical, emotional, or behavioral conditions to the nursing staff.

  • Vital Signs and Monitoring:

    • Measure and record residents' vital signs, such as temperature, blood pressure, pulse, and respiration, as directed by nursing staff.
    • Assist with monitoring residents’ skin conditions, reporting any signs of skin breakdown or pressure sores.
    • Assist with weight checks, intake and output monitoring, and other health-related measurements.

  • Documentation:

    • Accurately document care provided and residents' responses to care in the facility’s electronic health record (EHR) or paper charts.
    • Maintain records of residents' food and fluid intake, toileting habits, and other observations as required.
    • Report any concerns or incidents to the supervising nurse and complete required documentation.

  • Resident Safety and Comfort:

    • Ensure residents’ safety by adhering to facility protocols and infection control guidelines.
    • Assist in maintaining a clean, organized, and comfortable living environment for residents.
    • Practice proper hand hygiene, use personal protective equipment (PPE) as required, and follow all safety procedures.

  • Emotional Support and Resident Interaction:

    • Provide compassionate care and emotional support to residents, engaging in conversation and offering comfort as needed.
    • Respect residents' dignity, privacy, and personal preferences, and promote their independence wherever possible.
    • Assist residents with social and recreational activities, encouraging participation to enhance their quality of life.

  • Team Collaboration:

    • Work collaboratively with nursing staff, therapists, and other healthcare professionals to ensure comprehensive care for residents.
    • Participate in care plan meetings and contribute to the development of individualized care plans.
    • Assist with transportation of residents to appointments, therapy sessions, or activities within the facility as needed.

Consistently provides friendly, courteous service to internal and external customers. Performs other related work. Generally works 6-8 hour shifts between 5:00 am and 10:00 pm.

Typical Duties and Responsibilities

  • Seeks opportunities to welcome, engage, serve, and thank customers. Maintains an atmosphere of friendly, enthusiastic customer service with an emphasis of taking care of the customer.
  • Takes orders, answers questions, and performs suggestive selling.
  • Prepares, stocks, displays, straightens, and rotates product in fresh food areas (Deli/Seafood/Pizza).

  • Handles frozen product.
  • Inspects all product for quality and freshness
  • Prepares case by putting the product in fresh pans, rotating product, putting product back, filling, etc.
  • Places proper signage on all products which includes pricing, description, code dating, and COOL information on all required products.
  • Cleans and maintains department equipment such as fryers, slicers, etc. by breaking down and reassembling equipment, operating dish washer and hand washing dishes, cleaning all appropriate parts with sanitizing solution.
  • Maintains clean and sanitary department by washing parts, tables and wrapping stations; taking trash and paper to the appropriate balers; cleans floors and coolers; cleaning and maintaining glass display counters on the inside and out; etc.
  • Receives inventory, stocks, verifies receipt of ordered product and orders.
  • Follows strict sanitary guidelines and completes associated records.
  • Performs other duties as assigned or needed.
  • Understands and follows all food safety procedures and requirements.

Requirements

Ability to:

  • Work varied shifts in a 24/7 operation; including night, weekends and holidays.
  • Communicate (hearing & speech) effectively with customers to receive orders and perform customer relation skills.
  • Conduct visual inspections, read and follow production guides, recipes and product labels, log production quantities, temperature readings, etc. on proper forms.
  • Perform basic math (add, subtract, divide and multiply) and compute weights and measures.
  • Perform duties with mental alertness involving potential hazards with respect to related procedures, equipment (e.g., knives) and work aides.
  • Complete training course and meet minimum time standards of productivity and accuracy.
  • Wear hair net, beard net and gloves and other personal protective equipment as required.
  • Use cleaning chemicals and handle related food products.
  • Stand, walk and move rapidly for extended periods of time.
  • Bend, stoop, twist, turn and reach over the counter and in tight areas frequently.
  • Lift up to 50 lbs. occasionally and reach, push and pull racks.
  • Handle refrigerated goods (-20°F to 28°F)
  • Work around machinery emitting heat (400°F rotisserie and 325°F hot shortening).
  • Must be 16 years of age or older.
  • Perform primary duties efficiently and accurately.

Additional Requirements:

  • Food Handlers Certification (Per State Laws)

Machines and Equipment Operated:

  • Cash Register
  • Film over wrapper, digital scales, etc.
  • Knives and other kitchen utensils.
  • Electric Slicers
  • Deep fryers, ovens, etc.
  • Oil filtering machine
  • Dishwasher
  • Trash compactor
  • Cardboard bailer
  • Hand, pallet jack
  • Conveyor ovens

The honest version of this ad:

Most Principal Engineer and Solution Architect ads read like a certification checklist wearing a blazer. We're not doing that.

Here's what's actually true: We're supporting a Google Cloud Partner working with genuinely large, complex customers, the kind still mid-migration off VMware and other clouds, not the kind who “just need someone to tidy up the diagrams.” You'd be the person customers trust to turn a messy Rehost / Replatform / Refactor decision into an architecture that actually survives contact with production.

If you’ve ever sat in a stakeholder meeting translating "why is this so slow" into a real GCP fix, keep reading!

What you'd actually be doing:

  • Designing the migration, not just diagramming it: Leading Rehost, Replatform, and Refactor strategies off VMware and other clouds onto GCP, and staying hands-on through to go-live, not handing it off after the pitch deck.

  • Running Compute, Serverless, GKE, and Cloud Run like they're all in your muscle memory: Picking the right compute model per workload instead of defaulting to whatever's familiar.

  • Making IaC and GitOps the default, not the exception: Terraform modules and GitOps pipelines that clients can actually own after you leave the room.

  • Bringing AI/ML into the architecture conversation: Vertex AI and BigQuery pipelines, with a working knowledge of where agentic frameworks (Agent Builder, ADK) genuinely fit vs. where they're hype.

  • Being the "why" behind the "what": Translating gnarly technical trade-offs into a narrative an exec will actually approve.

  • Mentoring as you go: Levelling up the Engineers around you, not hoarding the interesting problems.

What you won't be doing:

Sitting in an ivory tower producing architecture diagrams nobody implements. This is a build-and-ship role, you're the Architect and the Engineer!

What you'd bring to the role to have a meaningful impact:

  • Real commercial experience, specifically architecting and shipping on Google Cloud (not just “cloud-adjacent”).

  • Real depth across Compute, Serverless, GKE, Cloud Run, networking, and data services, the stuff that holds up under a real client audit, not just a whiteboard.

  • Terraform and GitOps fluency at the “clients can maintain this” level.

  • Python, Go, or Bash comfort, bonus points if you've touched Vertex AI or BigQuery pipelines in anger.

  • Professional Cloud Architect certs (or the hands-on runway to prove you don't need it).

  • Consulting instincts, where you can run a requirements session and defend a proposal without a script.

  • A genuine track record of building things, not just approving other people's builds.

We have a long-term history with this team, and we know exactly who you would be working with and supporting in this key role, so look no further if you are motivated by working for genuine down to earth humans who roll up their sleeves and lead from the front with their team, whilst they strive to stay at the forefront of the Google tech landscape...

title: SAP S/4HANA Delivery Manager
description:
Company Overview

Responsibilities

We are seeking an experienced SAP S/4HANA Implementation Project Manager to lead enterprise-scale digital transformation initiatives across our organization. This position is tailored for a seasoned professional with deep management consulting experience who is looking to transition into an internal industry role, taking true operational ownership of delivery from initial scoping through post-go-live stabilization.

The ideal candidate will demonstrate progressive leadership through at least three full-lifecycle SAP implementations, reflecting career growth from functional module lead to integration manager and into broad program or project management.

This role is located onsite in Reno, Nevada. This is not a hybrid or remote role.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead the end-to-end planning, execution, and delivery of major SAP S/4HANA implementation and optimization programs. This includes establishing rigorous scope management, schedule baselines, project charters, resource allocations, and budget governance.

  • Drive proactive alignment between executive business sponsors, operational process owners, internal IT teams, and external system implementation partners. You will facilitate decision-making forums and steering committee updates to maintain transparency and resolve roadblocks early.
  • Direct critical delivery phases including requirements gathering, process blueprinting, solution design, conference room pilots, integration testing, and cutover simulation. You will be responsible for defining acceptance criteria and go-live readiness gates across the enterprise.
  • Oversee data migration, legacy system decommissioning, third-party integration points, and overall testing strategy. This involves guiding teams through unit testing, end-to-end integration testing, user acceptance testing (UAT), and system performance testing.
  • Partner with organizational change management leads to execute comprehensive communication, training, and business readiness programs. You will ensure operational teams are fully prepared to adopt new digital processes with minimal business disruption during cutover and hypercare.

Qualifications

Preferred Qualifications & Certifications

  • Substantial prior experience working within a premier technology consulting firm or boutique SAP integration practice before moving into an in-house industry leadership role.
  • Active Project Management Professional (PMP) or Program Management Professional (PgMP) certification from the Project Management Institute (PMI).
  • Formal SAP certifications in SAP S/4HANA implementation, SAP Activate project management methodology, or specific functional modules.

  • Exposure to modern cloud platforms (such as RISE with SAP, AWS, Azure, or GCP) and related cloud enterprise architectures

Education/Experience

Required Experience & Skills

  • Proven track record leading or co-leading complex SAP S/4HANA greenfield or brownfield implementations in large enterprise environments. Candidates must understand the nuances of migrating legacy ERP ecosystems to S/4HANA platforms.
  • Successful participation in approximately three full-lifecycle SAP deployments demonstrating progressive career growth. Your progression should ideally reflect prior responsibilities as a functional module lead, an integration manager, and an overall project delivery lead.
  • Deep familiarity with SAP implementation lifecycles, cross-module touchpoints, interface technologies, and middleware dependencies. You should be capable of challenging technical assumptions and validating solution architecture feasibility.
  • Strong vendor management and negotiation skills when working with third-party system integrators and software partners. You will be expected to hold vendors accountable to statement-of-work deliverables, milestone timelines, and quality benchmarks.
  • Exceptional executive presence, verbal communication, and written presentation capabilities. You must be able to distill complex technical and functional challenges into clear business trade-offs for C-level executives and steering committees.

Education & Academic Background

  • Undergraduate Degree (Required): A Bachelor’s degree in Management Information Systems (MIS), Computer Science, Software Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Business Administration, Finance, Supply Chain Management, or a closely related quantitative/technical discipline is required. Equivalent practical experience demonstrating strong technical and operational acumen will also be considered.
  • Advanced Degree (Preferred): A Master of Business Administration (MBA) or a Master of Science in Information Systems, Technology Management, or Project Management is highly desirable. Advanced coursework or degrees help bridge strategic business objectives with complex technical architectures.
  • Continuous Learning: Demonstrated ongoing professional education in enterprise architecture, cloud transformation, enterprise software release management, or modern agile delivery practices is strongly valued.

You'll also regularly visit our Sydney clients for preventative maintenance, projects, troubleshooting and onsite support.

Our Sydney clients are predominantly located throughout the Sydney suburbs rather than the CBD, so you'll need to be comfortable travelling between client sites when required.

For us, it's about outcomes: doing great work, looking after the client and getting things done professionally and efficiently.

What You'll Be Doing

You'll work across a varied range of client environments, handling everything from everyday support requests through to more complex infrastructure and Microsoft 365 issues.

Day-to-day responsibilities may include:

  • Diagnosing and resolving technical issues remotely using our support and management platforms

  • Microsoft 365 administration and troubleshooting

  • Microsoft Entra ID / Active Directory

  • Windows Server environments

  • Remote Desktop Services and RemoteApp environments

  • Group Policy, authentication and user configuration

  • Microsoft 365 Exchange Online and email troubleshooting

  • Windows 10 and Windows 11 endpoints

  • Networking, internet and Wi-Fi troubleshooting

  • Microsoft SQL environments supporting industry-specific applications

  • 3CX and business communications

  • Endpoint, backup and security monitoring

  • Preventative maintenance and proactive client checks

  • Basic scripting and automation

  • Assisting with infrastructure upgrades and technology projects

You'll be allocated work through our service management platform, but this isn't purely a reactive helpdesk role.

Between support requests you'll also perform proactive maintenance, review client systems, check backups and monitoring platforms, identify potential problems and look for opportunities to improve the client's environment before something breaks.

Onsite Client Work

A key part of this role is being ClubIT's technical presence in Sydney.

While much of your normal support work can be completed from home, you'll regularly attend client sites throughout the Sydney suburbs to perform:

  • Preventative maintenance visits

  • Technology health checks

  • Infrastructure troubleshooting

  • Network and Wi-Fi work

  • Hardware installation and replacement

  • Projects and upgrades

  • Client meetings and technical reviews

  • Escalated onsite support

You'll therefore need a current driver's licence and the ability to travel to client sites around Sydney.

The Person We're Looking For

Technical ability matters, but so does how you work with people.

Our clients need someone who can walk into their business, communicate confidently with management and staff, solve problems and represent ClubIT professionally.

We're looking for someone who can:

Our Team

Position Overview

A yard parts puller is responsible for identifying, locating, and removing automotive parts from damaged or salvaged vehicles. The employee plays a critical role in the auto salvage industry by providing quality parts for repairs, ensuring efficient inventory management, and delivering excellent customer service. The parts puller's efficiency in extracting parts in a timely manner helps build customer loyalty and contributes to the organization's reputation for reliability and excellent customer service, which contributes to the organization's financial success.

The Parts Puller I job description encompasses the Parts Puller in Training and Parts Puller I job duties. This position is paid hourly and is non-exempt.

Key Responsibilities and Essential Job Functions

  1. Fulfillment – Parts Pulling
  • Identify and remove parts from vehicles using hand and power tools
  • Inspect parts for quality before they are removed from vehicles to ensure that they are in good condition and meet the organization's quality standards
  • Parts pullers may need to clean parts before they are sold or added to inventory, using water and soap to wash off dirt and grime or using a solvent or degreaser to remove oil or other contaminants
  • Notify the sales team of damaged parts, including identifying the part and providing details on the damage.
  • Support the fulfillment department and assist with any other duties, as assigned.
  • Maintain a clean and safe work environment by keeping the yard vehicle clean and organized, as well as following all safety guidelines and procedures to ensure a safe work environment.
  • Parts pullers may need to operate heavy equipment to assist in repositioning vehicles to gain access to pull parts, depending on the site.

2. Quality Control

  • Inspect parts for quality and defects; ensure only high-quality parts are retained for sale.

3. Customer Service

  • Parts pullers may need to interact with customers who are looking for specific parts.

4. Safety

  • Utilize expertise in operating heavy equipment and to safely move vehicles and parts.
  • Utilize expertise in operating the assigned yard vehicle around the facility
  • Adhere to safety regulations, environmental regulations, and company policies while performing duties.
  • Ensuring all equipment is properly inspected and following proper lifting and handling techniques to prevent injuries.
  • Wearing proper personal protective equipment (PPE)
  • Reports any issues to their supervisor.

5. Perform Other Duties as Assigned

title: Gaming Designer
description:
About the Role

Culmen International is seeking a Gaming Designer.

This position involves designing and developing serious games, simulation-supported activities, and interactive exercise experiences for public health and medical preparedness, response, recovery, and continuity missions. The position transforms exercise objectives, operational plans, threat information, and subject-matter expertise into realistic game mechanics, scenarios, participant decisions, and multimedia products that enable readiness and improve performance.

What You’ll Do in Your New Role

  • Design, develop, test, facilitate, and refine serious games and simulation-supported activities for federal, state, local, tribal, territorial, regional, and interagency audiences.
  • Translate exercise objectives, plans, policies, capabilities, corrective actions, and operational challenges into game concepts, rules, roles, decision points, scenario modules, and measurable outcomes.
  • Develop realistic scenarios, storylines, injects, timelines, participant materials, facilitation questions, control-cell products, and Master Scenario Events Lists.
  • Apply HSEEP doctrine and sound instructional, experiential-learning, and game-design principles to seminars, workshops, tabletop exercises, games, drills, functional exercises, and full-scale exercises.
  • Incorporate computer simulation, model outputs, visual interfaces, video vignettes, video injects, and virtual-delivery capabilities into exercise programs when appropriate.
  • Collaborate with modeling and simulation specialists, systems designers, planners, facilitators, evaluators, analysts, multimedia personnel, and subject matter experts to produce integrated exercise experiences.
  • Support concept and objectives meetings, initial and midterm planning meetings, in-progress reviews, MSEL development and synchronization meetings, final planning meetings, exercise execution, hotwashes, and after-action meetings.
  • Prototype and playtest game mechanics and supporting materials; collect participant and stakeholder feedback and revise products to improve realism, usability, accessibility, and alignment with objectives.
  • Develop evaluation criteria and data-collection opportunities that allow exercise teams to assess decisions, actions, coordination, plans, policies, and corrective-action implementation.
  • Review technical and analytical products and interpret modeling or simulation results for incorporation into exercise design and real-time participant play.
  • Prepare and deliver briefings, demonstrations, facilitator guidance, participant instructions, technical documentation, and decision-support materials.
  • Maintain awareness of current industry standards, emerging technologies, virtual environments, and best practices in serious gaming, simulation, and exercise design.
  • Complete recurring and short-turn assignments within established deadlines and maintain accessible, organized project files and deliverables.
  • Travel as authorized to support planning conferences, exercise delivery, evaluation, training, real-world response activities, or stakeholder meetings.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in game design, simulation, instructional design, emergency management, public health, computer science, digital media, or a related field.
  • Relevant experience designing games, simulations, or interactive exercises for the U.S. Government or another complex operational organization.
  • Experience developing scenarios, game mechanics, injects, participant materials, facilitation content, and exercise-support products.
  • Experience incorporating technical data, model results, or simulation capabilities into realistic decision-based activities.
  • Ability to interpret operational requirements and convert complex subject matter into clear, engaging, and objective-driven participant experiences.
  • Ability to collaborate with multidisciplinary teams and communicate effectively with technical and nontechnical stakeholders.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft 365 applications and the ability to learn and use Government-provided exercise, collaboration, multimedia, and virtual-delivery tools.
  • Ability to manage multiple concurrent priorities and respond effectively to short-notice or surge requirements.

Desired Qualifications

  • Knowledge of HSEEP doctrine and experience supporting the full exercise planning, conduct, evaluation, and improvement-planning cycle.
  • Experience supporting public health preparedness, emergency management, incident response, continuity, consequence modeling, or interagency operations.
  • Experience creating visual interfaces, video vignettes, video injects, digital game assets, or virtual simulation environments.
  • Experience facilitating games or exercises for senior leaders, government personnel, emergency responders, healthcare partners, or interagency audiences.
  • Familiarity with the National Response Framework, National Incident Management System, Emergency Support Function #8, and federal preparedness and response doctrine.
  • Experience developing accessible digital and multimedia products consistent with Section 508 requirements.

Culmen International is committed to enhancing international safety and security, strengthening homeland defense, advancing humanitarian missions, and optimizing government operations. title: Personal Care Attendant III
description:
Do you have a background or interest in healthcare and a passion for helping older adults and their families? Are you looking for a rewarding career where you can make a meaningful difference while working in a supportive, team-oriented environment?


Join Woodlands Senior Living—we’re hiring immediately!

At Woodlands Senior Living, you’ll have the opportunity to make a positive impact in the lives of seniors while building a fulfilling career with a trusted Maine organization.

We are proud to be the first senior living organization in Maine to earn accreditation from The Joint Commission. This recognition reflects our commitment to high standards of quality, safety, and experience for the residents, families, and team members we serve.


About Woodlands Senior Living

Woodlands Senior Living is a Maine-based, family-owned and operated organization providing assisted living and memory care throughout Maine. Our mission is simple: to make each day the best day possible for every resident we serve.

Our team members are committed to:

  • Providing compassionate, high-quality care to older adults
  • Supporting residents and their families with dignity and respect
  • Creating a safe, welcoming, and inclusive environment
  • Working collaboratively as part of a supportive team
  • Upholding high standards of professionalism, quality, and service

If you’re passionate about helping others and want a career where your work truly matters, we’d love to have you join the Woodlands Senior Living team.


Position Summary

Full-Time, Part-Time, and Weekend Opportunities Available!

As a member of our resident care team, you will play an important role in helping our residents live safely, comfortably, and with dignity. You will provide compassionate assistance with daily activities, personal care, and other services based on each resident’s individual needs, assessment, and service plan.

You will work as part of a supportive team and follow applicable federal and state regulations, company policies and procedures, and established standards of care.


Key Responsibilities

  • Provide supervision and assistance with Activities of Daily Living (ADLs), including transferring, mobility, bathing, dressing, grooming, personal hygiene, toileting, and eating.
  • Assist residents with Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADLs), including appointments, telephone use, transportation, housekeeping, laundry, meal preparation and service, and shopping.
  • Provide medication administration services as permitted by your training, certification, and applicable regulations.
  • Provide resident care in a manner that promotes safety, dignity, independence, and quality of life.
  • Observe residents for changes in physical condition, behavior, or overall well-being and promptly report and document concerns in accordance with company policies and applicable regulations.
  • Obtain and accurately document vital signs as assigned.
  • Follow each resident’s individualized assessment and service plan.
  • Maintain appropriate confidentiality and protect resident information in accordance with company policies and applicable privacy requirements.
  • Work collaboratively with other members of the resident care team to provide consistent, high-quality care.
  • Perform other duties within the scope of your training and responsibilities as needed to support our residents and team.

Resident Information & Confidentiality

Team members may access resident records and protected health information (PHI) only as necessary to perform their job responsibilities and support quality of care, compliance, and regulatory requirements. All resident information must be handled with appropriate confidentiality and in accordance with company policies and applicable laws and regulations.


Working Conditions & Physical Requirements

This position involves regular interaction with residents, families, team members, healthcare professionals, and regulatory personnel in a senior living environment.

The position may require:

  • Frequent standing, walking, bending, reaching, and assisting residents with mobility and daily activities.
  • Working on carpeted and concrete surfaces throughout the community.
  • Working varying schedules, including weekends, holidays, extended hours, or in other roles when business or resident needs require.
  • Responding to emergency situations, including severe weather, evacuations, and other unforeseen circumstances.
  • Exposure to common healthcare and senior living workplace conditions, including cleaning products, disinfectants, odors, dust, and other environmental factors.
  • Following established infection prevention and safety practices when working with residents who may have infectious illnesses or other health conditions.

At Woodlands Senior Living, every team member has an opportunity to make a meaningful difference in the lives of our residents. If you’re compassionate, dependable, and committed to providing exceptional care, we invite you to join our team.

title: Team Leader, SRE
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Team Leader, SRE based in Spain.

As Team Leader, SRE, you’ll lead a highly technical Site Reliability Engineering team responsible for the reliability of critical cloud infrastructure and developer platforms.
The role combines approximately 60% hands-on technical contribution with 40% people leadership, giving you meaningful influence over both engineering direction and team development.
You’ll work across Kubernetes, AWS, PostgreSQL, CI infrastructure, observability, security, and reliability practices.
You’ll help evolve a growing SRE function, strengthening SLOs, incident response, on-call practices, and operational excellence.
At the same time, you’ll own the career development, performance, hiring, and overall health of your team.
The environment is fully remote and asynchronous, requiring strong written communication, autonomy, and thoughtful prioritization.
This is an opportunity to shape reliability practices while remaining close enough to the technology to guide decisions and lead through complex incidents.

Accountabilities

  • Lead and develop an SRE team, owning the full career lifecycle of direct reports, including onboarding, feedback, performance management, progression, and hiring.
  • Coach engineers on both technical craft and interpersonal skills, creating clear opportunities for growth and development.
  • Foster a healthy, collaborative team environment by understanding team dynamics, addressing conflicts constructively, and maintaining effective retrospective practices.
  • Represent the SRE team across engineering and with senior leadership, communicating priorities, challenges, progress, and technical direction.
  • Define and prioritize SRE objectives, balancing operational commitments with project delivery and protecting the team's focus.
  • Own the support rotation and on-call model, ensuring sustainable operational coverage and effective incident response.
  • Provide technical leadership across core infrastructure, including Kubernetes, AWS, PostgreSQL, DNS, TLS, CI infrastructure, and related platform services.
  • Drive the evolution of reliability practices, including Service Level Objectives (SLOs), error budgets, incident management, observability, and post-incident improvements.
  • Partner with Security teams on infrastructure threats, patching, security controls, audits, and compliance requirements.
  • Oversee infrastructure-related vendor relationships, including renewals and commercial discussions in collaboration with senior leadership.
  • Stay hands-on enough to review technical work, challenge architectural decisions, contribute to complex problems, and provide credible technical direction during incidents.
  • Help mature the organization's reliability practices by identifying operational gaps and turning lessons from incidents into lasting engineering improvements.
  • Balance short-term operational demands with longer-term platform investments and engineering goals.

    • Requirements:

    • Proven experience leading an SRE, infrastructure, platform, or DevOps engineering team, with direct responsibility for team members' growth, performance, and career progression.
    • Strong people-management and coaching skills, with demonstrated ability to develop engineers and provide clear, constructive feedback.
    • Experience hiring engineers and assessing both technical capability and broader engineering judgment.
    • Strong conflict-resolution and team-dynamics skills, with the ability to build commitment around shared organizational goals.
    • Deep hands-on experience in Site Reliability Engineering, DevOps, cloud infrastructure, or a closely related discipline.
    • Production experience with Kubernetes, including operational troubleshooting, reliability, scaling, and real-world failure scenarios.
    • Significant experience with AWS and cloud infrastructure at meaningful scale.
    • Hands-on experience building, enabling, or scaling AI infrastructure.
    • Strong understanding of observability principles and practices.
    • Experience with Infrastructure as Code, particularly Terraform.
    • Experience with CI/CD platforms such as GitLab CI, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, or comparable technologies.
    • Strong knowledge of Docker and shell scripting.
    • Experience owning or operating reliability practices including incident response, on-call, SLOs, error budgets, and post-incident improvement processes.
    • Previous experience working in regulated environments and understanding the associated operational and compliance requirements.
    • Exceptional prioritization skills, particularly when operational workload competes with project delivery.

    • Experience with a backend programming language such as Elixir, Java, Clojure, Node.js, Python, or similar is a plus.
    • Familiarity with modern observability technologies such as OpenTelemetry, distributed tracing, or Honeycomb is advantageous.
    • Experience with PostgreSQL or Aurora operations, including performance, connection pools, and query optimization, is beneficial.
    • Experience administering Linux systems outside cloud environments is a plus.
    • Knowledge of infrastructure security from both defensive and offensive perspectives is advantageous.
    • Familiarity with cloud cost management and FinOps is beneficial.
    • Experience growing an engineering team from a small starting point, including establishing hiring standards, is a plus.
    • Fluent English communication skills are required.
    • Ability to work effectively in a fully remote and asynchronous environment.

      • Benefits:

      • Flexible, asynchronous working model that allows you to organize your schedule around your life.

title: Sr. Configuration Management Specialist
location: Fort Walton Beach, Florida, United States
description:
At Zone 5 Technologies, we're redefining what's possible in unmanned aircraft systems. Our team of engineers and innovators is developing cutting-edge autonomous solutions that push the boundaries of UAS technology - solving complex challenges that matter.

We're building the future of UAS capabilities, and we're looking for exceptional talent to join us. If you're driven by hard problems, energized by rapid innovation, and ready to make an impact on next-generation flight systems, you belong here.

Position Overview

Join our growing aerospace and defense organization as a Senior Configuration Management Specialist (Level III). This role independently executes and coordinates configuration management across assigned programs, products, and lifecycle phases. The specialist partners with Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Software, Systems Engineering, and Program Management to maintain configuration integrity from concept and development through production, delivery, and sustainment.

The Level III specialist serves as a trusted program CM practitioner and may lead defined workstreams, facilitate change-control activities, and mentor less-experienced team members. This is an individual-contributor position aligned to enterprise CM governance and direction from the Senior Configuration Manager.

This is one onsite position with location flexibility. The selected candidate may be based at the Dallas-Fort Worth, Fort Walton Beach, or San Luis Obispo site and should identify their preferred location when applying.

What You Will Do

  • Own day-to-day configuration management execution for assigned programs, products, and projects while ensuring alignment with enterprise policies, program plans, contracts, and applicable industry requirements.
  • Develop and maintain program configuration management plans, procedures, work instructions, checklists, and lifecycle records under enterprise CM governance.
  • Establish, document, and maintain configuration identification and product structures for hardware, software, firmware, documentation, interfaces, and technical data.
  • Coordinate functional, allocated, product, production, as-built, as-tested, and as-maintained baseline activities as required by the program lifecycle and contract.
  • Support and facilitate Configuration Control Boards (CCBs) and Software Configuration Control Boards (SCCBs), including agenda preparation, change-package readiness, stakeholder coordination, decision records, and action tracking.
  • Review engineering change requests, engineering change orders, deviations, waivers, problem reports, and related change documentation for completeness, traceability, classification, effectivity, and implementation planning.
  • Maintain configuration status accounting for approved changes, baselines, releases, effectivity, serial applicability, open actions, implementation status, and technical data deliveries.
  • Verify that approved changes are fully implemented across affected drawings, specifications, bills of material, work instructions, software repositories, test artifacts, planning records, and downstream business systems.
  • Help maintain alignment among requirements, design data, EBOMs, MBOMs, SBOMs, ERP/MRP, MES, QMS, PDM/PLM, and software-development repositories to strengthen the digital thread.
  • Perform release-readiness and baseline-completeness reviews before production, test, delivery, or major technical milestones.
  • Support functional and physical configuration audits, production readiness reviews, first article activities, customer reviews, and internal or external compliance assessments.
  • Identify and resolve configuration discrepancies involving engineering data, manufacturing planning, software versions, effectivity, serialized product records, and as-built documentation.
  • Coordinate configuration records and technical data packages required for customer delivery, contractual reporting, audit readiness, and product acceptance.
  • Contribute configuration management scope, assumptions, schedules, risks, deliverables, and basis-of-estimate inputs to proposals and program planning activities.
  • Develop program-level metrics and concise status reports covering change throughput, aging actions, baseline health, release readiness, implementation completion, and emerging CM risks.
  • Provide practical CM guidance and training to cross-functional stakeholders and mentor junior CM personnel in established processes and tools.
  • Collaborate across operating sites to promote consistent execution while addressing local program and production needs.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in engineering, systems engineering, information management, business, or a related discipline, with at least five years of relevant configuration management experience; an equivalent combination of education and directly applicable experience may be considered.
  • Hands-on experience performing configuration identification, change control, status accounting, baseline management, release management, implementation verification, and configuration audits.
  • Experience supporting complex hardware, software, firmware, or integrated product development in aerospace, defense, manufacturing, or another highly regulated environment.
  • Working knowledge of engineering drawings, specifications, bills of material, part and document revision control, effectivity, serialization, and product lifecycle records.
  • Ability to evaluate change packages for cross-functional impact and trace changes through engineering, manufacturing, quality, supply chain, test, software, and delivery records.

$95,000—$126,000 USD

  • Comprehensive benefit package options include medical, dental, vision, life, and more.

title: M04 - Helpdesk Support Engineer
description:
Role Overview

We are seeking an ICT Operations Support resource to support the operational takeover and steady-state management of enterprise ICT platforms, mobile services and related services.

The role will provide continuity across multiple stakeholders, drive day-to-day operational follow-through, maintain service and funding visibility, support service management continuity, oversee mobile and device operations, and coordinate service improvements and security-conscious operating models for different user populations.

Key Responsibilities

Portfolio Operations, Funding and Service Management

  • Review current IT processes, structures, and ways of working to understand how well they support business needs.
  • Manage and track subscriptions, billing, cost recovery, funding, procurement / logistics interfaces, utilisation and payment reconciliation.
  • Maintain the operational picture for service requests, quotas, migrations, lease extensions, outstanding actions and key dependencies.
  • Coordinate service teams, Service Reps, Finance/Funding, Procurement and other supporting parties to drive actions to closure.

Technical Service Management Operations and Continuity

  • Gather and document key assumptions that will guide IT improvements.
  • Coordinate day-to-day service management activities and interfaces covering subscriptions, billing, service requests, quotas, site operations and escalation.
  • Track staffing, contract, funding, security clearance and understudy / replacement arrangements to mitigate transition risk plans for moving from current to future state.

Mobile and Device Operations

  • Oversee mobile service procurement, demand, device/account mapping, configuration, onboarding, handover, replacement, reassignment and termination.
  • Maintain accurate device, subscription and user entitlement records and coordinate resolution of operational issues.

Service Flexibility and Security Controls

  • Support exploration of differentiated operating models for different target audiences, including eligibility, approvals and provisioning arrangements.
  • Coordinate assessment of proportionate security controls for different user populations, including temporary staff and the feasibility/governance of MAC-based access or whitelisting controls where applicable.

Governance, Documentation and Improvement

Maintain action / decision trackers, SOPs, RACI matrices, process flows and the Operations Handbook / Handover Pack.

Identify gaps and improvement opportunities and coordinate implementation with the relevant service, security and technical owners.

Requirements & Qualifications

Educational Qualification & Experience

  • Experience in public-sector or large-enterprise ICT environments.
  • 8+ years of experience with enterprise service models, shared services or vendor-managed ICT services.
  • Working knowledge of complex enterprise ICT operating environments is advantageous.

Technical & Professional Competencies

  • Understanding of ICT service delivery, operations, service management and vendor management.
  • Familiarity with asset / device lifecycle management, endpoint provisioning, software baseline controls and access-control concepts.
  • Ability to work with funding, billing, subscription, asset and service records and reconcile operational dependencies.

Soft Skills & Communication Attributes

  • Strong coordination, analytical and problem-solving skills with disciplined follow-through.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication and stakeholder facilitation skills.
  • Strong documentation, process visualisation and action-tracking capability.
  • Ability to communicate operational and security considerations clearly to both service and non-specialist stakeholders.

title: Team Leader, SRE
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Team Leader, SRE based in Netherlands.

As Team Leader, SRE, you’ll lead a highly technical Site Reliability Engineering team responsible for the reliability of critical cloud infrastructure and developer platforms.
The role combines approximately 60% hands-on technical contribution with 40% people leadership, giving you meaningful influence over both engineering direction and team development.
You’ll work across Kubernetes, AWS, PostgreSQL, CI infrastructure, observability, security, and reliability practices.
You’ll help evolve a growing SRE function, strengthening SLOs, incident response, on-call practices, and operational excellence.
At the same time, you’ll own the career development, performance, hiring, and overall health of your team.
The environment is fully remote and asynchronous, requiring strong written communication, autonomy, and thoughtful prioritization.
This is an opportunity to shape reliability practices while remaining close enough to the technology to guide decisions and lead through complex incidents.

Accountabilities

  • Lead and develop an SRE team, owning the full career lifecycle of direct reports, including onboarding, feedback, performance management, progression, and hiring.
  • Coach engineers on both technical craft and interpersonal skills, creating clear opportunities for growth and development.
  • Foster a healthy, collaborative team environment by understanding team dynamics, addressing conflicts constructively, and maintaining effective retrospective practices.
  • Represent the SRE team across engineering and with senior leadership, communicating priorities, challenges, progress, and technical direction.
  • Define and prioritize SRE objectives, balancing operational commitments with project delivery and protecting the team's focus.

  • Drive the evolution of reliability practices, including Service Level Objectives (SLOs), error budgets, incident management, observability, and post-incident improvements.
  • Partner with Security teams on infrastructure threats, patching, security controls, audits, and compliance requirements.
  • Oversee infrastructure-related vendor relationships, including renewals and commercial discussions in collaboration with senior leadership.
  • Stay hands-on enough to review technical work, challenge architectural decisions, contribute to complex problems, and provide credible technical direction during incidents.
  • Help mature the organization's reliability practices by identifying operational gaps and turning lessons from incidents into lasting engineering improvements.
  • Balance short-term operational demands with longer-term platform investments and engineering goals.

    • Requirements:

    • Proven experience leading an SRE, infrastructure, platform, or DevOps engineering team, with direct responsibility for team members' growth, performance, and career progression.
    • Strong people-management and coaching skills, with demonstrated ability to develop engineers and provide clear, constructive feedback.
    • Experience hiring engineers and assessing both technical capability and broader engineering judgment.
    • Strong conflict-resolution and team-dynamics skills, with the ability to build commitment around shared organizational goals.
    • Deep hands-on experience in Site Reliability Engineering, DevOps, cloud infrastructure, or a closely related discipline.

    • Significant experience with AWS and cloud infrastructure at meaningful scale.
    • Hands-on experience building, enabling, or scaling AI infrastructure.
    • Strong understanding of observability principles and practices.
    • Experience with Infrastructure as Code, particularly Terraform.
    • Experience with CI/CD platforms such as GitLab CI, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, or comparable technologies.
    • Strong knowledge of Docker and shell scripting.
    • Experience owning or operating reliability practices including incident response, on-call, SLOs, error budgets, and post-incident improvement processes.
    • Previous experience working in regulated environments and understanding the associated operational and compliance requirements.
    • Exceptional prioritization skills, particularly when operational workload competes with project delivery.
    • Strong written communication skills and comfort working in an asynchronous, globally distributed environment.

    • Experience with a backend programming language such as Elixir, Java, Clojure, Node.js, Python, or similar is a plus.

UnityPoint Clinic

Referral Center Representative

Monday-Friday 8:00AM-5:00PM

Find a fulfilling career and make a difference with UnityPoint Health.

As Commercial Counsel, you’ll be the first dedicated legal hire supporting a rapidly growing AI business with complex commercial and regulatory needs.
You’ll take ownership of customer, supplier, and partner agreements, handling drafting and negotiations under US law from initial review through signature or resolution.

Working closely with Finance, founders, customers, and external advisers, you’ll build reusable templates, negotiation positions, and workflows that make legal work more efficient.

Apply now and take the next step towards a rewarding legal career with Law Partners.

title: Graduate Firmware Engineer
description:
About Graphcore

Graphcore is a global leader in artificial intelligence computing systems. We design advanced semiconductors, software, and data center systems that provide the specialized processing power needed to advance AI while improving the efficiency required for broad adoption.

As part of SoftBank Group, Graphcore belongs to a family of companies developing transformative technologies. Our U.S. engineering teams contribute to the hardware and software platforms that support the next generation of AI systems.

The Opportunity

We are looking for a recent graduate or early-career engineer to join the BMC Engineering team as a Graduate Firmware Engineer. You will develop low-level and embedded firmware that supports the operation, control, monitoring, and validation of advanced compute systems.

You will work with experienced firmware, hardware, systems, and software engineers throughout the development lifecycle. The role combines hands-on implementation with automated testing, lab-based debugging, hardware bring-up, and analysis of interactions between firmware and the underlying platform.

What You Will Do

  • Design, implement, test, and maintain system and embedded firmware in C, C++, or Python.
  • Take ownership of defined firmware features and deliver them from requirements and design through implementation, validation, and documentation.
  • Develop and debug firmware in a Linux-based engineering environment using appropriate diagnostic tools and techniques.
  • Create automated tests and scripts that improve firmware validation, test coverage, and engineering efficiency.
  • Contribute to continuous integration and delivery workflows for firmware development and testing.
  • Plan and conduct engineering experiments, analyze test data, and communicate findings clearly.
  • Support lab setup, system configuration, hardware bring-up, and firmware validation on development platforms.
  • Investigate firmware behavior and hardware-software interactions, identify root causes, and implement verified fixes.
  • Work across BMC, firmware, hardware, silicon, systems, and software teams to reproduce and resolve technical issues.
  • Write clear design notes, test procedures, change descriptions, and technical findings.
  • Follow established engineering and coding practices and contribute constructively to code and design reviews.

What You Will Bring

  • A bachelor's or master's degree in computer engineering, electrical engineering, computer science, or a closely related field, completed recently or expected before the role begins.
  • A strong foundation in C or C++ and working knowledge of Python or another scripting language.
  • Understanding of computer architecture, embedded systems, firmware, and low-level software concepts.
  • Familiarity with Linux environments, command-line development tools, and version-control systems.
  • Experience applying structured debugging methods to software, firmware, or hardware-software problems.
  • Ability to interpret technical requirements, break work into manageable tasks, and deliver reliable results with appropriate guidance.
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively across engineering disciplines.
  • Curiosity, sound engineering judgment, and willingness to learn new technologies, tools, and development methods.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Academic, internship, or personal project experience developing embedded software or firmware.
  • Experience with microcontrollers, embedded processors, system-level firmware, or hardware bring-up.
  • Experience using lab equipment to test or debug hardware-based systems.
  • Experience with automated testing, Python scripting, or continuous integration workflows.
  • Exposure to baseboard management controllers, platform management, data center hardware, or high-speed compute systems.
  • Experience debugging interfaces or interactions between hardware and software.

These qualifications are helpful, not required. We encourage you to apply even if you do not meet every preferred qualification.

United States Benefits Overview

Graphcore offers competitive compensation and programs designed to support employees' health, financial well-being, flexibility, and development. Benefits for eligible U.S. employees may include:

Benefits vary by work location, employment status, and plan eligibility and are subject to the terms of the applicable plans and company policies. This overview is not a contract or guarantee of benefits.

Articulates messages in a way that is broadly understandable. Models and encourage the expression of diverse ideas and opinions. Actively listens and checks for understanding. Not afraid to have the conversations that are needed for the greater good.

title: Logistics Specialist L3, AWS Logistics Services
description:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Logistics Specialists play a vital role in the success of Amazon Web Services by providing the right part, in the right place at the right time. Your contribution to this success would be maintaining the onsite parts room in AWS Data Centers, by managing the custody of computer hardware through their entire lifecycle. This involves receiving parts, safely storing parts, picking and delivering parts to hardware technicians, cycle counts, and shipping faulty hardware back to the vendor.

You will work closely with Data Centre Operations and Engineering teams to ensure reliable functioning and repair activities to support our customers, while adhering to our operational tenants of safety, security and availability.

Key job responsibilities
- Maintaining inventory to ensure that proper stock levels are managed to support build and repair activities.
- Physically receiving and issuing out of parts as needed for internal customers.
- Loading, unloading and transporting parts between different sites.
- Keeping accurate stock records for all items within our care through physical cycle counts.
- Maintaining the safety, organization, and cleanliness of all workspaces using Amazon 7S principles
Travel:
- The role may require the successful candidate to travel to other sites in the in the Melbourne metro area to assist in conducting cycle counts, receiving stock into the inventory control system, replenishing stock and returning defective stock. Travel between sites will require own transport, all travel related costs will be reimbursed.

Physical / Environmental Demands:
- Amazon Operates with a principle of safety first. With this principle, we take significant care to ensure all employees operate in a safe manner and have appropriate tools to support them in undertaking their roles safely. The activities below are required with the safety principle applied.
- Loading and unloading shipments.
- Standing, sitting, and walking (including stairs) for prolonged periods of time.
- Willing and able to frequently push, pull, squat, bend and kneel.
- Reach and stretch to position equipment and fixtures while maintaining balance.
- Push or pull heavy objects of up to 16kg into position and participate in group lifts of 20kg or more.
- Coordinate body movements when using tools or equipment.
- Work with and/or around moving mechanical parts.
- Work in an office and warehouse environment where the noise level is low to moderate.

A day in the life
The MEL Data Center Logistics team, supports infrastructure deployment across Melbourne's data center cluster. We manage the end-to-end logistics lifecycle — receiving, ingesting, inventory management, and cycle count accuracy — ensuring critical components are available to keep builds on track. Our culture is built on ownership, continuous learning, and bias for action. We've developed a structured training program that accelerates on boarding and equips new members to contribute quickly. Operating across multiple MEL sites, we embrace start-up challenges as opportunities to build scalable processes. Our work directly enables AWS to serve millions of customers worldwide.

Your day will be spent carrying out Logistical support functions for our Data Centers. This will involve physical control and processing of spare parts transactions, consumables stock replenishment, and cycle counting of stock.

About the team
About AWS

Diverse Experiences
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

Inclusive Team Culture
AWS values curiosity and connection. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.

Mentorship and Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

title: Solutions/Software Analyst/Scientist/Engineer - Workflow
description:
About Us

Founded in 2011, Fulgent has evolved into a premier, full-service genomic testing company built around a foundational technology platform.

Through our diverse testing menu, Fulgent is focused on transforming patient care in oncology, anatomic pathology, infectious and rare diseases, and reproductive health. We believe that by providing a wide range of effective, flexible testing options in conjunction with best-in-class service and support, we can redefine the way medicine is managed for patients and clinicians alike.

Since integrating with our therapeutic development business, Fulgent is also developing drug candidates for treating a broad range of cancers using a novel nanoencapsulation and targeted therapy platform. By merging our fields of expertise, we aim to become a fully integrated precision medicine company.

Summary of Position

We are seeking a full-time entry-level hybrid analyst/scientist/engineer to join our fast-growing family. We are an engineering focused culture with multiple technical teams: Interface, Workflow, Distributed Systems, Bioinformatics, and IT. We are the backbone of the company and work closely with other teams: Lab, Genetic Scientists, Research, Client Services, Marketing, Sales, and Management. Our primary responsibility is to ensure the operations of the lab, scaling its growth, and augmenting its capabilities. You'll be evaluating operational processes, building solutions, developing algorithms, coordinating projects, and managing clinical genetic data. You are expected to learn about bioinformatics, genetics, and medical science to aid the diagnostic quest to improve the lives of the patients around the world. You are expected to perform administration, analyst, scientist, and engineering roles to aid our pursuit of providing next level diagnostic services to patients in need. You are expected to participate in bringing new diagnostic solutions to the market. You will be expected to apply computer science beyond programming.


Key Job Elements

This hybrid analyst/scientist/engineer role at Fulgent is an assortment of multiple professions. It is expected that all roles listed are fulfilled. The individual must have a strong understanding of each role and be able to fulfill them as needed within company projects, team projects, or within individual projects. Specialized operational, analytical, and technical training for all roles are provided for entry-level hires. All individuals in this position are expected to join projects, products, and teams within the capacity required of them. They are expected to be, or will become, strong at interdisciplinary knowledge sharing and exchange. This job position requires creative thinking, in-depth technical knowledge, and intellectual analysis. There will be times when you are expected to be project leaders and other times when you will be project members. This allows leaders to practice being followers and followers the opportunity to lead. Your primary responsibility is to ensure successful operations within the lab. This may require you to solve complex business, scientific, or engineering problems using analytical, procedural, and/or creative abilities.

It is expected that you will learn and understand our required clinical standards/guidelines (ACMG, ACOG, CLIA, CAP, HIPAA, HITECH, etc.) so that you may act as advisory specialists to other departments and leads. When capable and trained, it is expected that you will participate in establishing operational policy and procedures to be followed by other departments. This position is not simple. This position is not standard. It will require a strong foundation within Computer Science, Mathematics, and/or Statistics to be applied within all roles. Computer Science, Mathematics, or Statistics are not industries within themselves, but a catalyst to other industries. As a clinical diagnostics lab, we are members of the healthcare industry. As a research lab, we are members of the genetic biotechnology industry. As a technology lab, we are members of the solutions, systems, and integration industry. It is expected that you will understand, or learn, genetics, biology, computation, business, operations, management, analytics, and administration. It is expected that you will understand, or learn, their applied forms of clinical reporting, diagnostic procedures, next-generation sequencing analysis, software engineering, bioinformatic annotation, product management, leadership, data science, business intelligence, and high-throughput workflow management. You will be reporting to your department lead, Jimmy Liu. It is expected that you will be assisting your department and your department lead towards successful operations and successful projects.

You’ll review responses generated from personalized prompts and information retrieved through connected Google applications.
Your work will focus on relevance, accuracy, contextual understanding, personalization, and the overall quality of the user experience.
You’ll identify subtle issues such as incorrect assumptions, irrelevant recommendations, inconsistencies, and inappropriate personalization.
The role requires careful analysis and strong written communication to turn observations into clear, actionable feedback for AI model improvement.

title: Athletic Trainer
description:
Overview

Concentra has an immediate need for an experienced and passionate Full-Time ATC at our client's site in Green Bay, WI. This position offers an opportunity to work at a dynamic worksite and make an impact on employee health, wellness, and safety!

Salary: Starting at $68K (negotiable)

Schedule: Monday-Thursday 6AM-2:30PM and 2 flexible hours each week at our local brick and mortar

Sign-On Bonus: $1,500.00

Are you ready to take your career to new heights? At Concentra, you will be a vital member of our patient care team and play a crucial role in providing exceptional care to our patients. Our mission is to improve the health of America's workforce, one patient at a time. Join us at Concentra and see how your clinical competency and compassion can make a meaningful difference in the lives of the patients you serve.

As an Onsite Athletic Trainer, you will promote and maintain health and wellbeing for client based occupational medicine program focusing on delivering exceptional patient care and reducing work-related injuries. The Certified Athletic Trainer-Onsite (CAT-O) plays an important role in workers’ compensation case coordination, worker injury and illness management, providing health promotion and injury prevention services, emergency response services, and return to work job placement for an onsite client. The CAT-O often works directly with the client’s Health and Safety Leader to create a healthier and safer workforce.

Responsibilities

  • Provide basic first aid treatment for musculoskeletal and non-musculoskeletal injuries and illnesses as specified in Physician Standing Orders, testing such items as range of motion and strength, reflex and sensory integrity, and functional status
  • Identify, evaluate and refer injured associates to the appropriate clinicians in order to receive the best care for their work-related injuries and illnesses
  • Follow appropriate action plan and standing orders to respond to onsite medical emergencies
  • Assist in managing Workers' Compensation cases through claim capture and follow-up
  • Collaborate with client’s Human Resources team and management on return to work (RTW) job placement
  • Track and communicate MSD-related statistics for client stakeholders
  • Manage pre-employment functional testing process and provide vision acuity testing
  • Coordinate injury prevention programs, as well as ergonomic training and evaluation
  • Perform comprehensive ergonomic job analyses, including task analyses, risk factor identification and quantification, posture analysis and body mechanics analysis and support administrative and ergonomic changes to the work environment
  • Create job rotation plans for production areas and monitor compliance
  • Create pre-shift preventative activity program and monitor compliance
  • During rehabilitation, implement treatment plans that incorporate therapeutic exercise, modalities and work conditioning as necessary (State-specific regulations apply) as specified in Physician Standing Orders
  • Use innovation, creative solutions and employee empowerment to design and/or implement interventions
  • Administer drug and alcohol testing
  • Promote personal health and wellbeing in the workplace
  • Perform data analysis to measure direct and indirect costs of musculoskeletal disorders
  • Provide monthly and annual reports for rehab utilization, cost-savings, and cost avoidance
  • Perform administrative requirements such as completing necessary forms, reports, etc. in a timely manner. Documentation may include patient files, invoices, monthly reports, budgets, expense and outcome tools.
  • Create an environment of trust and caring, which allows workers to take responsibility to reduce or eliminate actions or behaviors under their control that contribute to injury and illness
  • Communicate regularly with safety personnel regarding rehab and injury prevention activities
  • Attend meetings and serve on committees as requested
  • Author articles for various newsletters and the company Intranet site as requested

This job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

  • Active and current license to practice in the state of jurisdiction if applicable
