title: Transfer Admissions Counselor - Traditional Day
location: Fort Wayne Campus - Fort Wayne, IN 46803
description:
Indiana Tech is a thriving, independent, teaching-oriented institution with a focus on career-oriented programs in business, engineering, information technology and computer science, criminal justice, life sciences, human services, and many other concentrations. Indiana Tech enrolls nearly 1,500 students in its traditional undergraduate programs on its picturesque main campus and nearly 5,000 students in its College of Professional Studies programs online and onsite at 15 regional locations. Degrees are offered at the associate, bachelor, master, and doctoral levels.

Over 41% of our students are either globally or domestically diverse; this contributes to our unique vibrant and inclusive campus community. All academic programs are designed to provide students with relevant and practical experiences, including an emphasis on internships. The university is accredited by the Higher Learning Commission.

Indiana Institute of Technology embraces diversity and equal opportunity intentionally. We are committed to building a team that represents a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. We believe that diversity and inclusion among our employees is critical to our success with respect to educating our students to become global citizens. Indiana Tech is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

Indiana Tech has big plans for its future. Learn more at Indiana Tech Strategic Plan.

Reporting to the Executive Director of Admissions, the Transfer Admissions Counselor is responsible for recruiting, counseling, and enrolling prospective transfer students into Indiana Tech’s traditional undergraduate programs. This position serves as the primary point of contact for transfer students throughout the admissions process, including application review, transfer credit evaluation coordination, financial aid guidance, and enrollment advising.

The Transfer Admissions Counselor develops and maintains relationships with community colleges, faculty, staff, and external partners to facilitate transfer pathways and increase transfer student enrollment. The position works collaboratively with the Transfer Advisor in the Office of Student Success and other campus partners to support a seamless transition from admission through enrollment, promote student success, and enhance the overall transfer student experience.

Work will be performed in a manner that contributes to the university’s enrollment objectives while supporting Indiana Tech’s mission, vision, and values. The Transfer Admissions Counselor serves as an active member of the Indiana Tech Transfer Task Force and collaborates across campus to improve transfer processes, strengthen partnerships, and advance initiatives that support transfer student recruitment, enrollment, and success.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

Transfer Recruitment and Enrollment

  • Recruit prospective transfer students through in-person appointments, phone calls, text messaging, email communications, virtual meetings, and admissions events.
  • Manage transfer recruitment and develop strategies to increase transfer student enrollment.
  • Build and maintain relationships with community colleges, academic advisors, faculty, and transfer coordinators.
  • Represent Indiana Tech at transfer fairs, community college visits, campus events, and other recruitment activities.
  • Assist transfer students through the admissions, financial aid, and enrollment processes.
  • Conduct individual counseling sessions with students regarding transfer opportunities, degree programs, costs, and scholarship options.
  • Develop and execute transfer-specific communication and recruitment plans designed to generate applications, deposits, and enrollments.

Transfer Credit Evaluation and Admissions Review

  • Request, monitor, and coordinate transfer credit evaluations with the Transfer Advisor and other campus partners.
  • Review completed transfer evaluations with students and explain degree applicability, remaining requirements, and graduation pathways.
  • Conduct preliminary reviews of transcripts and admissions documents to determine admissions eligibility and application readiness.
  • Make admissions recommendations and decisions in accordance with institutional policies and established admission standards.
  • Advocate for students to maximize transferability of previously earned coursework.
  • Complete transcript reviews, transfer credit evaluations, admissions evaluations, application processing, and other enrollment-related duties as needed during peak application and enrollment periods.

Student Success Collaboration

  • Collaborate closely with the Transfer Advisor in the Office of Student Success to support a seamless transition for transfer students from admission through enrollment and persistence.
  • Coordinate regularly regarding transfer student needs, academic planning, registration readiness, and student support services.
  • Partner with the Transfer Advisor to identify and address barriers to enrollment, retention, and student success.
  • Participate in joint outreach efforts and initiatives designed to improve the transfer student experience and increase student persistence.
  • Share relevant student information and enrollment updates in accordance with institutional policies to ensure continuity of support throughout the student lifecycle.

Indiana Tech Transfer Task Force

  • Serve as an active member of the Indiana Tech Transfer Task Force.
  • Collaborate with campus partners to identify opportunities to improve transfer student recruitment, enrollment, retention, and graduation outcomes.
  • Assist in the development and implementation of transfer initiatives, articulation agreements, policies, and procedures.
  • Provide feedback and recommendations based on transfer student trends, challenges, and enrollment data.
  • Support institutional efforts to create and enhance transfer pathways that improve student access and success.

Team Collaboration and Operational Support

  • Participate in admissions events including visit programs, open houses, accepted student events, orientation activities, and transfer-specific programs.
  • Assist with recruitment travel, presentations, and outreach initiatives as assigned.
  • Support departmental recruitment initiatives and collaborate with admissions staff to ensure enrollment goals are achieved.
  • Contribute to a positive team environment and assist with special projects and additional responsibilities as assigned.
  • Adhere to all university, state, and federal regulations related to student recruitment and admissions practices.

Measures of Accomplishment

  • Achievement of individual and departmental transfer enrollment goals.
  • Growth in transfer applications, admits, deposits, and enrolled students.
  • Timely completion of transfer credit evaluations and admissions decisions.
  • Development and maintenance of community college partnerships and transfer pathways.
  • Effective participation and contribution to the Indiana Tech Transfer Task Force.
  • Accurate and timely documentation of student interactions within Slate CRM.
  • Positive service and responsiveness to students, families, and campus partners.

Qualifications

Required

  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university.
  • Strong interpersonal, organizational, and communication skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
  • Ability to travel and maintain insurability under university requirements.

Preferred

  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and Slate CRM, preferred.
  • Previous experience in admissions, higher education, recruitment, sales, customer service, or transfer student services, preferred.
  • Familiarity with transfer credit evaluation processes, articulation agreements, and student success initiatives, preferred.

Experience

Two years or more work experience within admissions is preferred, and bachelor’s degree required.

Application materials must include a cover letter and resume. Applicants must be prepared to provide a written response to Tech's mission and vision. The position remains open until filled; a review of candidates will commence as application materials are received.

title: Senior Problem and Major Incident Officer
description:
The Queensland Fire Department (QFD) provides fire prevention, preparedness and response services to fire in the built and landscape environments, as well as scientific and specialist capabilities to Queensland communities. The QFD provides a multi-hazard emergency response, including road crash rescue, bushfire, hazardous material, technical and vertical rescue, severe weather incidents, remote and swiftwater rescue, and provides a number of functions supporting community safety outcomes.

The department encompasses Queensland Fire and Rescue (QFR), Rural Fire Service Queensland (RFSQ), as well as the broader department which work together to pre-empt, prevent, mitigate and manage the consequences of fires and other emergencies on Queensland communities and support our large volunteer membership across the state.

The QFD is an organisation that is committed to reframing the department’s relationship with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, communities, and organisations through activities identified in the QFD Reframing the Relationship Plan, contributing to Closing the Gap outcomes and building our cultural capability.

A part of delivering the Service Management and Operations vision is to lead and drive the day-to-day delivery of Information Communication and Technology (ICT) service desk and regional support services and programs. The Service Management team is responsible for managing effective change and release process for new capability and providing coordination and management of major incidents and problems, including managing the service catalogue, improving customer experience, creating engaged customers and facilitating a trusted relationship with customers in operational and corporate support areas to achieve optimal outcomes for the departments strategic operational and business requirements.


Reporting to the ICT Service Transition Manager, you will play a critical role in managing Major Incidents and Problems across all controlled environments within the department. You will provide expert advice on Major Incident and Problem resolution processes in line with ITIL4 principles. You will be responsible for developing, implementing, and maintaining robust processes within QFD.

Highly desirable requirements

  • 5+ years’ experience demonstrating practical knowledge in Major Incident, Problem Resolution and Change Management processes.

  • Experience and qualifications in the ITIL 4 Service Management framework, including certification in ITIL 4 Practitioner would be considered highly desirable.

  • Sound understanding and familiarity with the ability to understand current technologies from a support perspective.

Special requirements

  • The incumbent will be appointed as a staff member of QFD. The role will be required to undertake non-continuous shift work in accordance with the Queensland Public Service Officers and Other Employees Award - State 2015. Roster patterns will include day and afternoon shifts including weekends. The incumbent may also be required to participate in an on-call roster outside of the rostered shift work arrangement.

  • This role may require work to be performed out-of-business hours and in response to crisis management in support of operational employees who play a vital role in providing the 24/7, 365 days a year emergency response and public safety capability the organisation delivers to the Queensland community.

Your part in the ongoing success of our department, in supporting key frontline services will see you responsible for a variety of work, including, but not limited to:

  • Assist in the maturation of Incident and Problem Management procedures based on Information Technology Infrastructure Library (ITIL) standards and ensure compliance and effective management of the Major Incident and Problem Management processes.

  • Lead Major Incidents to ensure timely identification, logging, categorisation, prioritisation and resolutions of incidents is achieved.

  • Proactively prevent the recurrence of Major Incidents through maintaining close working relationships with Change Management and operational support teams by running post incident analysis.

  • Coordinate the management of Major Incidents to ensure rapid resolution of normal service operation to minimise the adverse impact on business operations across the customer environments.

  • Ensure Major Incidents are effectively documented, communicated and managed and recommend effective deployment of resources to achieve agreed outcomes.

  • Provide advice to management and stakeholders regarding the impact and treatment of Problems and Incidents.

  • Perform proactive Incident and Problem Management activities to recognise trends among incident records and identify and raise problems

To determine your suitability for the role, you will be assessed on the following Leadership Competencies for Queensland behavioural profiles that link to what we are looking for in this role:

Leadership Competency Stream – Individual Contributor (leading self)

Vision

  • Stimulates ideas and innovation
  • Makes insightful decisions

Results

  • Builds enduring relationships
  • Drives accountability and outcomes

Accountability

  • Fosters healthy and inclusive workplaces
  • Pursues continuous growth

Once you join us we will want you to exemplify the QFD shared values of:

  • Respect
  • Integrity
  • Trust
  • Courage
  • Loyalty

title: Strategy & Operations, Office of the CCO
location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

The Office of the Chief Commercial Officer is a small team that works directly with our CCO, go-to-market leadership, and company leadership on Anthropic’s highest-priority commercial initiatives. We take on problems that do not sit cleanly inside one team, such as standing up a program that spans Product, Finance, Legal, and Sales, or preparing the material our executives and Board use to make decisions. Our commercial business is growing faster than its operating processes can be built, so a growing share of the job is stepping into gaps and running something important, while making sure other teams are building the capabilities to permanently own.

You will own workstreams end to end. One week that means running the go-to-market side of a pressing situation, from the communications plan for customers and account teams to the daily readout for executives. Another week it means building the analysis behind a resourcing decision or a new program and writing it up for the CCO. This is an internal role. You will report to the CCO’s chief of staff, and you will have an unusually broad view of how the company makes decisions.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Drive priority go-to-market initiatives from plan to delivery, removing blockers, escalating early, and connecting the right people across teams at the right time

  • Build the analysis, draft the document or deck, and turn input from many teams into a recommendation executives can act on

  • Prepare content for the CCO and leadership team, including weekly staff meetings, updates to the Office of the CEO, Board materials, and leadership offsites

  • Track the go-to-market organization’s top priorities and keep a current view of status, owners, and risks

  • Act as a bridge between go-to-market and Product, Finance, Legal, Safeguards, and Research, so that what account teams hear from customers reaches product decisions and those decisions reach account teams in a usable form

  • Step in where something important has no clear owner, run it until it has a permanent home, and hand it over cleanly

  • Close out same-day executive requests quickly and to a high standard

You may be a good fit if you:

  • Have 4+ years of experience in management consulting, strategy and operations, a chief of staff team, or a similarly rigorous environment working with senior executives

  • Structure ambiguous problems well and get to a clear recommendation

  • Can get to a number yourself in a spreadsheet, in SQL, or with Claude, check it against a second source, and explain where it came from

  • Write and speak clearly and briefly for executive audiences

  • Are as willing to maintain the tracker and chase the last open items as to write the strategy

  • Are comfortable with significant autonomy and with priorities that shift on short notice, pay close attention to detail, and know when to escalate

  • Build trust quickly with senior people across the company who are short on time

  • Use AI tools as a core part of how you work

  • Care about Anthropic’s mission and about getting safe, useful AI to customers

Strong candidates may also have

  • Experience in technology, SaaS, or enterprise software, or exposure to go-to-market strategy, sales operations, or customer success

  • Experience running a product launch, a program office, or another cross-functional effort with many owners and a fixed date

  • Familiarity with how large enterprises buy and adopt technology, including security, legal, and procurement review

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$190,000—$270,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

description:
See your work in a new light.

At LUX Infusion, we’re reimagining infusion care to be more human, supportive, and connected. Inspired by lux—meaning light - we guide patients, providers, and partners through complex therapies with clarity, compassion, and confidence.

As a clinician-led, U.S.-based organization, we put people first - helping patients feel seen and supported through faster therapy starts, dedicated care coordination, and meaningful collaboration. Our commitment to inclusion, diversity, equity, and advancement (IDEA) is central to our culture, ensuring every team member feels valued and empowered to make a difference.

Schedule: Monday–Friday, 8:00 AM–5:00 PM EST
Location: On‑site — Syracuse, NY

See Your Work in a New Light

At LUX Infusion, we believe infusion care deserves more light — more warmth, more clarity, and more connection. That commitment extends beyond clinical care to the financial processes that ensure patients can begin and continue therapy without unnecessary barriers.

We’re looking for a Billing Specialist who wants their work to mean something — someone who brings accuracy, accountability, and purpose to the reimbursement process that supports patient access to care.

Why This Role Matters

Billing accuracy and timeliness are essential to keeping patients on therapy and ensuring care teams can focus on what matters most — the patient. The Billing Specialist plays a critical role in verifying reimbursement data, submitting clean claims, and resolving payments appropriately.

In this role, you’ll contribute to work that:

  • Helps patients maintain uninterrupted access to infusion therapy
  • Supports clinicians and operations teams through reliable revenue‑cycle execution
  • Ensures compliance with payer contracts and reimbursement standards
  • Strengthens a patient‑first, clinician‑led organization focused on outcomes

Behind every successful infusion is a billing process that works — and this role helps make that happen.

What You’ll Do

In this role, you will:

  • Prepare and submit insurance claims for home infusion services, including medications, nursing, and supplies
  • Process electronic pharmacy claims to Medicare Part D, Medicaid, and commercial insurance plans
  • Verify that all prescription reimbursement data is complete, accurate, and entered timely prior to weekly and month‑end close
  • Confirm documentation aligns with billed services, codes, and expected reimbursement
  • Review payments received and apply them accurately to patient accounts through final resolution
  • Maintain a strong understanding of payer contracts, coverage criteria, and reimbursement guidelines
  • Address billing inquiries and resolve discrepancies with professionalism and clarity
  • Stay current on billing regulations, coding guidelines, and payer requirements
  • Work with clearinghouses and billing systems to support clean claims and efficient workflows
  • Assist with data entry, administrative, and clerical billing tasks as needed

What We’re Looking For

You may be a great fit if you bring:

  • Strong attention to detail and analytical thinking
  • A customer‑service mindset paired with financial accuracy
  • Comfort working in a fast‑paced, deadline‑driven environment
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills
  • Ownership and care in work that directly affects patient access

Required Qualifications

  • High school diploma or GED
  • Minimum of two (2) years of experience in medical billing and collections
  • Experience providing customer service to internal and external stakeholders
  • Basic proficiency with Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint)

Preferred Qualifications

  • Five (5) or more years of medical billing and collections experience
  • Prior home infusion therapy billing experience
  • Experience with CareTend, CPR+, or similar billing systems

You don’t need to check every box — we care just as much about how you approach your work as what’s on your resume.

Why LUX Infusion

At LUX Infusion, we believe care deserves more light — more warmth, more clarity, and more connection.

Here, you’ll find:

  • Purpose‑driven work that directly supports patient access to care
  • A patient‑first, clinician‑led culture
  • Collaborative revenue cycle, pharmacy, and operations teams
  • Flexibility through on‑site or remote work options

Come help ensure accuracy supports access — and see what’s possible when care comes first.

$26—$28 USD

title: Semi-Senior Frontend Developer (React / Next.js)
description:
Semi-Senior Frontend Developer (React / Next.js)

Full-time contractor · Fully remote

Cloudnonic is an international, fully remote cloud and software company. We build customized cloud-native systems for clients in Europe and North America, and we're looking for a Semi-Senior React developer to join the team.

Who we are

Cloudnonic Corp. is a digitally native software and cloud startup based in the Kitchener/Waterloo area, Ontario, Canada. We're fully remote, with developers in Canada and South America and clients across Europe, North America, and South America. We work across healthcare, finance, construction, and manufacturing, and we take the time to understand each client's industry so we can serve it well with technology.

We're big on AI and the cloud. Our services range from app and web development to AI and cloud integration, plus technology consulting: designing feasible, secure, cost-effective architectures for non-technical clients and advising them on their tech stack.

The role

As a React developer you'll work on multiple client projects at once, each with its own tech stack, code, and idiosyncrasies. You'll work with a wide range of code, libraries, and technologies and build the kind of adaptability that comes from switching between projects rather than staying in one repository.

We deliver AI-first. AI generates our tickets and acceptance criteria, we pair with AI while developing, and every pull request goes through AI review before a senior engineer reviews it. That makes us fast. It also means we have no room for developers who can only prompt. You need to be able to read what the AI produced, know when it's wrong, and fix it yourself: solid fundamentals in JavaScript, React's rendering model, semantic HTML, browser performance, and HTTP are the baseline, not a bonus. If you can't explain your code without the tool that wrote it, this isn't the role for you. Part of our technical interview is done without AI assistance.

You'll work directly with clients to architect solutions, discuss new features, and present your progress, most of the time in English. You'll learn to present ideas to clients in a professional, friendly way. Expect to be challenged constantly, and to enjoy the work along the way.

What will help you succeed

  • Self-starter who doesn't need micromanagement
  • Flexible and goal-oriented
  • Enjoys being challenged and learning something new every day
  • Strong passion for coding; promotes clean, maintainable code
  • Team player, yet autonomous, with a positive spirit
  • Picks up new technologies constantly and with ease
  • Understands the trade-offs of working as a contractor vs. an employee

We trust you to organize your day, prioritize your week, and keep the team and clients updated as you go.

Requirements

Language

  • Fluent Spanish
  • Advanced English (able to hold a client conversation without difficulty)

Technical

  • 1–2 years of full-time coding experience in React and Next.js
  • Strong programming fundamentals: you can design, debug, and explain your code without AI assistance
  • Experience with React Native
  • Experience with JSON and RESTful services
  • Experience with Agile methodologies

Bonus

  • Unit and integration testing
  • Fluent English (B2+)
  • Concise, efficient written and oral communication

What we offer

  • Fully remote: work from home or anywhere you choose
  • Competitive pay: rates that compete with the best in the Latin American market, tailored to your seniority and skills, paid in the currency you prefer
  • Crypto payment available on request
  • Full-time contractor: you manage your own finances
  • Flexible hours: we work across time zones and trust you to get your work done on your schedule
  • Company culture: no rigid hierarchy; hard work and enjoying the journey are not in conflict
  • Gaming: online games with colleagues over Discord is a regular thing here
  • Broad technical exposure: many technologies and challenges in a short time; you won't get bored in the same repositories
  • International clients: US, Canada, Germany, and beyond, with the languages and cultures that come with them
  • Professional development: sponsored online courses and certifications on demand
  • Career development: build expertise across industries, not only in code

Interested?

If this sounds like you and you meet the minimum requirements, apply.

title: Commercial Counsel
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Commercial Counsel based in Switzerland.

As Commercial Counsel, you’ll be the first dedicated legal hire supporting a rapidly growing AI business with complex commercial and regulatory needs.
You’ll take ownership of customer, supplier, and partner agreements, handling drafting and negotiations under US law from initial review through signature or resolution.
A key part of the role will be addressing emerging AI-contracting questions around data use, training, output ownership, liability, and warranties.
You’ll also provide practical guidance on data protection, enterprise deals, diligence, and legal readiness across a cross-border organization.
Working closely with Finance, founders, customers, and external advisers, you’ll build reusable templates, negotiation positions, and workflows that make legal work more efficient.
You’ll have significant autonomy in a small, high-trust environment where decisions are made by owners and legal judgment directly influences commercial outcomes.
This is an opportunity to build a legal function from the ground up while staying deeply involved in the business and the deals it signs.

Accountabilities

  • Review, draft, and negotiate customer, supplier, and partner agreements under US law, including SaaS terms, order forms, NDAs, and DPAs.
  • Provide clear, commercially practical legal recommendations and remain involved with matters through signature, resolution, or final escalation.
  • Own AI-specific contracting issues, including data use and training, ownership of outputs, liability allocation, warranties, and related commercial risks.
  • Lead legal readiness for enterprise transactions and due diligence processes.
  • Develop and maintain practical contract templates, negotiation positions, and an organized contract archive covering recurring commercial, AI, and data issues.
  • Own practical data-protection work by translating regulatory and specialist advice into clear actions, owners, deadlines, and follow-up.
  • Manage relationships with external counsel, including preparing briefs, coordinating advice, monitoring budgets, and engaging jurisdiction-specific or specialist advisers when required.
  • Support fundraising and corporate transactions, including maintaining records, approvals, filing deadlines, and authorities across US, Polish, and German entities.
  • Coordinate legal matters across jurisdictions while recognizing the limits of US-law expertise and involving appropriate local or specialist counsel when necessary.
  • Improve legal intake, drafting, obligation tracking, and administrative workflows through approved AI tools combined with appropriate human review.
  • Track legal obligations after contracts are signed and ensure relevant teams understand material commitments and follow-up actions.
  • Build and maintain a prioritized legal-readiness roadmap covering enterprise reviews, data protection, and relevant AI regulatory requirements.
  • Establish practical workflows for external-counsel briefs, budgets, advice, and outstanding corporate-support matters.

    • Requirements

    • Admission to practice in a US state with substantial hands-on experience drafting and negotiating commercial agreements governed by US law.
    • Demonstrable experience personally handling agreements such as SaaS contracts, order forms, NDAs, DPAs, and other B2B commercial agreements.
    • Strong commercial judgment and the ability to distinguish material business risks from non-critical drafting preferences.
    • Ability to propose practical, workable alternatives that support commercial objectives while appropriately managing legal risk.
    • Proven ability to own matters end to end, including negotiation, resolution, obligation tracking, administrative follow-through, and escalation.
    • Strong understanding of when US-law expertise is sufficient and when local or specialist counsel should be involved, particularly across European jurisdictions.
    • Experience working with cross-border businesses and multiple legal entities is highly valuable.
    • Excellent written and spoken English, with the ability to communicate clearly with customers, founders, finance teams, and external advisers.
    • Highly organized, discreet, proactive, and comfortable working independently with limited process or supervision.
    • Ability to identify legal issues early and communicate them together with a proposed course of action.
    • Familiarity with GDPR and practical data-protection matters is advantageous.
    • Experience with B2B software, AI products, or AI/data contracting is a strong plus.
    • Experience working with venture-backed companies, fundraising, or financing rounds is beneficial.
    • Familiarity with enterprise procurement processes and security reviews is advantageous.
    • Experience with multi-entity or cross-border corporate management is a plus.
    • Comfortable using approved AI tools to improve legal intake, drafting, tracking, and other workflows while maintaining appropriate human oversight.
    • Willingness to work in a hands-on legal role rather than focusing primarily on corporate governance or delegating drafting and negotiations.

      • Benefits

      • Top-of-the-market salary.
      • Meaningful ownership and responsibility within an early-stage, growing environment.
      • Remote work available within Europe.
      • Warsaw preferred, with remote flexibility across Europe.
      • Opportunity to build the first dedicated legal function and establish its processes, templates, and workflows.
      • Direct involvement in commercial deals, enterprise transactions, AI contracting, and strategic legal matters.
      • High level of autonomy in a small, high-trust team with minimal bureaucracy.
      • Opportunity to shape how the legal function evolves as enterprise and cross-border requirements grow.

      • Exposure to emerging legal questions around AI, data, SaaS, and cross-border technology operations.

title: Tier 3 System Administrator Lead
description:
Ardent is seeking a Tier 3 System Administrator Lead to join our team.

This is an on-site position in Washington, D.C.

Position Description:

Ardent is seeking a Tier 3 System Administrator Lead to support the United States Holocaust Memorial Museum (USHMM) and the technology foundation behind its historically important mission.. Reliable systems, storage, backup, and cloud services are essential to the Museum’s work preserving Holocaust history, supporting education, and serving the public. The Tier 3 System Administrator Lead will be responsible for the end-to-end operational integrity, availability, maintenance, and recovery of the Museum’s server ecosystem. The position supports onsite operations to enable 24x7x365 enterprise escalation requirements.

Responsibilities and Duties:

  • Lead administration, monitoring, maintenance, troubleshooting, and recovery for physical, virtual, and cloud-based Windows and Linux servers.
  • Perform operating system patching, storage-capacity monitoring, hardware maintenance, critical-service restart and validation, backup verification, SSL certificate renewal, firmware and BIOS updates, and directed vulnerability remediation.
  • Administer and troubleshoot VMware ESXi and vCenter environments, AWS EC2 and related cloud services, Microsoft SQL, MySQL, Oracle, certificate services, and Active Directory infrastructure within the assigned operational scope.
  • Use advanced Linux and Windows administration skills, including shell scripting, to automate repeatable support activities and accelerate diagnosis and recovery.
  • Support AWS operations including Linux EC2 lifecycle management, S3 administration, Route 53 records, VPC routing, Lambda monitoring, CloudWatch monitoring, and approved IAM execution.
  • Deploy physical, virtual, and cloud servers; complete domain joins, IP and DNS registration, security baselines, backup policy association, documentation, and asset tagging.
  • Operate backup, restore, and recovery services using Museum-supported platforms, including daily job review, restoration requests, annual disaster recovery exercises, bare-metal recovery, and runbook validation.
  • Support storage platforms and services, including PowerScale, OneFS, Cohesity, S3, Glacier, Unity, and associated monitoring, access, capacity, firmware, and recovery activities.
  • Provide data center hardware support, vendor RMA coordination, equipment and cable labeling, environmental and rack-capacity monitoring, and approved physical changes.
  • Serve as technical lead for third-party hosted applications, vendor updates, secure remote access, certificates, domains, OS patching, and application-tier services such as IIS, Apache, or JBoss.
  • Create and maintain accurate implementation, configuration, recovery, change, incident, and operational documentation; coordinate significant changes through Museum change-control processes.
  • Provide Tier 3 escalation and after-hours support for incidents affecting critical infrastructure, including data center and AWS services.

Requirements:

  • Expertise in Linux and Windows server administration and shell scripting.
  • Demonstrated experience maintaining operational integrity across on-premises, virtual, and cloud-based server environments.
  • Advanced troubleshooting experience with server hardware, operating systems, virtualization, storage, backup, databases, identity services, and network dependencies.
  • Experience with VMware, Microsoft Windows Server, Linux, AWS, Active Directory, DNS, SSL certificates, and enterprise patching and monitoring practices.
  • Experience executing backup, restoration, disaster recovery, bare-metal recovery, and hardware failure remediation activities.

title: Vulnerability Engineer
company: Health New Zealand - Te Whatu Ora
description:
• Work from anywhere in New Zealand, with remote working available
  • Join our national Cyber Protection and Response team
  • Build smarter vulnerability management through automation, scripting and technology

Health New Zealand | Te Whatu Ora is firmly grounded in the principles of Te Tiriti o Waitangi and is committed to building a health system that serves all New Zealanders. Through integration and collaboration, we're creating a nationally connected health system that delivers equitable, high-quality care for the people of Aotearoa.

These are flexible location roles and can be based at any Health New Zealand office across New Zealand with option to work remotely for the right candidate.

About the role

We have two exciting opportunities for Vulnerability Engineers to join our Vulnerability Management team within Cyber Protection and Response.

This is a hands-on engineering role where you'll help strengthen Health New Zealand's national vulnerability management capability. You'll work across our technology environment to identify vulnerabilities, improve scanning and remediation processes, and build automation that helps our teams respond to security risks more effectively.

We're looking for someone who can take a broad view of the cyber threat landscape, understand how emerging vulnerabilities could impact our environment, and turn that knowledge into practical technical solutions.

You'll have the opportunity to work across a wide range of infrastructure, including cloud, Windows, Linux and networking environments. You'll also partner with our infrastructure and patch management teams to support remediation and help ensure vulnerabilities are addressed effectively.

A big part of the role will be finding ways to work smarter - whether that's through scripting, automation, integrating security tools or improving existing workflows. You'll have the freedom to bring your ideas to the table, explore new approaches and make a real impact.

About the Team

The National Cyber Security team is responsible for protecting Health New Zealand's digital environment while enabling the safe delivery of healthcare services across the country.

The Vulnerability Management team sits within Cyber Protection and Response and plays a key role in identifying, prioritising and reducing cyber security risks across a complex national technology environment.

We're a collaborative and open team that values knowledge sharing, continuous improvement and practical problem-solving. You'll have the opportunity to work with a wide range of technical teams and contribute to meaningful work that strengthens cyber security across Aotearoa.

What you'll bring

We're looking for someone with a strong cybersecurity foundation, practical vulnerability management experience and a genuine interest in automation and solving technical challenges. You'll be confident working across technical environments, developing automation and explaining complex security issues in a clear and straightforward way.

You will also bring:

  • 3-5 years' experience in vulnerability management, security engineering, security tooling, DevSecOps or a related cyber security role
  • Hands-on experience with vulnerability management platforms such as Tenable, Nessus, Qualys or equivalent
  • Strong experience identifying, assessing, prioritising and managing vulnerabilities through to remediation
  • Experience with scripting and automation using Python, PowerShell or similar
  • Experience across cloud, Windows, Linux, networking and infrastructure environments
  • An understanding of cyber threats and how vulnerabilities may affect an organisation's risk
  • Experience integrating security tools, platforms and workflows
  • The ability to investigate issues, identify improvements and work independently
  • Strong communication skills and confidence engaging with technical teams and senior stakeholders
  • A curious and motivated approach, with a willingness to learn and keep up with emerging threats and technologies

Experience with infrastructure as code, CI/CD pipelines, SIEM, EDR, Microsoft Defender, Sentinel or cloud security platforms would be an advantage.

You'll also need to be able to obtain and maintain the appropriate New Zealand Government security clearance.

Working at Health New Zealand

Health New Zealand | Te Whatu Ora is dedicated to ensuring excellent healthcare for the people of Aotearoa through our values of care and respect, collaboration, accountability, innovation, and excellence.

We are committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse workforce where everyone feels valued. We welcome applications from all people, including Māori, Pacific Peoples, disabled people, and the Rainbow community.

How to Apply

If you're ready to take the next step in your cybersecurity career and help strengthen our national vulnerability management capability, apply today.

All applications must be submitted through our online careers portal by Thursday, 22 October.

Please note that if we receive a high number of suitable applications, we may close the role earlier than the advertised closing date.

If you have any questions about the role, please contact Ash Mohan at ash.mohan@tewhatuora.govt.nz.

You’ll work across Kubernetes, AWS, PostgreSQL, CI infrastructure, observability, security, and reliability practices.
You’ll help evolve a growing SRE function, strengthening SLOs, incident response, on-call practices, and operational excellence.
At the same time, you’ll own the career development, performance, hiring, and overall health of your team.
The environment is fully remote and asynchronous, requiring strong written communication, autonomy, and thoughtful prioritization.

  • Help mature the organization's reliability practices by identifying operational gaps and turning lessons from incidents into lasting engineering improvements.
  • Balance short-term operational demands with longer-term platform investments and engineering goals.

    • Requirements:

title: Deputy Director of Industrial Security
description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Security Team at Anduril is the cornerstone of defense, employing unparalleled security measures and state-of-the-art technology to ensure the protection of our people, assets, operations, and innovations. Given the unique nature of this company, our team supports a host of standard and non-standard taskings integrating physical and digital measures to stay ahead of evolving threats. We also uphold stringent industry and government compliance, creating a secure environment that nurtures the development of cutting-edge defense solutions and ensures Anduril's continued growth and innovation in a complex global landscape.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are seeking an experienced, proactive, and dynamic leader to serve as the Deputy Director of Industrial Security. In this critical leadership role, you will assist with overseeing the strategic direction and operational execution of our enterprise-wide industrial security program. You will lead a large, geographically dispersed security team across the United States, including Regional Facility Security Officers (RFSOs), site-level Facility Security Officers (FSOs), and a centralized Personnel Security (PERSEC) team. The ideal candidate brings extensive hands-on experience as an FSO, deep subject matter expertise in 32 CFR Part 117 (NISPOM) Must be able to work within a collaborative team environment and take independent action, analyze problems, and provide security focused solutions to Anduril and government personnel.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Serve as the senior technical authority on 32 CFR Part 117 (NISPOM Rule), ensuring absolute enterprise-wide compliance across all cleared facilities.
  • Leverage expertise with US government security policies, procedures and industry experience as it relates to Industrial security.
  • Build a culture of compliance, operational excellence, customer service, and continuous improvement across all security functions.
  • Establish team KPIs, conduct performance reviews, allocate resources effectively, and develop professional growth pathways for security personnel.
  • In coordination with the security education manager, develop and deliver applicable security education topics to program personnel.
  • Oversee and standardize Standard Practice Procedures (SPPs) for all cleared locations.
  • Lead preparation efforts for Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) security reviews, vulnerability assessments, and internal self-inspections.
  • Serve as an escalated point of contact for complex security violations, and adverse information reporting. Oversee and coordinate all activities related to FOCI.


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelors Degree and ten years of industrial security-related experience.
  • Exceptional time management and prioritization skills, with the ability to achieve goals and targets while handling multiple tasks.
  • Minimum of 5+ years directly managing large, cross-functional, and geographically dispersed teams (including managing managers/regional leaders).
  • FSO Background: Direct experience having served as an appointed Facility Security Officer (FSO) for a possessing/cleared facility.
  • Ability to communicate and interact professionally and courteously both orally and in writing with all levels of employees, management and customers.
  • Experience integrating security operations following corporate Mergers & Acquisitions (M&A).
  • Active Top Secret
US Salary Range
$166,000—$220,000 USD

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

Benefits

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

  • No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

  • Please always verify communications:
    • Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.
    • Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

  • Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

  • What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

Data Privacy

To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit .

This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. title: Applied ML Engineer
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an Applied ML Engineer based in France.

As an Applied ML Engineer, you’ll work at the intersection of machine learning research, experimentation, and production engineering.
You’ll turn ideas from research papers into rigorous experiments, measurable evidence, and reliable products.
The role spans model evaluation, model internals, inference infrastructure, backend systems, and user-facing product experiences.
You’ll work hands-on with modern ML models, designing evaluations that reveal what methods can—and cannot—demonstrate.
You’ll also build production-grade tooling that makes complex experiments repeatable, observable, and accessible to users.
The environment values technical judgment, ownership, scientific rigor, and the ability to move comfortably across the technology stack.
It’s an opportunity to help transform emerging ML techniques into practical systems that people can trust.

Accountabilities

  • Reproduce and evaluate machine learning research methods using open-weight and API-accessible models.
  • Design evaluation datasets, probes, scoring approaches, baselines, calibration tests, and experiment harnesses.
  • Work directly with model weights, logits, hidden states, activations, model APIs, and inference infrastructure when required.
  • Build and extend evaluation infrastructure covering experiment runners, judges, persistence, orchestration, reporting, and reproducibility.
  • Turn research workflows into intuitive product experiences, including experiment configuration, execution, traces, comparisons, reports, and review workflows.
  • Investigate how verification methods behave when models are modified through fine-tuning, merging, quantization, distillation, safety removal, or deliberate evasion.
  • Design controlled experiments that distinguish meaningful signals from artifacts, confounders, and misleading correlations.
  • Produce clear technical reports that separate measured evidence from interpretation and hypotheses.
  • Deliver production-quality systems with APIs, asynchronous jobs, databases, observability, testing, deployment, and documentation.
  • Contribute across research, experimentation, engineering, and product as priorities evolve.
  • During the first six months, reproduce and document at least one published model-provenance or verification method, including its capabilities, assumptions, and limitations.
  • Build a repeatable model-verification runner with versioned inputs, artifacts, metrics, and reports, and make at least one verification workflow accessible through the product interface.
  • Run controlled experiments across base, fine-tuned, merged, quantized, and known distilled models, improving understanding of when verification methods succeed, fail, and why.

    • Requirements:

    • Strong Python engineering skills, with hands-on experience using PyTorch and Hugging Face Transformers.
    • Solid understanding of machine learning evaluation, including dataset design, baselines, metrics, calibration, false positives and negatives, statistical uncertainty, and reproducibility.
    • Ability to read ML research papers critically and implement methods from first principles rather than relying entirely on existing packages.
    • Professional software engineering experience beyond notebooks, including APIs, asynchronous jobs, databases, logging, testing, deployment, and documentation.
    • Familiarity with open-weight models and a practical understanding of how modern LLM inference systems operate.
    • Ability to work across backend and frontend boundaries, with sufficient React/TypeScript knowledge to help make complex experiments and results understandable to users.
    • Strong experimental and analytical judgment, particularly around distinguishing what evidence demonstrates from what it merely suggests.
    • High ownership and initiative, with the ability to identify problems, propose solutions, and drive projects forward independently.
    • Comfort working in a fast-moving startup environment where priorities can change quickly and engineers may operate across multiple functions.
    • Experience with model provenance, fingerprinting, watermarking, distillation detection, red-teaming, safety evaluation, interpretability, or related areas is a plus.
    • Experience with activation and representation analysis, probing, model hooks, logits, hidden states, or other model-internals techniques is advantageous.
    • Familiarity with evaluation and inference infrastructure such as DSPy, LiteLLM, Temporal, Ray, vLLM, PostgreSQL/pgvector, or comparable technologies is beneficial.
    • Experience with Next.js, React, TypeScript, data visualization, or experiment dashboards is a plus.
    • Experience running and serving open-weight models on GPUs, including reasoning about latency, throughput, memory, precision, and cost trade-offs, is valuable.
    • Experience designing adversarial evaluations or testing systems against deliberate attempts to evade detection is an advantage.
    • A strong commitment to producing production-quality code, tests, tooling, and documentation that other engineers can confidently operate and extend.

      • Benefits:

      • Opportunity to work on applied machine learning at the intersection of research, experimentation, engineering, and product.
      • End-to-end ownership across model evaluation, model internals, infrastructure, backend systems, and user-facing experiences.
      • Exposure to modern open-weight models, LLM inference systems, and emerging ML verification techniques.
      • A role with significant technical autonomy and the opportunity to shape both experiments and production systems.
      • Fast-moving startup environment with evolving priorities and cross-functional collaboration.
      • Opportunity to translate cutting-edge research into practical, measurable, and user-accessible products.
      • The opportunity to build systems and evaluation methodologies designed to produce evidence that users can understand and trust.

title: Underbar tjej i Lomma söker personlig assistent ca 35-40%
description:
Vi på KSJ AB jobbar med personlig assistans – som det är tänkt! 
Här möter du Karin, Magnus, Sylvia och Bibban med lång erfarenhet, stort engagemang och ett hjärta för människor. Vi vet att bra assistans bygger på trygghet, respekt och ett nära samarbete. Med lång och gedigen erfarenhet inom personlig assistans, både från stora och mellanstora bolag, vet vi vad som krävs för att skapa trygghet, kontinuitet och livskvalitet för våra kunder - men också för våra viktiga assistenter.

Om arbetet innebär insatser åt barn krävs att du lämnar in ett utdrag ur belastnings- och misstankeregistret, som sparas hos oss i 2 år, i enlighet med gällande lagstiftningar.

Är du student eller söker extra jobb? 35-40% till denna underbara tjej.

Vecka 2: Må, ti, fre 16.00-22.00

Vecka 3: Mån, tis, to, fre 16.00-22.00

Mån, tis, to, fre 16.00-22.00

Utöver detta tillkommer tre pass på helgen under dessa fyra veckor, då jobbar man lördag kl. 09.00–22.00 eller söndag kl. 08.00–19.00

Vi söker framför allt en ansvarstagande och engagerad person som tycker om barn och efter introduktion kan arbeta självständigt med Selma.

Bor du inte i Lomma är det viktigt att du har körkort och tillgång till bil.

title: Human-Centered Design Specialist IV - UI/UX
description:
Overview

LMI is seeking a Human-Centered Design (HCD) Specialist III-IV - UI/UX to support the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) portfolio. This role will focus on creating intuitive, accessible, visually cohesive, and user-centered digital experiences based on stakeholder research and user needs.

The successful candidate will bring a strong background in user experience and user interface design, with demonstrated ability to translate research findings, workflows, and requirements into high-quality digital experiences. This individual will create user flows, wireframes, prototypes, interaction patterns, interface designs, and reusable design components that guide development teams from concept through implementation.

The role will work across the HCD lifecycle, including discovery, stakeholder engagement, design, prototyping, usability testing, and iteration. Compared with a technically oriented HCD role, this position will place greater emphasis on interaction design, visual hierarchy, interface behavior, usability, design systems, and the quality and consistency of the overall user experience.

LMI is a new breed of digital solutions provider dedicated to accelerating government impact with innovation and speed. Investing in technology and prototypes ahead of need, LMI brings commercial-grade platforms and mission-ready AI to federal agencies at commercial speed.

Leveraging our mission-ready technology and solutions, proven expertise in federal deployment, and strategic relationships, we enhance outcomes for the government, efficiently and effectively. With a focus on agility and collaboration, LMI serves the defense, space, healthcare, and energy sectors—helping agencies navigate complexity and outpace change. Headquartered in Tysons, Virginia, LMI is committed to delivering impactful results that strengthen missions and drive lasting value.

Responsibilities

UI/UX and Product Design

  • Design intuitive, effective, and visually cohesive user experiences for digital products supporting VA programs and stakeholders.
  • Translate research findings, business requirements, user needs, and technical requirements into clear design concepts.
  • Develop user flows, task flows, information architectures, navigation models, wireframes, interface designs, and interactive prototypes.
  • Create low- through high-fidelity designs that enable stakeholders to experience and evaluate concepts before development.
  • Design interface components, interaction patterns, layouts, forms, dashboards, workflows, and data-rich experiences.
  • Establish and apply consistent visual and interaction patterns across digital products.
  • Contribute to design systems, component libraries, UX standards, and reusable design assets where appropriate.
  • Prepare clear developer handoff documentation and collaborate with technical teams during implementation.
  • Participate in design reviews and provide design guidance as solutions move from prototype through development.

HCD Research and Discovery

  • Conduct stakeholder interviews, user interviews, workshops, usability studies, and other HCD discovery activities.
  • Help stakeholders articulate user goals, needs, frustrations, behaviors, workflows, and desired outcomes.
  • Synthesize qualitative research into findings, themes, personas, user journeys, experience maps, design principles, and recommendations.
  • Connect research findings directly to UI/UX design decisions.
  • Develop and test design hypotheses through prototypes and iterative user feedback.
  • Facilitate usability testing and translate test results into prioritized design improvements.

Accessibility and Inclusive Design

  • Apply Section 508, WCAG, and inclusive-design requirements to digital experiences.
  • Design for users with different abilities, levels of digital proficiency, roles, and operating environments.
  • Incorporate accessibility considerations into navigation, forms, visual hierarchy, content presentation, interaction patterns, and prototypes.
  • Collaborate with technical teams to address accessibility early rather than treating compliance as a final-stage review.

Magnify Reports and HCD Deliverables

  • Support development of Magnify Reports, the formal HCD deliverable associated with each SBIR contract.
  • Provide research findings, personas, journey maps, visualizations, prototype concepts, user feedback, and design recommendations for inclusion in formal HCD documentation.
  • Develop polished visual artifacts and presentations to communicate findings and proposed experiences to client and internal stakeholders.
  • Clearly document design rationale and trace significant design decisions back to user research or validated requirements.

Stakeholder and Team Collaboration

  • Facilitate design sessions, co-design workshops, prototype reviews, and usability-testing sessions.
  • Present design concepts and explain design decisions to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Collaborate closely with HCD researchers, technical designers, developers, analysts, product owners, healthcare subject matter experts, and program leadership.
  • Balance user needs, business requirements, accessibility considerations, and technical constraints when developing solutions.
  • Participate in Agile ceremonies and integrate UX activities into iterative delivery cycles.
  • Participate actively in LMI's HCD community of practice by sharing tools, templates, patterns, techniques, and lessons learned.

Qualifications

Required

  • Bachelor's degree in Human-Centered Design, User Experience Design, Interaction Design, Graphic Design, Human-Computer Interaction, Information Design, Psychology, or a related field.
  • 5-7+ years of professional experience in UI/UX, product design, HCD, interaction design, or a related discipline.
  • Demonstrated experience designing digital products from early concept through prototype and development handoff.
  • Strong proficiency with Figma or comparable modern UI/UX design and prototyping tools.
  • Demonstrated experience developing user flows, wireframes, interactive prototypes, and polished interface designs.
  • Strong understanding of information architecture, interaction design, visual hierarchy, usability, and user-centered design principles.
  • Experience conducting or participating in user research and usability testing.
  • Ability to translate research findings and complex requirements into intuitive user experiences.
  • Knowledge of Section 508, WCAG, accessibility, and inclusive-design practices.
  • Strong written, verbal, presentation, and facilitation skills.
  • Ability to independently organize and prioritize design work across multiple activities.
  • Ability to work effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a Public Trust clearance.

Desired

  • Master's degree in Human-Centered Design, Human-Computer Interaction, UX Design, Interaction Design, or a related field.
  • Portfolio demonstrating UI/UX design, research-informed design decisions, user flows, wireframes, prototypes, design systems, or shipped digital experiences.
  • Experience designing for federal government, healthcare, public-sector, or enterprise environments.
  • Prior experience supporting VA or VHA programs.
  • Experience designing dashboards, complex workflows, enterprise applications, or data-rich experiences.
  • Experience creating or contributing to design systems and reusable component libraries.
  • Familiarity with Microsoft Power Platform, SharePoint, Power BI, or Microsoft 365 environments.
  • Experience with Agile, Lean UX, Design Thinking, or iterative product development.
  • Relevant UX, accessibility, HCD, or Agile certifications.

Target salary range: $100,000 - $130,000.

The salary range displayed represents the typical salary range for this position and is not a guarantee of compensation. Individual salaries are determined by various factors including, but not limited to location, internal equity, business considerations, client contract requirements, and candidate qualifications, such as education, experience, skills, and security clearances.

Position Title

Sepsis Coordinator

Job Description

Purpose & Scope:

The Sepsis Coordinator is a registered nurse who leads the hospital's sepsis performance improvement program, serving as the clinical and administrative lead for early recognition, timely treatment, and regulatory compliance related to sepsis care across the continuum. This role drives adherence to CMS SEP-1 core measure bundle requirements, partners with emergency department, intensive care, and medical-surgical unit leadership to close performance gaps and serves as the primary educator and data steward for sepsis-related quality outcomes. The Sepsis Coordinator works collaboratively with physicians, nursing staff, pharmacy, laboratory, and hospital administration to reduce sepsis-related mortality, length of stay, and readmissions.

title: Tier 3 Network Lead
description:
Ardent is seeking a Tier 3 Network Lead to join our team.

This is an on-site position in Washington, D.C.

Position Description:

Ardent is seeking a Tier 3 Network Lead to support the United States Holocaust Memorial Museum (USHMM) and the technology foundation behind its historically important mission. The Museum’s ability to preserve Holocaust history, educate the public, and connect staff and visitors depends on secure, resilient, and high-performing wired and wireless infrastructure. The Tier 3 Network Lead is responsible for the performance, availability, and operational maintenance of the Museum’s wired, wireless, WAN, Internet, cloud-connectivity, and distributed antenna infrastructure. The position supports onsite operations to enable 24x7x365 enterprise escalation requirements.

Responsibilities and Duties:

Lead operations, monitoring, maintenance, troubleshooting, and restoration for LAN, WAN, Internet, Wi-Fi, cloud connectivity, and distributed antenna systems across Museum-supported locations.

  • Install and configure switches and routers; monitor device health, bandwidth, latency, jitter, packet loss, throughput, interfaces, access points, and circuit performance.
  • Diagnose and resolve network outages, routing loops, connectivity issues, authentication failures, RF interference, hardware failures, and performance degradation.
  • Apply approved firmware and software updates to network switches, routers, wireless switches, and access points in coordination with Museum change-control requirements.
  • Use SolarWinds Orion and associated alert dependencies to identify actionable events, reduce alert noise, detect degrading infrastructure, and support proactive and reactive Problem Management.
  • Provide expert-level routing and switching support for the Museum’s Cisco Nexus, Catalyst, ASR, regional switching, and related wired infrastructure.
  • Operate and maintain Aruba Central-managed wireless infrastructure, monitor client and access-point health, maintain wireless diagrams and RF maps, and report security issues to the Museum CISO.
  • Coordinate with Internet service providers, circuit providers, cloud-connectivity providers, and equipment vendors for outages, installations, upgrades, troubleshooting, restoration, and after-action reporting.

title: Technical Writing Assistant, CBP SOD Support
description:
Overview

Join a team where innovation meets mission. Our AI, cloud, cyber, and modernization solutions save agencies thousands of hours, safeguard national security, and strengthen health and humanitarian missions worldwide. With more than 1,700+ team members, 1,500+ AI & data experts, and 100+ prime contracts, we deliver at scale and with purpose.

We’ve been recognized as a Top Workplace by The Washington Post for six consecutive years and named to the Inc. 5000 list of Fastest-Growing Private Companies in 13 of the past 14 years. Credence is a welcoming environment for those looking to grow and make a meaningful impact. We encourage employees to push boundaries and help solve critical, world-changing federal challenges.

Position Summary

Credence has an immediate need for a Technical Writing Assistant to support U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) in the development, maintenance, and lifecycle management of agency policy documentation. This is a 100% remote position supporting a mission-critical federal customer.

The ideal candidate should possess exceptional organizational skills and an eye for detail that catches what others miss. Success in this role requires precision over volume — accurate citations, clean formatting, disciplined version control, and clear tracking of where every document stands in the review and approval cycle. The Technical Writing Assistant serves as the day-to-day steward of a large policy library, fielding research requests from government stakeholders, validating the authorities that underpin existing policy, formatting documents to CBP-approved standards, and shepherding materials through routing and concurrence.

Requirements

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to the duties listed below:

  • Must be able to maintain the CBP policy library, including document intake, indexing, version control, and archiving of superseded material.
  • Will be responsible for providing responsive customer service to the Security Operations Division (SOD) on policy searches and research inquiries.
  • Will conduct independent research and analysis to support the development of new policy.
  • Will validate references and authorities cited in policy documents and determine whether the scope of expiring policy remains relevant, requires revision, or should be sunset.
  • Will create and track routing sheets, monitoring each document action through review, concurrence, and final approval.
  • Will assist with web content management, including posting, updating, and organizing policy content on CBP sites.
  • Must have the ability to utilize Microsoft Word and Adobe Acrobat Pro to format documents into CBP-approved formats, applying styles, templates, cross-references, tables of contents, bookmarking, and accessibility remediation.
  • Must have demonstrated experience utilizing Microsoft PowerPoint to create presentations depicting workflows, processes, and organizational charts.
  • Must have prior experience proofreading and copy editing a wide range of materials, including directives, handbooks, standard operating procedures (SOPs), memoranda, and briefing products.
  • Must maintain working knowledge of a broad range of current guidelines, regulations, policies, and handbooks pertinent to CBP activities.

Qualifications:

  • Must have a Bachelor’s degree in Technical Writing or a related field is required.
  • Must have a minimum of 5 years of relevant technical writing/editing experience.
  • Must have advanced proficiency with Microsoft Word (styles, templates, cross-references, tables of contents, track changes) and Adobe Acrobat Pro (PDF creation, bookmarking, form fields, Section 508 accessibility).
  • Must have proficiency with Microsoft PowerPoint, including building workflow diagrams and organizational charts.
  • Must have demonstrated experience maintaining a document, policy, or knowledge library with disciplined version control.
  • Must be able to conduct independent research, validate source authorities, and summarize findings clearly.
  • Must have exceptional proofreading and copy-editing skills, with strong command of grammar, usage, and a recognized style guide.
  • Must be stakeholder engaging, with a service-oriented approach to fielding research requests.
  • Must be able to work well within Teams.
  • Must have excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Must have the ability to maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive data.
  • Must have the ability to manage multiple concurrent document actions in a fast-paced environment.
  • Must be able to work independently with minimal supervision in a fully remote setting.
  • Must be a U.S. Citizen and able to obtain and maintain a favorable CBP suitability determination.

Preferred:

  • Prior experience supporting CBP, DHS, or another federal law enforcement or homeland security organization.
  • Familiarity with federal policy document types (directives, handbooks, musters, SOPs, memoranda) and agency policy lifecycle and review processes.
  • Experience with routing sheets, staffing packages, or comparable government concurrence workflows.
  • Experience with SharePoint and web content management systems.
  • Working knowledge of Section 508 / WCAG accessibility requirements for documents and web content.
  • Experience researching statutory and regulatory authorities (U.S. Code, CFR, executive orders, agency directives

Salary Range: $80,000.00 to $90,000.00 annually. Actual compensation will be determined based on the selected candidate's experience, education, skills, and overall qualifications.
