description:
Overview

As a patient-focused organization, University of Utah Health exists to enhance the health and well-being of people through patient care, research and education. Success in this mission requires a culture of collaboration, excellence, leadership, and respect. University of Utah Health seeks staff that are committed to the values of compassion, collaboration, innovation, responsibility, integrity, quality and trust that are integral to our mission. EO/AA

This position performs routine and complex laboratory testing using manual and automated methods and procedures useful in patient diagnosis and treatment.

Corporate Overview: University of Utah Health is an integrated academic healthcare system with five hospitals including a level 1 trauma center, eleven community health centers, over 1,600 providers, and a health plan serving over 200,000 members. University of Utah Health is nationally ranked and recognized for our academic research, quality standards and overall patient experience. In addition to our clinical delivery system, we have a School of Medicine, School of Dentistry, College of Nursing, College of Pharmacy, and College of Health providing education and training for over 1,250 providers annually. We have over 2 million patient visits annually and research grants exceeding $350 million. University of Utah Hospitals and Clinics represents our clinical operations for the larger health system.

Responsibilities

Essential Functions

  • Receives and logs specimens, including demographic and testing information into laboratory database.
  • Communicates with appropriate personnel to verify recipient/donor information as necessary.
  • Performs specialized histocompatibility assays such as HLA typing, HLA antibody testing and crossmatching, using various techniques, with some assistance from senior staff.
  • Performs initial analysis of assays, with assistance from senior staff, as needed.
  • Enters results into laboratory computer system and may create reports.
  • Ensures attending physician or appropriate clinical personnel obtain patient lab results.
  • Prepares, labels, and performs quality control inspections on laboratory reagents under direction of senior staff.
  • Makes quality control record entries.
  • Monitors inventory of laboratory supplies.
  • Participates in conferences and continuing education.
  • Performs on-call work.

Knowledge / Skills / Abilities

  • Ability to perform the essential functions of the job as outlined above.
  • Demonstrated human relation and effective communication skills.
  • Ability to provide care appropriate to the population served.
  • Coordinate with other departments, physicians, residents, or patients effectively to ensure accurate diagnosis, information, and/or scheduling.
  • Capable of troubleshooting and recognizing technical problems as they arise, seeking assistance from the supervisor when controls fail and results are not as expected.
  • Incumbents in this position may be required to work unscheduled hours and rotate on call responsibilities.
  • The staff member must be able to demonstrate the knowledge and skills necessary to provide care appropriate to the age of the patients served on his or her assigned unit.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of the principles of life span growth and development and the ability to assess data regarding the patient's status and provide care as described in the department's policies and procedures manual.

Qualifications

Required

  • Bachelor's degree in Medical Laboratory Science or relevant science degree and one year of laboratory experience.

Qualifications (Preferred)

Preferred

  • American Society of Clinical Pathologist (ASCP) certification as a Medical Technologist or equivalency (ASCP certification equivalency for this position may be one year of lab experience).
  • One year of Lab Experience

Working Conditions and Physical Demands

Employee must be able to meet the following requirements with or without an accommodation.

  • This position involves light work that may exert up to 20 pounds and may consistently require light work involving lifting, carrying, pushing, pulling or otherwise moving objects or lab equipment. Workers in this position may be exposed to the chemicals used in a laboratory setting.

Physical Requirements

Color Determination, Lifting, Listening, Sitting, Speaking, Standing

title: Grades 9-12 Counselor
description:
Grades 9-12 School Counselor


McLean School (), a K-12 co-educational independent school in Potomac, Maryland, seeks a compassionate, skilled, and collaborative Grades 9-12 School Counselor to support students’ social-emotional well-being and learning and partner with faculty and families to foster student success. This 10-month position begins immediately and will remain open until filled. For 70 years, McLean School has helped bright K-12 students realize their full potential by providing a comprehensive college-preparatory program that emphasizes small classes and differentiated instruction. Through our Abilities Model®, we embrace both traditional learners and those with mild-to-moderate learning challenges. We recognize and teach individual strengths, responding to areas of challenge but never defining students by them.


The Upper School Counselor plays a vital role in supporting adolescents’ social, emotional, and behavioral development during a critical period of growth and transition. As a member of the Student Support and Social-Emotional Learning team, the counselor provides short-term direct counseling services, consults with teachers and families, and, as appropriate, with outside providers, and collaborates with administrators to ensure students are supported academically, emotionally, and socially as they prepare for postsecondary pathways.

Key Responsibilities

School-Wide & Preventive Programming

  • Contribute to the Upper School social-emotional learning initiatives, including programming focused on stress management, healthy relationships, identity development, and resilience.
  • Support wellness initiatives related to academic balance, technology use, and mental health awareness.
  • Assist with re-entry planning following extended absences, hospitalizations, or other significant disruptions.

Student Support

  • Support students with executive functioning, organization, time management, and
    strategies related to academic demands.
  • In consultation with the administration, provide short-term individual and small-group counseling to Upper School students to address anxiety, stress management, peer relationships, self-advocacy, and school adjustment.
  • Assist students in navigating transitions, including entry into Upper School, changes in academic placement, and preparation for postsecondary settings.
  • Provide crisis intervention, risk assessment, and safety
    planning in collaboration with school leadership.
  • Maintain timely and appropriate documentation consistent with school policies and professional standards.

Collaboration & Consultation

  • Work closely with Upper School faculty, advisors, Learning Services team, college counseling, and administrators to develop and implement student support plans.
  • Participate in student support meetings and grade-level meetings.
  • Consult with teachers on classroom strategies that promote wellness, engagement, and independence.
  • Partner with families to support adolescent development and reinforce strategies across home and school.


Professional Responsibilities

  • Maintain confidentiality and ethical standards consistent with licensure requirements and best practices for work with adolescents.
  • Engage in ongoing professional development related to adolescent mental health, social-emotional learning, trauma-informed practices, and supporting students with learning challenges.
  • Uphold McLean School’s mission, values, and commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging.


Qualifications

  • Master’s degree in Counseling, Social Work, Psychology, or a related field.
  • Maryland licensure or eligibility for licensure as a Counselor, Social Worker, or Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW).
  • Experience working with adolescents in a school setting.
  • Knowledge of adolescent development and mental health, including anxiety, depression, ADHD, and executive functioning challenges.
  • Knowledge of Individualized Education Plans and 504’s.
  • Strong interpersonal, organizational, and communication skills.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively within a multidisciplinary team.
  • Experience supporting students with self-advocacy and preparation for college or other postsecondary pathways.

Attributes

  • Warm, steady, and developmentally attuned to adolescents.
  • Proactive, flexible, and solutions-oriented.
  • Committed to fostering student independence, resilience, and self-awareness.
  • Strong alignment with McLean School’s inclusive and student-centered philosophy.

Salary Range: $70,000-$100,000


McLean School is an equal opportunity employer and considers all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, ancestry, national origin, age, sex, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, family responsibilities, disability, genetic status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. If you need reasonable accommodation due to a disability during recruitment, please contact the Director of Executive Support and Recruitment,
Robin Speller.

title: Engineering Intern - Summer 2027
description:
About Prime

About Prime Controls

Established in 2004, Prime Controls, L.P. is a family-owned Systems Integration and I&C Construction firm dedicated to meeting clients’ industrial automation and control requirements. As a Main Automation Contractor, we offer comprehensive solutions, supported by our size, expertise, and extensive experience. With a professional team of 1000+ employees, Prime Controls serves customers nationwide from our Dallas, Texas headquarters and offices throughout the United States. Our mission is to deliver the highest quality professional services while prioritizing our employees’ well-being and fostering an exceptional workplace environment.

Overview

The Role

Spend your summer building real instrumentation & controls (I&C) systems alongside our engineering team. As an Engineering Intern, you’ll support active projects across data center, energy, semiconductor, and water/wastewater markets—and see how a Platinum Rockwell Automation partner takes a project from design through commissioning.

Responsibilities

  • Support design engineers in developing instrumentation and electrical design deliverables, including drawings, panel layouts, and wiring diagrams.
  • Assist with PLC, HMI, and SCADA configuration and testing under the guidance of senior engineers.
  • Participate in systems and application engineering tasks, including factory acceptance testing (FAT).
  • Help compile submittals, technical documentation, and as-built records.
  • Research components and support procurement and bill-of-material (BOM) activities.
  • Attend project meetings and site walkdowns to understand end-to-end project execution.

What You’ll Bring

Required

  • Currently pursuing a bachelor’s degree in Electrical, Mechanical, Computer, or a related engineering discipline.
  • Rising junior or senior standing preferred; in good academic standing.
  • Coursework or familiarity with controls, circuits, or automation concepts.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office.
  • Strong problem-solving and communication skills and a willingness to learn in both office and field settings.
  • Available to work full-time for the duration of the summer program; travel to project locations may be required.

Preferred

  • Exposure to AutoCAD, EPLAN, or PLC programming.
  • Prior internship, co-op, or hands-on project experience.

Internship Details

  • This is a full-time summer internship running approximately 8–10 weeks during Summer 2027, based at various Prime Controls locations.
  • Interns work alongside experienced professionals on meaningful, real-world projects and receive mentorship throughout the program.
  • The internship is designed to build practical, career-ready skills and to help interns explore career paths at Prime Controls.
  • Strong performers may be considered for future internship terms or full-time opportunities.

Work Environment & Physical Demands (Text Only)

When on site, the intern may be exposed to outdoor weather conditions, moderate to loud noise, and typical construction hazards, and must follow all site safety and personal protective equipment (PPE) requirements. title: 2026 Sr. Program Organizer
description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

The Sr. Program Organizer will support a team of part-time Program Organizers (POs) in delivering efficient and thoughtful support to program participants, as well as supporting the program as a full-time Program Organizer themselves.


This is a fast-paced, scaling program, and we're looking for someone who hits their stride in that kind of environment — someone who picks up new information quickly, adapts as priorities shift, and brings genuine passion for democratic participation to everything they do. As a Sr. Program Organizer, you’ll develop a deep, holistic understanding of the program that allows you to move fluidly between tasks and priorities, carrying knowledge and momentum from one assignment into the next.


You’ll work closely with the Deputy Director of Program, Organizer Experience to oversee a pod of part-time POs. Our POs are the heart of Rally Organizing Programs – creating virtual experiences that leave participants feeling enthusiastic, supported, and confident as trusted messengers in their communities. POs work in shifts, covering both event leadership and inbox support. As Sr. Program Organizer, you’ll be the first level of support for a pod of POs, ensuring the consistent high quality of staff performance and participant experience by regularly observing and providing feedback on event quality and identifying areas for improvement, as well as supporting them through their onboarding & training phase. While you serve as a team captain, you also act as a full-time Program Organizer, being willing to jump into any role a part-time Program Organizer covers at a moment’s notice - often jumping between tasks and priorities.


We’re looking for people who are excited about creating team culture for a diverse group of individuals and supporting a group of part-time staff as they navigate a quickly ramping role. You’re also ready to jump into a fast-paced environment yourself and be the person the team can count on when we need a gap filled! You’re comfortable coaching teams through encouragement and don’t shy away from addressing challenging moments. If you’re energized by helping teams reach their full potential and shifting priorities, we’d love to have you on our team.


This is a full-time, remote, and temporary position with an estimated start date of Tuesday, September 29 and an end date of Friday, November 13.

DETAILS & COMPENSATION

Location: Remote

Compensation: $5,860/month

Schedule: Full-time

Hours Expectations: This role requires a flexible schedule, including some evenings and weekends, to accommodate recruitment and event volume. We anticipate a six day workweek in the final stretch, starting in October and running through Election Day.

JOB DUTIES

  • Work with the Deputy Director of Program, Organizer Experience to create the team culture for the POs, including: information sharing, feedback structure, event quality
  • Serve as the primary lead for a designated cohort of POs
    • Host regular in check-ins, answer questions, and share program updates
    • Provide constructive, actionable feedback and coaching to POs to strengthen their event facilitation and inbox coordination
  • Serve as a full-time Program Organizer, including swinging into the following roles:
    • Event Leadership: Lead 1-hour virtual events end-to-end, serving as the face of the program to participants. Each event involves filling one of three rotating event roles, managing breakout rooms throughout the session, and monitoring rapid-response Slack channels in real time.
      • Above all, Program Organizers foster a positive, inclusive environment where participants feel supported, confident, and excited about the work they're doing. A customer service and solutions-oriented mindset is key — you'll be fielding questions on the fly and helping participants troubleshoot in real time, all while keeping the energy high.
    • Inbox Support: Work in the inbox as the primary point of contact for our participants, responding to inquiries via the program inbox and providing timely, accurate, and helpful information. You'll assist participants in navigating program logistics, requirements, deadlines, and resources — and where needed, identify and troubleshoot issues or escalate them to the appropriate team.
      • This isn't just reactive support. You'll proactively follow up with participants to ensure they're on track, help with onboarding processes, and gather feedback on participant experiences to share with the broader team. A solutions-oriented mindset and genuine empathy for participants are essential — we want every participant to feel supported every step of the way.

title: Technical Account Engineer
description:
What You Can Expect

In this role, you serve as the primary technical point of contact for Zoom's most strategic enterprise customers, owning integration challenges from first report to final resolution across Zoom's full suite of Video, Native, Mobile, and CoBrowse SDKs. Day to day, you partner with SDK engineering, Solutions Engineers, and CSMs to diagnose multi-layer technical problems, lead customer troubleshooting calls, and translate complex issues into documented solutions that millions of developers depend on. Candidates without hands-on experience reading and debugging code across JavaScript, TypeScript, or Python, or without direct API/SDK integration or troubleshooting experience, will find the core technical demands of this role difficult to meet. This is a strong opportunity for a technically grounded customer advocate ready to solve hard problems and make a measurable difference at scale. This role reports to a Manager, Technical Account Engineer.

About the Team

The API & SDK team serves as the embedded technical experts for Zoom's most demanding enterprise accounts, covering the full lifecycle of SDK and API integration challenges across Video, Native, Mobile, and CoBrowse SDKs. We collaborate closely with iOS, Web, and CoBrowse engineering alongside TAMs, CSMs, and Solutions Engineers to ensure end-to-end issue ownership and resolution. Our mission is to keep Zoom's most strategic customers running and make their developers' lives easier.

Responsibilities

  • Own end-to-end technical support for enterprise customers integrating Zoom's Video SDK (Web, iOS, Android), Meeting SDK, Native SDK, Mobile SDK, and CoBrowse SDK into their products.
  • Debug across the full stack, including client-side JavaScript/TypeScript, native iOS (Swift/Objective-C) and Android (Kotlin/Java), Python backend services, and REST/WebSocket APIs.
  • Reproduce, isolate, and document customer-reported bugs using session logs, HAR traces, and SDK diagnostics, then drive resolution in close partnership with engineering.
  • Lead technical troubleshooting calls with customer engineering teams to diagnose issues, provide workarounds, and coordinate fixes with Zoom SDK engineering.
  • Translate customer pain into engineering action by filing detailed bug reports, advocating for feature requests, and ensuring fixes land in the right SDK release.
  • Develop and deliver customer-facing technical documentation, architecture diagrams, migration guides, and release-impact assessments.

What We're Looking For

  • 5+ years of experience in developer advocacy, solutions engineering, or developer relations, with a focus on API/SDK integration, troubleshooting, or customer enablement
  • Working knowledge of JavaScript, TypeScript, and Python, with comfort reading and debugging code written by others
  • Solid understanding of RESTful APIs, OAuth 2.0 (Server-to-Server and Authorization Code), webhooks, and API rate-limit patterns
  • Hands-on experience integrating or troubleshooting client-side SDKs (Web, iOS, or Android); experience with real-time communication SDKs such as WebRTC, SIP, or SRTP is a plus
  • Ability to analyze network traces, console logs, HAR files, and crash reports to isolate and pinpoint root cause
  • Proven ability to communicate with equal clarity to engineering and product audiences, with strong written and verbal English skills
  • Experience with iOS (Swift/Objective-C), Android (Kotlin/Java), CoBrowse technologies, RTMS, media pipelines, or CI/CD frameworks for SDK releases is a bonus

Ways of Working
Our structured hybrid approach is centered around our offices and remote work environments. The work style of each role, Hybrid, Remote, or In-Person is indicated in the job description/posting.


Benefits
As part of our award-winning workplace culture and commitment to delivering happiness, our benefits program offers a variety of perks, benefits, and options to help employees maintain their physical, mental, emotional, and financial health; support work-life balance; and contribute to their community in meaningful ways. Click Learnfor more information.


About Us
Zoomies help people stay connected so they can get more done together. We set out to build the best collaboration platform for the enterprise, and today help people communicate better with products like Zoom Contact Center, Zoom Phone, Zoom Events, Zoom Apps, Zoom Rooms, and Zoom Webinars.
We’re problem-solvers, working at a fast pace to design solutions with our customers and users in mind. Find room to grow with opportunities to stretch your skills and advance your career in a collaborative, growth-focused environment.

Our Commitment

At Zoom, we believe great work happens when people feel supported and empowered. We’re committed to fair hiring practices that ensure every candidate is evaluated based on skills, experience, and potential. If you require an accommodation during the hiring process, let us know—we’re here to support you at every step.

This form is solely for applicants who require an accommodation due to a qualifying medical disability. Non-accommodation-related requests, such as application follow-ups or technical issues, will not be addressed.


Our interviews are supported by BrightHire, a tool that helps us create a consistent and thoughtful interview experience and may include recordings. Please refer to our candidate privacy statement for more information of how we use your data.

title: Literacy Research Associate
description:
Overview

Are you passionate about supporting and partnering with educators to improve educational opportunities and outcomes, with a focus on English language arts/literacy instruction? Are you looking for opportunities to use your experience, knowledge, and research skills to support educators to improve teaching, learning, and the systems that support them? Are you an enthusiastic collaborator, eager to work closely with colleagues and grow your skill set? Do you value working directly with practitioners through applied research and examining questions of critical interest to educators?

SRI Education is committed to designing and implementing high-quality research, evaluation, and technical assistance (i.e., providing research-grounded support to educators). We investigate and influence critical questions and issues in K–12 and postsecondary education, improving systems, enhancing instruction, addressing student wellbeing, and supporting diverse learners. We seek to hire an Literacy Research Associate with experience conducting research who can contribute to projects focused on English language arts (ELA)/literacy as well as support projects across other education content areas.

This position is fully remote within the U.S., however if you prefer onsite and are located near an SRI office, we may accommodate a hybrid work schedule.

Responsibilities

  • Work on an interdisciplinary team to evaluate and/or provide technical assistance for large-scale improvement efforts. These are likely to include professional learning programs or the development of new resources designed to support foundational skills, reading comprehension, multilingual learners, writing from source material, and disciplinary literacy at scale.
  • Lend ELA/literacy expertise to projects on an ad hoc basis (provide occasional consultation or targeted contributions around topics such as: literacy assessment, measuring literacy-focused instructional practice, review of ELA curricular materials, and reviewing and synthesizing current literacy research.
  • Conduct literature, website, document, and policy scans and reviews.
  • Support data collection and analysis (e.g., survey administration and data visualizations; scheduling and conducting classroom observations; conducting interviews and analyzing qualitative data).
  • Provide project management and coordination support (e.g., tracking progress toward project milestones; making recommendations for project procedures; creating, organizing, and managing project documents and databases, such as schedules and status reports for clients).
  • Prepare district research applications and Institutional Review Board (IRB) packages.
  • Contribute to meeting facilitation via activities such as taking notes, summarizing and synthesizing themes, coordinating collection of feedback, and analyzing data and summarizing results.
  • Prepare reports, briefs, and presentations of research findings appropriate for non-academic, academic, and policy audiences.
  • Consider diverse perspectives and experiences in our work.
  • Engage in professional learning through ongoing project-embedded mentorship and professional development opportunities.

Qualifications

  • Cover letter is required: In your cover letter, in addition to describing what interests you about this position, please include information about your training and experience in ELA/literacy
  • A master’s degree in the social sciences, education, policy, or related fields
  • 2 years ELA/literacy teaching experience (K–12) in the US public education system, especially in historically underserved communities;
  • Due to contract requirements, U.S. citizenship is required.
  • Experience with multiple research and/or technical assistance methods, such as:
    • Research methods may include large-scale surveys, experimental research, or case study methods, with strong preference for experience in K-12 school settings
    • Technical assistance methods may include activities such as contributing to needs sensing, conceptualizing technical assistance plans, designing educator professional learning activities, or developing tools to support data use and/or use of evidence-based practices in K-12 school system
  • Experience writing well-structured, clear, and concise research summaries and sections of reports or briefs, or translating existing research into presentations, tools, and resources for educators and/or policymakers
  • Ability to discuss research tasks or technical assistance activities with individuals and organizations in the field, study sites, or study participants;
  • Capacity to support multiple projects simultaneously and change focus as priorities shift through use of strong organizational skills
  • Knowledge of software applications such as Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint
  • Willingness to travel 5-6 times per year for school site visits, with many visits lasting for 3-4 days each

*Candidates who proceed to the interview process will be asked to provide writing samples.

The salary range is: $56,776-$94,040/yr. Salary ranges will vary and are based on several factors, including geographic location, market competitiveness and equity amongst internal employees in similar roles. Positions may also qualify for SRI's Pay for Outstanding Performance program or the annual Performance Based Compensation program. SRI also has a competitive benefits package, to view details please go to https://www.sri.com/resources/benefits/. SRI will accept applications until the position is filled.

SRI is an independent nonprofit research institute headquartered in Menlo Park, Calif., with a rich history of supporting government and industry. We create and deliver world-changing solutions for a safer, healthier, and more sustainable future. For almost 80 years, we have collaborated across technical and scientific disciplines to discover and develop groundbreaking products and technologies and bring innovations and ideas to the marketplace.

title: Construction Superintendent
description:
Overview

Next 150 Construction is seeking a Construction Superintendent III. The Construction Superintendent II/III leads complex trade scopes or multiple crews within a major project, providing direct field leadership to ensure work is executed in accordance with approved scope, safety requirements, quality standards, and schedule commitments. This role supports self-performance operations while collaborating closely with the Lead Superintendent on jobsite logistics, resource planning, and sequencing, mentoring junior field leaders, workforce coordination, and union engagement while assisting with advanced planning and execution activities.

This position also supports the implementation of field technology, sustainability practices, and continuous improvement initiatives to enhance safety, quality, and operational efficiency. This role will report onsite in New Florence, MO daily.

Responsibilities

  • Leads and coordinates assigned trade contractors, self-performed crews, and field activities to ensure work is executed safely, efficiently, and in accordance with approved scope, schedule, and quality requirements
  • Develops, documents, and communicates detailed work plans for assigned scopes and ensures compliance with approved work plans and field directives
  • Maintains a thorough understanding of contract documents, drawings, specifications, and coordination requirements to support effective trade-level planning; verifies that all required permits, inspections, and compliance documentation are in place for assigned work areas
  • Acts as the primary Next 150 safety representative for assigned scopes, enforces applicable safety policies and procedures, and supports a strong safety-first culture in the field
  • Oversees quality control for assigned trades, conducts inspections, documents findings, and implements corrective actions to maintain compliance with project and company standards
  • Leads contractor meetings related to assigned scopes and coordinates activities with field and project leadership
  • Maintains accurate daily field reports, safety documentation, and production records using Procore and other required systems
  • Creates and manages trade-level schedules and implements contingency plans to maintain commitments and mitigate impacts; communicates schedule status, constraints, and updates to the applicable team
  • Plans and manages jobsite logistics for assigned scopes, including access, material flow, temporary facilities, and sequencing
  • Assists in resolving jurisdictional disputes and field-level conflicts within assigned scopes
  • Tracks production, labor hours, and productivity metrics, and reports variances to field leadership
  • Executes self-perform operations for assigned scopes, including workforce planning and quantification of labor, materials, and equipment needs
  • Assists with forecasting and cost-of-work projections for assigned scopes
  • Coaches and mentors less experienced team members; trains team members to help support skill development and consistent execution
  • Supports a positive and inclusive work environment
  • Supports sustainability initiatives and environmental compliance requirements within assigned scopes
  • Collaborates with the Lead Superintendent on advanced planning, resource allocation, and continuous improvement initiatives

Qualifications

KEY COMPETENCIES

  • Communicate Effectively - Listen to understand and clearly convey information in all forms based on the audience to ensure shared meaning of the message.
  • Act Inclusively - Ensure that actions and behaviors are respectful; show empathy and treat others with dignity. Leverage capabilities and insights of individuals with diverse perspectives, abilities and motivation.
  • Solve Problems - Identify, prioritize and implement alternatives for a solution.
  • Demonstrate Agility/Adaptability - Maintain effectiveness and adjust to change by exploring the rationale, trying new approaches, and collaborating with others to make the change successful. Create an atmosphere of open-mindedness to change.
  • Drive for Results - Show passion and commitment while delivering on business outcomes. Create a sense of individual ownership and accountability.
  • Champion Innovation - Identify opportunities for new and improved ways of doing things that result in value added, unique and differentiated solutions.

EXPERIENCE/EDUCATION

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Engineering or Construction Management
  • Minimum 2-8 years of experience in a superintendent role on construction projects
  • OSHA 30 hour certified
  • Or equivalent combination of education and experience

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & ABILITIES

  • Strong technical and communication skills
  • Excellent organizational skills
  • Ability to work in a team environment
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office, safety and site operations software, project management software, and construction management software
  • Knowledge of construction-documenting and drawing, with knowledge of all phases of construction
  • Knowledge in all divisions of work, methods, materials, scheduling and cost control
  • Ability to create a “safety first” environment by showing a commitment to Zero Injury principles and sustainability practices
  • Strong union and non-union engagement and labor relations

Next 150 Construction Services has an unwavering focus on safety, the environment and caring about everyone involved in our work.

Qualified applicants who are offered a position must pass a pre-employment substance abuse test.

Next 150 Construction Services is not accepting unsolicited resumes from third party recruiters at this time.

Next 150 Construction Services is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, color, national origin, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, protected veteran status, or disability status.

title: Event Conversion Labourer
description:
Job Description

Part-Time; Event-Based

Wage: $31.54/hour (PG12P) plus 10% in lieu of benefits and vacation.

Date Posted: September 23, 2026

Who we are…

The Pacific National Exhibition is an iconic institution in BC, famous for bringing generations of people together to celebrate and build memories. This 116-year-old, non-profit organization has an annual operating budget of over $70 million dollars and generates revenue through four activity streams: the 15-day annual summer Fair which averages more than 700,000 people annually, Playland amusement park which welcomes 400,000 guests annually including Fright Nights, and a busy year-round portfolio of events including concerts, trade shows and film, cultural and community events. In total we bring over 2 million people through the site each year. The fourth activity stream is park care and facility maintenance. The PNE is proud of the work it does at Hastings Park and has a vibrant team that is passionate about events, guest experience and delivering memorable experiences.

At the PNE, we strive to create an environment that reflects our organization’s core values: Enthusiasm, Excellence and Evolution. With a focus on these core values, we are committed to achieving our mission which is to “Deliver Memorable Experiences” for all who interact with the PNE whether it is our guests, our employees, or the community.

We are seeking diligent and hard-working individuals that have a passion for the Events industry and the Pacific National Exhibition (PNE). Our Labourer team works work under the direction of the Director, PNE Maintenance & Facility Operations and are responsible for site maintenance, and setup/teardown of events. They will operate vehicles and tools/equipment in compliance with all health and safety requirements as determined by WorkSafeBC, and all other applicable legislation and company policies.

Why join our Team?

  • Exhilarating and fun-loving culture
  • Flexible work environment
  • Opportunity for free or discounted tickets to shows, events, sports games, and much more
  • Staff discounts for Playland, The Fair, and Fright Nights, as well as all PNE Food Stands
  • Competitive compensation package
  • Opportunity to create lasting memories and friendships!

What will you do this year?

In your role as an Event Conversion Labourer, your primary accountabilities will be to:

  • Help in the set-up of events by moving equipment, furniture, cleaning, setting up seating, hockey boards (dashers), Bleachers Seats and general event prep etc.
  • Perform maintenance and janitorial tasks including cleaning washrooms, mopping, sweeping, vacuuming, and stocking supplies as needed.
  • Service and maintain equipment operated by site maintenance.
  • Effectively use heavy and light equipment, depending on the jobsite/assignment.
  • Assemble and dismantle special event facilities.
  • Maintain a safe and clean work environment.
  • Perform other related work as required.

What else?

  • Previous general labour and janitorial experience is required.
  • Must be capable of lifting 50lb objects; be highly motivated and able to work alone.
  • A valid class 5 BC driver’s license is required.
  • Previous experience operating a forklift is preferred.
  • A valid forklift operating license is an asset.
  • A valid aerial lift or fall arrest certification is an asset.
  • Knowledge of materials, methods and equipment used in janitorial work.
  • Knowledge of methods and practices used in servicing and maintaining equipment operated.
  • Knowledge of methods, materials, tools, and equipment used in assembling and dismantling special event facilities and in performing maintenance and janitorial tasks.
  • Successful completion of grade 12 preferred.
  • OFA Level I (or higher) is considered an asset.
  • Skill in the operation of construction and maintenance equipment and the use of tools used in servicing, minor maintenance tasks are desirable.
  • Ability to carry out work orders and prepare and maintain work records.
  • Must have CSA approved steel toe boots.
  • Must be available to work a variety of shifts including weekends, weekdays, and overnight shifts.
  • Must be comfortable working an event-based schedule, as hours of work will vary.
  • Candidates must undergo a Criminal Record Check.

Who are you?

  • Team Player
  • Passionate
  • Skillful communicator
  • Proactive
  • Committed

Where and when to APPLY?

Applications can be submitted via the PNE website at www.pne.ca/jobs and will be accepted until the role is filled.

Preference will be given to candidates who submit their resume/cover letter before Sunday, October 11th. We look forward to hearing from you!

The PNE is proud to be an equal opportunity employer, committed to creating an inclusive workforce that reflects the diverse community we proudly serve. All applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, colour, national or ethnic origin, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, disability, or age. title: Process Automation Lead
description:
We bring the energy!

Through purpose and people - not just through the infrastructure we operate, but through the way we show up for each other, our customers’ and our communities. The future of energy is in our hands. Let’s shape it together.

Go beyond keeping the lights on. Solve energy challenges that matter most.

We have an opportunity for a Process Automation Lead to join our team. As the Process Automation Lead, you’ll lead a small team of Process Automation Specialists to map, simplify, re-engineer and automate how work is performed across AusNet. You’ll enforce the standards for process analysis and automation delivery, prioritise and allocate your team’s capacity against the highest value opportunities, and run a disciplined delivery cadence.

Combining deep process expertise with hands-on automation capability and people leadership, you’ll reduce manual effort, improve quality and create measurable business value using technologies such as Microsoft Power Automate and emerging AI-enabled automation and process management / mapping tools.


What you’ll be doing:

  • Lead and develop a team of three Process Automation Specialists, building capability in process analysis, re-engineering and automation.

  • Manage the automation pipeline, prioritising work based on value, risk, urgency and team capacity.

  • Drive delivery through effective backlog management, planning, reviews and continuous improvement.

  • Maintain process mapping, re-engineering and automation standards aligned to Enterprise Process Management frameworks.

  • Act as the senior contact for process automation, reporting on priorities, performance and realised benefits.

  • Partner with stakeholders to analyse current-state processes, identify pain points, waste and improvement opportunities.

  • Facilitate workshops to uncover process issues and define automation opportunities.

  • Establish a clear understanding of current-state processes, controls, data, dependencies and performance baselines.

  • Document current and future-state processes using agreed modelling standards and frameworks.

  • Simplify and redesign processes by removing waste, addressing root causes and avoiding automation of inefficient practices.

  • Assess and prioritise automation opportunities based on value, feasibility, risk and return on investment.

  • Translate business needs into clear requirements, acceptance criteria and solution designs.

  • Oversee the design, build, testing, deployment and maintenance of workflow and robotic process automations.

  • Ensure security, privacy, compliance, auditability and operational support requirements are embedded throughout the automation lifecycle.

  • Lead testing, defect resolution, deployment, training and handover activities.

  • Monitor automation performance, adoption and benefits, driving continuous improvement.

  • Evaluate emerging AI and automation capabilities and apply them where safe, governed and appropriate.


You don’t need to check every box; however, we’re looking for a good combination of:

  • Demonstrated people leadership experience, including leading, coaching and developing a small team of specialists and managing performance, development and workload.

  • Proven ability to manage capacity allocation and demand across multiple concurrent initiatives and competing stakeholder priorities, with transparent trade-offs and realistic commitments.

  • Deep, demonstrated expertise analysing, mapping and improving end-to-end business processes, including current and future-state design – familiarity with industry standard process frameworks and methodologies strongly regarded, with the ability to set standards and uplift others.

  • Demonstrated experience in process optimisation, including but not limited to identifying process waste and process re-engineering for value outcomes.

  • Demonstrated experience in process simulations (manual or automated)

  • Hands-on experience designing, building, testing and supporting workflow or robotic process automations.

  • ·Experience with Process mapping tools strongly regarded.

  • Experience with automation tools. Microsoft Power Automate experience is desirable.

  • Ability to elicit and translate business needs into clear requirements, acceptance criteria and practical automation designs.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capability, with a focus on removing root causes and delivering measurable outcomes.

  • Ability to work directly with stakeholders at different levels, facilitate process discussions and communicate technical concepts in plain language.

  • Understanding of automation lifecycle practices including development standards, testing, deployment, exception handling, monitoring, documentation and support.

  • Awareness of AI-enabled automation, process mining, Copilot capabilities and responsible AI considerations is desirable.

  • Awareness of cyber security, privacy, data governance, records management and regulatory obligations relevant to automation solutions.

  • Relevant tertiary qualification in business, technology, engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.

  • Experience in utilities, energy or another regulated and operationally complex environment is desirable.

  • Strongly Regarded: Expertise or accreditation in BABOK, Lean, Kaizen, Six Sigma, APQC, Scrum Master or equivalent agile certification, and experience in process mapping and process mapping toolsets


The AusNet experience is all about…

  • Growing your impact: We’ll support you to build your career through real opportunities and strong connections.

  • Solving some of the most complex energy challenges of our time: We love unpacking complex challenges in clever ways and looking at things differently.

  • Being part of a team that cares deeply about each other: We share in the good times and support in the tough times.


We’re committed to building an inclusive culture and a diverse workforce. We believe different perspectives are essential to our success, and we encourage all applicants to apply. If you need any adjustments during the recruitment process, we're happy to discuss how we can support you.


At AusNet, we bring the energy! Ready to make your impact? Apply now!

title: Applied ML Engineer
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an Applied ML Engineer based in Switzerland.

As an Applied ML Engineer, you’ll work at the intersection of machine learning research, experimentation, and production engineering.
You’ll turn ideas from research papers into rigorous experiments, measurable evidence, and reliable products.
The role spans model evaluation, model internals, inference infrastructure, backend systems, and user-facing product experiences.
You’ll work hands-on with modern ML models, designing evaluations that reveal what methods can—and cannot—demonstrate.
You’ll also build production-grade tooling that makes complex experiments repeatable, observable, and accessible to users.
The environment values technical judgment, ownership, scientific rigor, and the ability to move comfortably across the technology stack.
It’s an opportunity to help transform emerging ML techniques into practical systems that people can trust.

Accountabilities

  • Reproduce and evaluate machine learning research methods using open-weight and API-accessible models.
  • Design evaluation datasets, probes, scoring approaches, baselines, calibration tests, and experiment harnesses.
  • Work directly with model weights, logits, hidden states, activations, model APIs, and inference infrastructure when required.
  • Build and extend evaluation infrastructure covering experiment runners, judges, persistence, orchestration, reporting, and reproducibility.
  • Turn research workflows into intuitive product experiences, including experiment configuration, execution, traces, comparisons, reports, and review workflows.
  • Investigate how verification methods behave when models are modified through fine-tuning, merging, quantization, distillation, safety removal, or deliberate evasion.
  • Design controlled experiments that distinguish meaningful signals from artifacts, confounders, and misleading correlations.
  • Produce clear technical reports that separate measured evidence from interpretation and hypotheses.
  • Deliver production-quality systems with APIs, asynchronous jobs, databases, observability, testing, deployment, and documentation.
  • Contribute across research, experimentation, engineering, and product as priorities evolve.
  • During the first six months, reproduce and document at least one published model-provenance or verification method, including its capabilities, assumptions, and limitations.
  • Build a repeatable model-verification runner with versioned inputs, artifacts, metrics, and reports, and make at least one verification workflow accessible through the product interface.
  • Run controlled experiments across base, fine-tuned, merged, quantized, and known distilled models, improving understanding of when verification methods succeed, fail, and why.

    • Requirements:

    • Strong Python engineering skills, with hands-on experience using PyTorch and Hugging Face Transformers.
    • Solid understanding of machine learning evaluation, including dataset design, baselines, metrics, calibration, false positives and negatives, statistical uncertainty, and reproducibility.
    • Ability to read ML research papers critically and implement methods from first principles rather than relying entirely on existing packages.
    • Professional software engineering experience beyond notebooks, including APIs, asynchronous jobs, databases, logging, testing, deployment, and documentation.
    • Familiarity with open-weight models and a practical understanding of how modern LLM inference systems operate.
    • Ability to work across backend and frontend boundaries, with sufficient React/TypeScript knowledge to help make complex experiments and results understandable to users.
    • Strong experimental and analytical judgment, particularly around distinguishing what evidence demonstrates from what it merely suggests.
    • High ownership and initiative, with the ability to identify problems, propose solutions, and drive projects forward independently.
    • Comfort working in a fast-moving startup environment where priorities can change quickly and engineers may operate across multiple functions.
    • Experience with model provenance, fingerprinting, watermarking, distillation detection, red-teaming, safety evaluation, interpretability, or related areas is a plus.
    • Experience with activation and representation analysis, probing, model hooks, logits, hidden states, or other model-internals techniques is advantageous.
    • Familiarity with evaluation and inference infrastructure such as DSPy, LiteLLM, Temporal, Ray, vLLM, PostgreSQL/pgvector, or comparable technologies is beneficial.
    • Experience with Next.js, React, TypeScript, data visualization, or experiment dashboards is a plus.
    • Experience running and serving open-weight models on GPUs, including reasoning about latency, throughput, memory, precision, and cost trade-offs, is valuable.
    • Experience designing adversarial evaluations or testing systems against deliberate attempts to evade detection is an advantage.
    • A strong commitment to producing production-quality code, tests, tooling, and documentation that other engineers can confidently operate and extend.

      • Benefits:

      • Opportunity to work on applied machine learning at the intersection of research, experimentation, engineering, and product.
      • End-to-end ownership across model evaluation, model internals, infrastructure, backend systems, and user-facing experiences.
      • Exposure to modern open-weight models, LLM inference systems, and emerging ML verification techniques.
      • A role with significant technical autonomy and the opportunity to shape both experiments and production systems.
      • Fast-moving startup environment with evolving priorities and cross-functional collaboration.
      • Opportunity to translate cutting-edge research into practical, measurable, and user-accessible products.
      • The opportunity to build systems and evaluation methodologies designed to produce evidence that users can understand and trust.
      • Location: Romania.
      • Additional compensation, flexibility, healthcare, and other benefits may be provided according to the partner company's employment package and local arrangements.

title: Modeling & Simulation Specialist
description:
About the Role

Culmen International is seeking a Modeling & Simulation Specialist.

The Specialist will provide designing, developing, and integrating modeling and simulation capabilities into public health and medical preparedness exercises, evaluations, and analytical activities. The specialist converts operational requirements and technical data into realistic, dynamic scenarios that help its partners assess readiness, identify gaps, validate plans and policies, and improve response capabilities.

What You’ll Do in Your New Role

  • Design, develop, test, and maintain modeling and simulation solutions that support federal public health and medical emergency preparedness, response, recovery, and continuity missions.
  • Integrate computer simulation and model outputs into exercise programs and dynamic scenarios for real-time delivery to participants.
  • Develop realistic simulation environments, games, data-driven injects, visual interfaces, video vignettes, and other enhancements for discussion-based and operations-based exercises.
  • Translate exercise objectives, operational plans, policies, corrective actions, and subject-matter input into simulation requirements, workflows, and technical products.
  • Support the full Homeland Security Exercise and Evaluation Program planning cycle, including scenario development, planning conferences, Master Scenario Events List development and synchronization, exercise execution, hotwashes, after-action activities, and corrective-action adjudication.
  • Develop and apply analytical tools to evaluate exercises and real-world response operations, identify recurring trends, and support evidence-based recommendations.
  • Analyze and visualize exercise, evaluation, corrective-action, and planning data using innovative technologies and reproducible methods.
  • Review technical and analytical results for accuracy, validity, usability, and alignment with exercise objectives and requirements.
  • Prepare and present technical findings, model outputs, demonstrations, briefings, reports, and decision-support materials to ASPR, HHS leadership, and interagency stakeholders.
  • Collaborate with exercise planners, facilitators, evaluators, analysts, systems personnel, and subject matter experts to ensure simulation capabilities are operationally relevant and effectively integrated.
  • Maintain current knowledge of industry standards, emerging technologies, and best practices related to modeling, simulation, distributed participation, and virtual exercise delivery.
  • Complete recurring and short-turn technical assignments within established deadlines and maintain accessible, organized project files and deliverables.
  • Travel as authorized to support exercise planning, execution, evaluation, training, real-world response activities, conferences, or meetings.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in a related field; a higher degree in a related field is a plus.
  • 2+ years of relevant experience designing games or simulations for the U.S. Government.
  • Experience in the development of computer simulation capabilities for use in government training, exercises, or operational environments.
  • Experience developing models and simulation requirements and supporting the ongoing maintenance of exercise or training databases and systems.
  • Experience integrating new developments into virtual simulation environments or other distributed exercise platforms.
  • Ability to interpret technical and operational requirements, evaluate model outputs, and clearly communicate findings to technical and nontechnical audiences.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft 365 applications and the ability to learn and use government-provided databases, collaboration tools, and analytical platforms.
  • Ability to meet deadlines, manage multiple priorities, and respond effectively to short-notice or surge requirements.
  • Ability to travel and work occasional evenings, weekends, or holidays when authorized and required by the task order.

Desired Qualifications

  • Experience with specialized modeling and simulation tools, including Advanced Modeling System tools and Computer-Aided Design (CAD) applications.
  • Knowledge of HSEEP doctrine and experience supporting seminars, workshops, tabletop exercises, games, drills, functional exercises, or full-scale exercises.
  • Experience supporting public health preparedness, emergency management, consequence modeling, incident response, continuity, or interagency operations.
  • Familiarity with the National Response Framework, National Incident Management System, Emergency Support Function #8, and federal preparedness and response doctrine.
  • Experience with data visualization, trend analysis, scenario-based analysis, and presentation of technical results to senior government stakeholders.
  • Experience producing accessible digital content and deliverables consistent with Section 508 requirements.

Culmen International is committed to enhancing international safety and security, strengthening homeland defense, advancing humanitarian missions, and optimizing government operations. With experience in over 150 countries, Culmen supports our clients to accomplish critical missions in challenging environments.

title: GSE Technician III
description:
JOB SUMMARY

The Ground Support Equipment (GSE) Technician III is a senior-level technician responsible for diagnosing, troubleshooting, repairing, rebuilding, maintaining, and inspecting a wide variety of ground support equipment, fleet vehicles, powered industrial trucks, generators, tow tractors, hydraulic systems, diesel and gasoline engines, electrical systems, and other support equipment used in aircraft maintenance operations. This position serves as a technical resource and mentor for GSE Technicians I and II while assisting with maintaining a safe, reliable, and operational GSE fleet supporting FAA Part 145 repair station operations.

Employees in this position are required to furnish and maintain the tools necessary to perform the essential functions of the job in accordance with the Company's Tool Program.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Diagnose complex mechanical, hydraulic, pneumatic, fuel, steering, suspension, braking, and electrical system failures on GSE and company fleet vehicles.
  • Perform advanced troubleshooting utilizing computer diagnostic software, electrical test equipment, schematics, service manuals, and manufacturer specifications.
  • Perform major repairs, overhauls, component replacements, preventive maintenance, and inspections on a variety of ground support equipment.
  • Fabricate, repair, and modify metal components using approved fabrication techniques and welding equipment, when qualified.
  • Read and interpret electrical schematics, hydraulic diagrams, blueprints, and technical manuals.
  • Perform preventive maintenance inspections and ensure equipment remains in safe operating condition.
  • Conduct operational testing following repairs to verify equipment performance and reliability.
  • Assist management with troubleshooting recurring maintenance issues, identifying root causes, and recommending corrective actions.
  • Research replacement parts, vendor information, technical manuals, and repair procedures.
  • Mentor and provide technical guidance to GSE Technician I and II employees.
  • Complete maintenance records, repair orders, inspection reports, and other required documentation accurately and timely.
  • Maintain accountability for company-owned tools, diagnostic equipment, and shop resources.
  • Maintain a clean, organized, and safe work area.
  • Comply with all Company policies, OSHA regulations, environmental requirements, hazardous waste procedures, and applicable federal, state, and local regulations.
  • Immediately report unsafe conditions, equipment deficiencies, accidents, or injuries.
  • Support operational requirements, including overtime, weekends, or emergency repairs as needed.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Invisible Technologies makes AI work. Our end-to-end AI platform structures messy data, automates digital workflows, deploys agentic solutions, measures outcomes, and integrates human expertise where it matters most.

Our platform cleans, labels, and structures company data so it is ready for AI. It adapts models to each business and adds human expertise when needed, the same approach we have used to improve models for more than 80% of the world’s top AI companies, including Microsoft, AWS, and Cohere.

Our successes span industries, from supply chain automation for Swiss Gear to AI-enabled naval simulations with SAIC, and validating NBA draft picks for the Charlotte Hornets.

Profitable for more than half a decade, Invisible reached $134M in revenue and ranked as the number two fastest growing AI company on the 2024 Inc. 5000. In September 2025, we raised $100M in growth capital to accelerate our mission of making AI actually work in the enterprise and to advance our platform technology.

About The Role

As a Software Engineer, Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) you'll work directly with clients and our internal delivery teams to build and deploy AI-powered solutions that transform how work gets done. You’ll own projects end-to-end: scoping ambiguous problems, prototyping AI workflows, and deploying scalable systems on top of our products — all while interfacing with technical and non-technical stakeholders.

This is a hybrid role: equal parts AI engineer, software builder, and technical consultant. It's perfect for someone who wants to be hands-on with models and close to the impact they generate.

What You’ll Do

  • Collaborate with delivery leaders to scope technical solutions to operational problems
  • Identify workflow optimizations through deep engagement with customer problems and work to build into a stable and scalable solution
  • Design and implement AI-powered workflows using LLMs, embedding models, retrieval systems, and automation tools
  • Translate messy real-world constraints (e.g., inconsistent data, latency requirements) into elegant engineering solutions
  • Iterate quickly based on real-time feedback from operators and clients
  • Build reusable tooling and infrastructure that accelerates future deployments

What We Need

  • Hands-on experience in software engineering or ML engineering — through professional roles, internships, or coursework/research projects
  • Strong Python skills and familiarity with libraries like PyTorch, Hugging Face, LangChain, or OpenAI APIs
  • Solid understanding of data pipelines, APIs, and production deployment (e.g., Docker, FastAPI, GCP/AWS)
  • Experience building usable systems from messy data and ambiguous requirements
  • Strong communication skills — you can explain technical decisions to delivery teams and client stakeholders
  • Entrepreneurial mindset and comfort working in fast-moving, unstructured environments
  • Be willing to be on-call for our customers when situations arise
  • Travel: Willingness to travel for on-site client engagements as needed
  • Onsite: Available to work from the office a few days per week, depending on team needs

What’s In It For You

Invisible is committed to fair and competitive pay, ensuring that compensation reflects both market conditions and the value each team member brings. Our salary structure accounts for regional differences in cost of living while maintaining internal equity.

The annual salary range for this position, depending on level, is: $93,000 - $217,000 USD

You can find more information about our geographic pay tiers here. During the interview process, your Invisible Talent Acquisition Partner will confirm which tier applies to your location. For candidates outside the U.S., compensation is adjusted to reflect local market conditions and cost of living.

*Bonuses and equity are included in all full-time offers. Final compensation is determined by a combination of factors, including location, job-related experience, skills, knowledge, internal pay equity, and overall market conditions. Because of this, every offer is unique. Additional details on total compensation and benefits will be discussed during the hiring process.

What It's Like to Work at Invisible:

At Invisible, we’re not just redefining work—we’re reinventing it. We operate at the intersection of advanced AI and human ingenuity, pushing the boundaries of what’s possible to unlock productivity and scale. Ownership is at the core of everything we do. Here, you won’t just execute tasks—you’ll build, innovate, and shape the future alongside world-class clients pushing the boundaries of AI.

We expect bold ideas, relentless drive, and the ability to turn ambiguity into opportunity. The pace is fast, the challenges are big, and the growth is unmatched. We’re not for everyone, and we’re okay with that. If you’re looking for predictable routines, this isn’t the place for you. But if you’re driven to create, thrive in dynamic environments, and want a front-row seat to the AI revolution, you’ll fit right in.

title: Health Information Scanning Analyst
description:
Overview

Our team members are the heart of what makes us better.

At Hackensack Meridian Health we help our patients live better, healthier lives — and we help one another to succeed. With a culture rooted in connection and collaboration, our employees are team members. Here, competitive benefits are just the beginning. It’s also about how we support one another and how we show up for our community.

Together, we keep getting better - advancing our mission to transform healthcare and serve as a leader of positive change.

The Deficiency Tracking/Susp Analyst is responsible for compiling, organizing and analyzing patient medical records for Hospital Inpatient and Hospital Outpatient services to support the network goals for accuracy, timeliness and completeness for purposes of continued patient care, revenue and compliance with Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), New Jersey Department of Health (NJDOH), The Joint Commission (TJC) and the Hackensack Meridian Health (HMH) Network policies and procedures.

This is an onsite evening shift position. The hours are 3pm-11:30pm, Monday-Friday and every other weekend. This position requires record retrievals from various areas of the hospital.

Responsibilities

A day in the life of a Deficiency Tracking/Susp Analyst at Hackensack Meridian Health includes:

  • Retrieves paper records of all discharged patients from the nursing units in each campus.
  • Ensures all discharged charts are accounted for, utilizing the Chart Reconciliation work queue in Epic.
  • Creates a list of all charts not received and communicates with nursing and ancillary staff to resolve status.
  • Organizes and assembles charts to remove documents that should not be scanned into the legal medical record and ensures that each page has the correct patient information.
  • Prepares medical records for scanning including labeling of documents removing staples and tape.
  • Scans documents into the legal medical record ensuring the complete original document is scanned appropriately for data integrity.
  • Performs quality control (QC) of all scanned images for accuracy of the patient chart- image is exact replica of the original paper document. Rescans and reindexes original document when necessary according to procedure.
  • Investigates, analyzes, verifies patient information utilizing multiple hospital computer applications to perform Document Corrections to maintain the accuracy and integrity of the patient record.
  • Assists with medical record merging of potential duplicates as necessary and accurately completes potential duplicate merges as per departmental policy.
  • Accurately reviews and analyzes HI deficiencies in Epic with a 98% accuracy rate which includes selecting the responsible physician(s).
  • Performs re-analysis of records accurately ensuring information meets regulatory requirements regarding content.
  • Continuously monitors and reviews Chart Deficiency work queues ensuring timeliness and accuracy.
  • As appropriate, performs physician suspension process by sending notification to the providers on their delinquent records.
  • Assists physicians in the completion of their medical record deficiencies as needed.
  • Performs release of information as necessary.
  • Assists patients with MyChart issues, providing verification codes, password assistance, and proxy access.
  • On a timely basis, requests archived medical records from the storage vendor as needed.
  • Answers the telephone within three rings identifying self and the department.
  • Responds professionally and addresses the caller's needs appropriately.
  • Routes medical record requests received to the ROI vendor.
  • Advises Coordinator or Supervisor on situations requiring follow-up.
  • Required to meet specific performance metrics of productivity, accuracy and quality assurance.
  • Other duties and/or projects as assigned.
  • Adheres to HMH Organizational competencies and standards of behavior.

Qualifications

Education, Knowledge, Skills and Abilities Required:

  • High School diploma, general equivalency diploma (GED), and/or GED equivalent programs.
  • Good organizational and communication skills.
  • Computer literate.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Proficient computer skills including such as Microsoft Office and Google Suite platforms.
  • This role can and may require you to bend, lift, and carry up to 10lbs of weight for extended periods of time.
  • This role can and may require you to walk and/or travel as needed to different floors, buildings, and sites within the HMH network to retrieve necessary documentation.

Education, Knowledge, Skills and Abilities Preferred:

  • Experience in health information or health care or related field.

If you feel the above description speaks directly to your strengths and capabilities, then please apply today!

Starting Minimum Rate

Minimum rate of $21.73 Hourly

Job Posting Disclosure

HMH is committed to pay equity and transparency for our team members. The posted rate of pay in this job posting is a reasonable good faith estimate of the minimum base pay for this role at the time of posting in accordance with the New Jersey Pay Transparency Act and does not reflect the full value of our market-competitive total rewards package. The starting rate of pay is provided for informational purposes only and is not a guarantee of a specific offer. Posted hourly rates may be stated as an annual salary in the offer and posted annual salaries may be stated as an hourly rate in the offer, depending on the level and nature of the job duties and credentials of the candidate. The base compensation determined at the time of the offer may be different than the posted rate of pay based on a number of non-discriminatory factors, including but not limited to: Labor Market Data: Compensation is benchmarked against market data to ensure competitiveness. Experience: Years of relevant work experience. Education and Certifications: Level of education attained, including specialized certifications, credentials, completed apprenticeship programs or advanced training. Skills: Demonstrated proficiency in relevant skills and competencies. Geographic Location: Cost of living and market rates for the specific location. Internal Equity: Compensation is determined in a manner consistent with compensation ranges for similar roles within the organization. Budget and Grant Funding: Departmental budgets and any grant funding associated with the job position may impact the pay that can be offered. Some jobs may also be eligible for performance-based incentives, bonuses, or commissions not reflected in the starting rate. Certain positions may also be eligible for shift differentials for work performed on evening, night, or weekend shifts. In addition to our compensation for full-time and part-time (20+ hours/week) job positions, HMH offers a comprehensive benefits package, including health, dental, vision, paid leave, tuition reimbursement, and retirement benefits.

title: Senior Planner - Men's Accessories
description:
Since 2011, THE ICONIC has redefined the future of retail in Australia and New Zealand. As the #1 fashion e-commerce & lifestyle destination in the region, our e-commerce platforms provide an inspiring and seamless end-to-end customer experience through our own technology innovations.

  • Works cross-functionally, establishing strong relationships with key departments. Uses these relationships to strengthen department’s position

From our ways of working to our growth mindset and sustainable approach, we each add unique value and have an incredible amount of fun doing it! People are our greatest asset and our ICONITE experience is designed to empower you to do your best work.

Here’s what to expect when you join THE ICONIC:

We are committed to making it easy for everyone to apply. If you require accessibility support or any adjustments during the recruitment process, please send an email to talent.attraction@theiconic.com.au

title: Senior Business Analyst - Manufacturing
description:

As an integral member of the IT FX/ MFG 4.0 Solution Portfolio team, the candidate needs to apply a high level of business systems analysis expertise in the Manufactory area. The candidate should have working knowledge on a manufacturing environment. Besides having extensive knowledge of Manufactory domain, Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), also need process/ digital solution Understanding with Warehouse Management Systems (WMS), Supply Chain/ costing domains such as Order Management, Inventory, Warehouse, Shipping, Transportation, Work in Process, Bills of Materials, and Purchasing, Standard costing would be an advantage. The candidate would lead analysis for conversion of existing legacy data, lead regression testing, and provide analyses and specifications for development work for any new or changed system requirements, to train, implement, and support business processes. Documents business policies, practices and procedures to meet company standards and user needs. Leverages existing system's standard functionality to implement efficient and consistent Avery Dennison Global processes and procedures. Brings a level of functional and technical knowledge of Manufactory Execution System/ Advance Production Scheduling Digital Solutions.

Key Responsibilities

  • Translate business objectives into requirements and functional specifications, supporting document creation and automation efforts.

  • Utilize business analysis, data mapping and data validation to assist the development of coding specifications.

  • Manages the execution of testing for assigned deliverables; identify and document test defects, document quality issues and communicate defects to assure resolution.

  • Prepares test and training plans. Develops training materials and delivers formal training for each new

In addition, tests and prepares new functionality as made available or as business requirements indicate. Ensures patches and upgrades are applied prior to production implementation.

  • English Proficiency: Fluent/Proficient in English (both written and spoken) with exceptional communication skills, confident in leading workshops and coordinating independently with MFG4.0 team, global IT, site leaders, and external vendors. Mandarin is a plus.

  • Very logical thinker. Very organized and structured in methodology and work habits.

  • Ability to see a need and provide a solution even if before being asked to provide a solution. Capable of performing analyst type tasks to understand and evaluate the business process/ requirement / change and define in detail the logical solution to the business need, using existing functionality or specifying upgrades to functionality to resolve business problems.

  • Assertive leadership, with effective skills in gaining internal customers’ - management and users’ - cooperation and acceptance of changes.

  • Training skills -- ability to organize, develop and deliver effective training using presentation, interaction and feedback. Prepare materials to facilitate hands-on learning.

  • Strong creativity and troubleshooting skills required, with ability to logically isolate and resolve complex problems, whether business or system oriented.

  • Willingness and ability to travel frequently domestic and international.

  • Independent workers - must be able to self-manage to a large part while planning and reporting task progress to supervisor and team.

Our offer
