Overview

Job Summary

Counts receipts from the previous day, encodes checks, balances the register against reports and enters data into the computer system. Consistently provides friendly, courteous customer service to internal and external customers. Performs other related work.

Typical Duties and Responsibilities

  • Seeks opportunities to welcome, engage, serve and thank customers. Maintains an atmosphere of friendly, enthusiastic customer service with an emphasis of taking care of the customer.
  • Totals applicable coupons and void/refund sheets by gathering checks, food stamps and coupons from registers and sorting coupons.
  • Verifies balance in the safe by counting all monies found therein by balancing against a total for the day, operating a computer, counting down the tills and insuring the right amount of dollar denominations are in the tills.
  • Balances the Money Transfer transactions, money order receipts and lotto machine against related information.
  • Provides information to General Office by running reports, inputting data by computer terminal, verifying cash and food stamps, preparing deposits, and inputting department sales and item counts.
  • Processes bad checks by inputting, writing-off checks and sending checks to proper entities (i.e., police, collection agency, etc.).
  • Performs accounts receivable by inputting data, billing the customer, sending statements, etc.
  • Deposits pop machine money by gathering money from vending machines and operating a money counter machine.
  • Performs duties with honesty and integrity.
  • Performs other duties as assigned or needed.

Requirements

Education:

  • High School Diploma or equivalent

Experience:

  • Performing 10 key by touch.
  • Counting money and performing basic mathematical calculations (add, subtract, divide and multiply).

Ability to:

  • Consistently provide friendly, courteous service to internal and external customers.
  • Work varied shifts between 3:00 am and 1:00 pm in a 24/7 operation; including night, weekends and holidays.
  • Reach cash register keys.
  • Remember various codes and understand/perform duties related to the bookkeeping system.
  • Sit for extended periods of time.
  • Visually read reports, computer screen, etc.
  • Perform tasks requiring manual dexterity (e.g., paperwork, filing, stapling, sorting, collating, etc.).
  • Lift 20 lbs. of coins in a bag.
  • Exhibit interpersonal skills through oral and written communication.
  • Must be 18 years of age or older.
  • Perform primary duties with efficiency and accuracy.

Additional Requirements:

  • Food Handlers Certification (Per State Laws).

Machines and Equipment Operated:

  • Office machines (computer terminal, copier/scanner, 10-key, fax machine, telephone, etc)
  • Encoder, Coin Counter, Currency Counter.

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature of work performed by the employees assigned to this job. All employees must comply with Company policies and applicable laws. The responsibilities, duties and qualifications required of personnel may vary.

EEO/Inclusivity

As the WinCo Foods community continues to grow, our variety of perspectives and wide range of experiences are essential to our strategy and success. We are committed cultivating and celebrating an inclusive environment in which all employees are valued and respected.

title: Team Leader, SRE
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Team Leader, SRE based in Portugal.

As Team Leader, SRE, you’ll lead a highly technical Site Reliability Engineering team responsible for the reliability of critical cloud infrastructure and developer platforms.
The role combines approximately 60% hands-on technical contribution with 40% people leadership, giving you meaningful influence over both engineering direction and team development.
You’ll work across Kubernetes, AWS, PostgreSQL, CI infrastructure, observability, security, and reliability practices.
You’ll help evolve a growing SRE function, strengthening SLOs, incident response, on-call practices, and operational excellence.
At the same time, you’ll own the career development, performance, hiring, and overall health of your team.
The environment is fully remote and asynchronous, requiring strong written communication, autonomy, and thoughtful prioritization.
This is an opportunity to shape reliability practices while remaining close enough to the technology to guide decisions and lead through complex incidents.

Accountabilities

  • Lead and develop an SRE team, owning the full career lifecycle of direct reports, including onboarding, feedback, performance management, progression, and hiring.
  • Coach engineers on both technical craft and interpersonal skills, creating clear opportunities for growth and development.
  • Foster a healthy, collaborative team environment by understanding team dynamics, addressing conflicts constructively, and maintaining effective retrospective practices.
  • Represent the SRE team across engineering and with senior leadership, communicating priorities, challenges, progress, and technical direction.
  • Define and prioritize SRE objectives, balancing operational commitments with project delivery and protecting the team's focus.
  • Own the support rotation and on-call model, ensuring sustainable operational coverage and effective incident response.
  • Provide technical leadership across core infrastructure, including Kubernetes, AWS, PostgreSQL, DNS, TLS, CI infrastructure, and related platform services.
  • Drive the evolution of reliability practices, including Service Level Objectives (SLOs), error budgets, incident management, observability, and post-incident improvements.
  • Partner with Security teams on infrastructure threats, patching, security controls, audits, and compliance requirements.
  • Oversee infrastructure-related vendor relationships, including renewals and commercial discussions in collaboration with senior leadership.
  • Stay hands-on enough to review technical work, challenge architectural decisions, contribute to complex problems, and provide credible technical direction during incidents.
  • Help mature the organization's reliability practices by identifying operational gaps and turning lessons from incidents into lasting engineering improvements.
  • Balance short-term operational demands with longer-term platform investments and engineering goals.

    • Requirements:

    • Proven experience leading an SRE, infrastructure, platform, or DevOps engineering team, with direct responsibility for team members' growth, performance, and career progression.
    • Strong people-management and coaching skills, with demonstrated ability to develop engineers and provide clear, constructive feedback.
    • Experience hiring engineers and assessing both technical capability and broader engineering judgment.
    • Strong conflict-resolution and team-dynamics skills, with the ability to build commitment around shared organizational goals.
    • Deep hands-on experience in Site Reliability Engineering, DevOps, cloud infrastructure, or a closely related discipline.
    • Production experience with Kubernetes, including operational troubleshooting, reliability, scaling, and real-world failure scenarios.
    • Significant experience with AWS and cloud infrastructure at meaningful scale.
    • Hands-on experience building, enabling, or scaling AI infrastructure.
    • Strong understanding of observability principles and practices.
    • Experience with Infrastructure as Code, particularly Terraform.
    • Experience with CI/CD platforms such as GitLab CI, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, or comparable technologies.
    • Strong knowledge of Docker and shell scripting.
    • Experience owning or operating reliability practices including incident response, on-call, SLOs, error budgets, and post-incident improvement processes.
    • Previous experience working in regulated environments and understanding the associated operational and compliance requirements.
    • Exceptional prioritization skills, particularly when operational workload competes with project delivery.
    • Strong written communication skills and comfort working in an asynchronous, globally distributed environment.
    • Ability to build strong relationships across engineering and become a trusted partner for teams bringing reliability challenges forward.
    • Experience with a backend programming language such as Elixir, Java, Clojure, Node.js, Python, or similar is a plus.
    • Familiarity with modern observability technologies such as OpenTelemetry, distributed tracing, or Honeycomb is advantageous.
    • Experience with PostgreSQL or Aurora operations, including performance, connection pools, and query optimization, is beneficial.
    • Experience administering Linux systems outside cloud environments is a plus.
    • Knowledge of infrastructure security from both defensive and offensive perspectives is advantageous.
    • Familiarity with cloud cost management and FinOps is beneficial.
    • Experience growing an engineering team from a small starting point, including establishing hiring standards, is a plus.
    • Fluent English communication skills are required.
    • Ability to work effectively in a fully remote and asynchronous environment.

      • Benefits:

      • Fully remote working environment.
      • Flexible, asynchronous working model that allows you to organize your schedule around your life.
      • Opportunity to work with a globally distributed engineering organization.
      • Significant ownership over both technical direction and people development.
      • Approximately 60% individual-contributor technical work and 40% leadership responsibilities.
      • Opportunity to shape and mature an evolving SRE and reliability practice.

title: Compliance Product Owner
description:
This is your opportunity to help shape the digital solutions supporting Orifarm's Compliance and Quality capabilities

About the job

We are looking for an experienced Compliance Product Owner to take ownership of the digital capabilities supporting Orifarm's Compliance and Quality processes.

In this role, you will be responsible for ensuring that our Compliance solutions continue to create business value, support regulatory adherence, and enable efficient and scalable ways of working. You will be responsible for managing and developing the digital capabilities supporting Compliance, Quality, Governance, Training, Document Management, and other regulated business processes.

The role combines elements of product ownership, compliance expertise, demand management, business engagement, and technical support. You will work closely with stakeholders across the organization to understand business needs, regulatory requirements, and compliance risks, translating them into actionable priorities and ensuring solutions are delivered and adopted successfully.

Success in the role is measured not only by delivering technology, but by strengthening compliance processes, reducing risk, improving audit readiness, and enabling measurable business outcomes.

Your key responsibilities will include:

  • Own and manage the roadmap, backlog, and priorities for Compliance platforms and digital capabilities
  • Partner with Compliance, Quality, Regulatory Affairs, and business stakeholders to translate regulatory requirements, risks, and improvement opportunities into actionable priorities
  • Drive end-to-end delivery from requirement definition and prioritization through implementation, adoption, and value realization
  • Ensure Compliance solutions remain secure, compliant, auditable, and aligned with internal policies and external regulatory requirements
  • Identify opportunities to standardize, automate, and improve compliance processes while managing key vendors and strategic partners

Who are you?

You enjoy working at the intersection of business, compliance, and technology and understand how digital solutions can enable compliant, efficient, and scalable operations in a regulated environment. You are able to move comfortably between strategic discussions and operational challenges, building strong relationships across both business and IT.

You are a pragmatic and proactive problem solver who can balance competing priorities, challenge existing ways of working constructively and take ownership of outcomes. You have a customer focus, as well as a focus on delivering real business value while maintaining compliance and governance standards.

Most importantly, you understand that technology is only successful when it is adopted, supports regulatory obligations, and creates measurable business outcomes.

We imagine that you have:

  • Experience as a Product Owner, Application Manager, Process Owner, System Admin, or similar role within a regulated environment
  • Strong understanding of Compliance, Quality, Regulatory Affairs, or GxP-regulated business processes
  • Experience with enterprise platforms such as Veeva Vaults, AssurX, Extedo, Ennov, MasterControl, ETQ Reliance, or similar (technical knowledge will be beneficial)
  • Strong stakeholder management skills with the ability to bridge business and IT
  • Fluent English skills and the ability to translate complex business and regulatory requirements into practical digital solutions

Who are we?

As the Compliance Product Owner, you will act as the primary link between Compliance stakeholders and Corporate IT. You will work closely with Compliance, Quality, Regulatory Affairs, Corporate IT, vendors, and external partners while helping shape the future of Orifarm's compliance technology landscape.

Compliance is a critical enabler of Orifarm's ability to operate across regulated markets and maintain the trust of health authorities, partners, customers, and patients. Our ability to meet regulatory requirements, maintain effective quality processes, and demonstrate audit readiness depends on robust governance, strong data foundations, and the right digital solutions.

Why should you join Orifarm?

At Orifarm, we are 2,300 employees united by a shared purpose: improving access to affordable medicine for the people who need it. Founded in Odense, Denmark in 1994 by Birgitte & Hans Bøgh-Sørensen, we have built our business on challenging conventional thinking to make affordable high-quality pharmaceuticals more accessible across Europe. Rather than developing new medicines, we focus on finding smarter ways to bring existing treatments to patients, creating value for pharmacies, healthcare systems, and society.

We live by the mindset Challenge Accepted. It reflects our explorer spirit and can-do attitude, where challenges are perceived as opportunities. We encourage people to ask questions, challenge assumptions, and take ownership. Across teams, functions, and markets, you will find a collaborative and supportive culture built on trust, respect, and a flat hierarchy where everyone has a voice and direct access to decision-makers.

When you join Orifarm, you will be empowered to make a real impact from day one. We offer autonomy and great opportunities for career advancement, enabling our employees to shape their professional development. We value flexibility and provide a hybrid work model with the possibility of working from home two days a week.

We invite you to join Orifarm, if you are curious, ambitious, and accept the challenge of bringing better deals of medicine to millions.

We encourage everyone to apply

At Orifarm, we welcome people from all backgrounds, recognizing that the best outcomes come from a diverse and inclusive work environment. Our commitment is to create an environment where different perspectives and skills drive innovation and contribute to a sustainable future. By creating such an environment, we are confident that we can achieve better results together.

description:
What we are looking for

SCS Engineers is looking for an energetic, forward-thinking Environmental Scientist or Environmental Engineer to join our Portland, Oregon office. You should be organized, embrace teamwork, and have the desire to grow professionally.

This position would be a hybrid of office and field-oriented technical work. Environmental surveys, sampling, and other field activities are an important basis for understanding the science and work underlying overall project work and opportunities for career growth.

How you can make an impact

  • Ability to work safely and efficiently in both office and field.
  • A mixture of office and field work expected; up to 20% field during the year; sometimes a week or more in the field for limited times during the year.
  • Manage small projects, or assist with managing larger projects, based on previous experience.
  • Coordinate, perform and/or manage field work for multiple projects.
  • Communicate with clients for field work coordination.
  • Sample multi-media: soil, soil vapor, groundwater, indoor air, methane, surface water, sediment, etc.
  • Record data during field work, which could include, but not limited to, soil characteristics, groundwater and surface water data, photographs, and summaries of visual observations through photography and written field logs in accordance with standard operating procedures.
  • Evaluate and interpret data recorded during field work for reporting purposes and to help determine future project needs in coordination with the project manager.
  • Complete quality control reviews of lab data and other work products.
  • Conduct Phase I Environmental Site Assessments and Phase II Investigations following ASTM Standards, based on experience level.
  • Design or provide design support for projects, in concert with senior engineering staff, based on experience level.
  • Oversee contractors during field activities for regulatory and safety compliance.
  • Report writing and preparation of supporting documentation including Phase I/II Environmental Site Assessments and groundwater and stormwater compliance reporting.
  • Field days at job sites throughout Oregon and Washington, or in other states, can be expected with this position.
  • Communicate project status, schedules and compliance issues with project managers.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's Degree in Geology, Environmental Science, Engineering or related field required.
  • At least two years of related experience required; more than 5 years of experience preferred.
  • Progress towards professional licensing (GIT, EIT) preferred, if applicable (geologists, engineers).
  • Experience with standard field equipment (multi-meters, pumps, controllers, etc.) preferred but not required.
  • HAZWOPER training completed and up to date preferred but not required.
  • Familiarity with water quality, environmental regulations, and environmental assessment/remediation preferred but not required.
  • Familiarity with Microsoft Office or similar software suites required.
  • Detail-oriented and a team player with good communication, technical writing, analytical, organizational, and time management skills.
  • Valid driver's license with driving record in good standing required.

Pay Range

USD $65,000.00 - USD $85,000.00 /Yr.

title: 22709 - Probation Service Officer - Newcastle
company: His Majesty's Prison and Probation Service
description:
Where applicants provide multiple location preferences, reserve lists will be managed in accordance with location preference/s, as indicated in your application. We will appoint in merit list order for each location outlined in the vacancy and hold a separate locational reserve list for each of these locations. After appointments have been made using this locational appointment process, any remaining candidates who met the benchmark for the role will remain on a locational reserve list in accordance with their preferences for 12 months.

Please only indicate preferences where you are prepared to work. If you are subsequently offered a role from the reserve list for a location preference indicated in your application and decline it, you will be removed from the reserve list for the vacancy, across all locational preferences.

All offers of employment will be made strictly in merit order, based on your performance throughout the recruitment process. Candidates at the top of the merit list will be offered vacancies as they arise in their chosen locations.

Once you have accepted an offer for a role, you will be withdrawn from any other live applications for the same role and will no longer be considered for those vacancies.

The addresses listed in the job advertisement are not an exhaustive list of potential base locations, they give an indication of some of the potential locations you could be based at.

We will therefore endeavour to offer you a vacancy within a 60-minute commute of your home location.

New entrants to the Civil Service will be expected to join at the entry point salary for the advertised band.

Existing Civil Servants will have their salary calculated in accordance with the Departments pay on transfer / pay on promotion rules.

The post is currently advertised without VISOR Vetting to enable appointment to take place as soon as possible, however, VISOR vetting will be required to be completed in post offer.

Some PSO roles require the completion of an apprenticeship as part of the required learning and development. You will be advised on commencement in role if you are required to complete it.

Working Arrangements & Further Information

The MoJ offers Hybrid Working arrangements where business need allows. This is an informal, non-contractual form of flexible working that blends working from your base location, different MoJ sites and / or from home (please be aware that this role can only be worked in the UK and not overseas). Some roles will not be suitable for Hybrid Working. Similarly, Hybrid Working will not suit everyone’s circumstances. Arrangements will be discussed and agreed with the successful candidate(s) and subject to regular review.

For nationally advertised roles, the successful candidate(s) will be appointed to a MoJ office location, which may include their nearest Justice Collaboration Centre or Justice Satellite Office. This will be discussed and agreed on the completion of pre-employment checks.

Some of MoJ’s terms and conditions of service are changing as part of Civil Service reform. The changes will apply to staff joining MoJ who are new to the Civil Service. Staff joining MoJ from other civil service employers will transfer onto the new MoJ terms if they are already on 'modernised' terms in their current post or onto 'unmodernised' MoJ terms if they are on 'unmodernised' terms at their current post. Details will be available if an offer is made.

Standard full time working hours are 37 hours per week excluding breaks which are unpaid. HMPPS welcomes part-time, flexible and job-sharing working patterns, where they meet the demands of the role and business needs. All applications for part-time, flexible and job-sharing working patterns will be considered in accordance with the HMPPS’ Flexible Working policy.

Benefits

The MoJ offers a range of benefits:

Annual Leave

Annual leave is 25 days on appointment and will increase to 30 days after five years’ service, plus public holidays. Leave for part-time and job share posts will be calculated on a pro-rata basis

Pension

The National Probation Service is covered by the Local Government Pension Scheme (LGPS) run through the Greater Manchester Pension Fund (GMPF). Please visit www.gmpf.org.uk for further information.

Please note: Any current Civil Servant who is a member of the PCSPS, by accepting an offer of employment to the National Probation Services will be opted out of the PCSPS and auto enrolled into the Local Government Pension Scheme.

Training

The Ministry of Justice is committed to staff development and offers an extensive range of training and development opportunities.

Networks

The opportunity to join employee-run networks that have been established to provide advice and support and to enable the views of employees from minority groups to be expressed direct to senior management. There are currently networks for employees of minority ethnic origin, employees with disabilities, employees with caring responsibilities, women employees, and lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgender.

Eligibility

All candidates are subject to security and identity checks prior to taking up post

Support

  • A range of ‘Family Friendly’ policies such as opportunities to work reduced hours or job share.
  • Access to flexible benefits such as voluntary benefits, retail vouchers and discounts on a range of goods and services.
  • For moves to or from another employer or moves across the Civil Service this can have implications on your eligibility to carry on claiming childcare vouchers. You may however be eligible for alternative government childcare support schemes, including Tax Free Childcare. More information can be found on or Childcare Choices. You can determine your eligibility at .
  • Paid paternity, adoption and maternity leave.
  • Free annual sight tests for employees who use computer screens.

Working for the Civil Service

The Civil Service Code sets out the standards of behaviour expected of civil servants.

We recruit by merit on the basis of fair and open competition, as outlined in the Civil Service Commission's recruitment principles. Should you feel that the recruitment process has breached the recruitment principles you are able to raise a formal complaint in the following order

  • To Transformative Business Services (0345 241 5358 (Monday to Friday 8am - 6pm) or e mail moj-recruitment-vetting-enquiries@resourcing.soprasteria.co.uk);
  • To Ministry of Justice Resourcing team (resourcing-management-office@justice.gov.uk);
  • To the Civil Service Commission (details available here)

As a Disability Confident employer, MoJ are committed to providing everyone with the opportunity to demonstrate their skills, talent and abilities, by making adjustments throughout all elements of the recruitment process and in the workplace. MoJ are able to offer an interview to disabled candidates who meet the minimum selection criteria, except in a limited number of campaigns.

You will be able to request reasonable adjustments to the recruitment process within the application form. If you need additional help completing the application form, please contact the TBS Recruitment Enquiries Team.

For more information on applying for a role as a candidate with a disability or long-term condition, please watch our animated videos.

Diversity & Inclusion

The Civil Service is committed to attract, retain and invest in talent wherever it is found. To learn more please see the Civil Service People Plan and the Civil Service Diversity and Inclusion Strategy.

A Great Place to Work for Veterans

The "Making the Civil Service a Great Place to work for veterans" initiative includes a guaranteed interview scheme to those who meet the minimum criteria to provide eligible former members of the Armed Forces with opportunities to secure rewarding jobs. Allowing veterans to continue to serve their country, and to bring highly skilled individuals with a broad range of experience into the Civil Service in an environment, which recognises and values your previous service in the Armed Forces.
For further details about the initiative and eligibility requirements visit:

Redeployment Interview Scheme

Civil Service departments are expected to explore redeployment opportunities before making an individual redundant. The MoJ is committed, as part of the Redeployment Interview Scheme, to providing opportunities to those who are 'at risk of redundancy'.

MoJ is able to offer an interview to eligible candidates who meet the minimum selection criteria, except in a limited number of campaigns. Candidates will not be eligible for the Redeployment Interview Scheme if they are applying on promotion.

Civil Service Nationality Rules

This job is broadly open to the following groups:

  • UK nationals
  • nationals of the Republic of Ireland
  • nationals of Commonwealth countries who have the right to work in the UK
  • nationals of the EU, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland or Liechtenstein and family members of those nationalities with settled or pre-settled status under the European Union Settlement Scheme (EUSS) (opens in a new window) https://www.gov.uk/settled-status-eu-citizens-families
  • nationals of the EU, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland or Liechtenstein and family members of those nationalities who have made a valid application for settled or pre-settled status under the European Union Settlement Scheme (EUSS)
  • individuals with limited leave to remain or indefinite leave to remain who were eligible to apply for EUSS on or before 31 December 2020
  • Turkish nationals, and certain family members of Turkish nationals, who have accrued the right to work in the Civil Service

Further information on nationality requirements (opens in a new window) https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/nationality-rules

Reserve list

A reserve list may be held for up to 12 months from which further appointments may be made for the same or similar roles.

title: Sr. Configuration Management Specialist
location: San Luis Obispo, California, United States
description:
At Zone 5 Technologies, we're redefining what's possible in unmanned aircraft systems. Our team of engineers and innovators is developing cutting-edge autonomous solutions that push the boundaries of UAS technology - solving complex challenges that matter.

We're building the future of UAS capabilities, and we're looking for exceptional talent to join us. If you're driven by hard problems, energized by rapid innovation, and ready to make an impact on next-generation flight systems, you belong here.

Position Overview

Join our growing aerospace and defense organization as a Senior Configuration Management Specialist (Level III). This role independently executes and coordinates configuration management across assigned programs, products, and lifecycle phases. The specialist partners with Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Software, Systems Engineering, and Program Management to maintain configuration integrity from concept and development through production, delivery, and sustainment.

The Level III specialist serves as a trusted program CM practitioner and may lead defined workstreams, facilitate change-control activities, and mentor less-experienced team members. This is an individual-contributor position aligned to enterprise CM governance and direction from the Senior Configuration Manager.

This is one onsite position with location flexibility. The selected candidate may be based at the Dallas-Fort Worth, Fort Walton Beach, or San Luis Obispo site and should identify their preferred location when applying.

What You Will Do

  • Own day-to-day configuration management execution for assigned programs, products, and projects while ensuring alignment with enterprise policies, program plans, contracts, and applicable industry requirements.
  • Develop and maintain program configuration management plans, procedures, work instructions, checklists, and lifecycle records under enterprise CM governance.
  • Establish, document, and maintain configuration identification and product structures for hardware, software, firmware, documentation, interfaces, and technical data.
  • Coordinate functional, allocated, product, production, as-built, as-tested, and as-maintained baseline activities as required by the program lifecycle and contract.
  • Support and facilitate Configuration Control Boards (CCBs) and Software Configuration Control Boards (SCCBs), including agenda preparation, change-package readiness, stakeholder coordination, decision records, and action tracking.
  • Review engineering change requests, engineering change orders, deviations, waivers, problem reports, and related change documentation for completeness, traceability, classification, effectivity, and implementation planning.
  • Maintain configuration status accounting for approved changes, baselines, releases, effectivity, serial applicability, open actions, implementation status, and technical data deliveries.
  • Verify that approved changes are fully implemented across affected drawings, specifications, bills of material, work instructions, software repositories, test artifacts, planning records, and downstream business systems.
  • Help maintain alignment among requirements, design data, EBOMs, MBOMs, SBOMs, ERP/MRP, MES, QMS, PDM/PLM, and software-development repositories to strengthen the digital thread.
  • Perform release-readiness and baseline-completeness reviews before production, test, delivery, or major technical milestones.
  • Support functional and physical configuration audits, production readiness reviews, first article activities, customer reviews, and internal or external compliance assessments.
  • Identify and resolve configuration discrepancies involving engineering data, manufacturing planning, software versions, effectivity, serialized product records, and as-built documentation.
  • Coordinate configuration records and technical data packages required for customer delivery, contractual reporting, audit readiness, and product acceptance.
  • Contribute configuration management scope, assumptions, schedules, risks, deliverables, and basis-of-estimate inputs to proposals and program planning activities.
  • Develop program-level metrics and concise status reports covering change throughput, aging actions, baseline health, release readiness, implementation completion, and emerging CM risks.
  • Provide practical CM guidance and training to cross-functional stakeholders and mentor junior CM personnel in established processes and tools.
  • Collaborate across operating sites to promote consistent execution while addressing local program and production needs.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in engineering, systems engineering, information management, business, or a related discipline, with at least five years of relevant configuration management experience; an equivalent combination of education and directly applicable experience may be considered.
  • Hands-on experience performing configuration identification, change control, status accounting, baseline management, release management, implementation verification, and configuration audits.
  • Experience supporting complex hardware, software, firmware, or integrated product development in aerospace, defense, manufacturing, or another highly regulated environment.
  • Working knowledge of engineering drawings, specifications, bills of material, part and document revision control, effectivity, serialization, and product lifecycle records.
  • Ability to evaluate change packages for cross-functional impact and trace changes through engineering, manufacturing, quality, supply chain, test, software, and delivery records.
Pay range for this role
$103,000—$131,000 USD

What's in it for you:

Benefits:

  • Competitive total compensation package
  • Comprehensive benefit package options include medical, dental, vision, life, and more.
  • 401k with company-match
  • 3 weeks of paid time off each year
  • 40 hours of sick time
  • 12 annual company holidays

Why Join Zone 5 Technologies?

  • Innovative Environment: Work on cutting-edge technology that is shaping the future of defense and aerospace.
  • Collaborative Culture: Join a team of passionate professionals dedicated to pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.
  • Career Growth: Opportunities for professional development and career advancement.

If you are passionate about unmanned aircraft technology and want to be a part of a dynamic and growing company, we would love to hear from you. Apply today and join the Zone 5 Technologies team!

title: Cabling Technician
description:
About Technology Plus:

Since 1995, Technology Plus has been a trusted technology partner for businesses, offering expertise in IT, Telecom, Cabling, Security, and Audio/Visual services. We pride ourselves on delivering personalized service that empowers our clients to focus on what they do best. As we continue to evolve, we're looking for a Cabling Technician to join our dynamic team!

Why You'll Love Working Here:

  • Family-Oriented Culture: We believe in work-life balance and foster a supportive, collaborative environment.

Position Overview:

We are seeking a dependable and motivated Cabling Technician who enjoys hands-on work and working as part of a team.

As a Cabling Technician, you'll assist with the installation, maintenance, and organization of low-voltage cabling and related equipment at client locations. This role involves working with structured cabling systems used for data, voice, security, and other technology solutions. You'll work alongside experienced team members to complete installations safely, accurately, and efficiently while providing professional service to our clients.

This is a full-time, hourly position (Monday to Friday, generally 8 AM - 5 PM) based in Louisville, KY. Work locations will vary based on client and project needs and may include offices, warehouses, construction sites, and other commercial environments. Occasional outdoor work may also be required.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Cable Installation: Assist with pulling, routing, securing, labeling, and organizing low-voltage cable, including data and voice cabling.
  • Equipment Installation: Assist with installing cable pathways, racks, jacks, faceplates, and other related equipment.
  • Termination and Testing: Assist with terminating and testing cabling to ensure proper installation and connectivity.
  • Project Support: Work with team members to complete cabling projects according to project requirements and timelines.
  • Troubleshooting: Assist with identifying and resolving basic cabling and connectivity issues.
  • Job Site Organization: Maintain clean, organized, and safe work areas and properly care for company tools and equipment.
  • Documentation: Accurately label cabling and equipment and assist with maintaining project documentation as needed.
  • Safety: Follow company safety procedures and job-site requirements while using ladders, tools, and other equipment.
  • Client Service: Maintain a professional and courteous presence when working at client locations.
  • Training: Participate in training and development opportunities to expand cabling and installation skills.

What We're Looking For:

  • High school diploma or equivalent preferred.
  • Previous experience with low-voltage cabling, construction, electrical work, installation, or a related field is preferred but not required.
  • Ability to use basic hand and power tools safely.
  • Mechanical aptitude and willingness to learn.
  • Ability to follow instructions and work both independently and as part of a team.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality work.
  • Dependable attendance and punctuality.
  • Professional communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to travel to client and project locations as required.
  • Ability to perform the physical requirements of the position, including standing, walking, bending, reaching, climbing ladders, and lifting and carrying materials and equipment.

Why Join Technology Plus?

At Technology Plus, we foster a welcoming and collaborative team environment. You'll be part of a company that values quality work, teamwork, and professional growth. Whether you're bringing previous cabling experience or looking to continue building your skills in the technology industry, you'll have the opportunity to learn from an experienced team and contribute to projects that make a difference for our clients.

Ready to Apply?

If you're dependable, detail-oriented, enjoy hands-on work, and are interested in growing your skills in the technology industry, we want to hear from you! Apply today and become part of the Technology Plus family.

title: Assistant Director of TAY Rapid Rehousing
description:
Mission Statement

Through the use of social and restorative justice principles, Five Keys provides traditionally underserved communities the opportunity to improve their lives through a focus on the Five Keys: EDUCATION, EMPLOYMENT, RECOVERY, FAMILY, COMMUNITY.

Rehousing Programs

Five Keys has case management contracts with the San Francisco Department of Homelessness and Supportive Housing (HSH) for a number of re-housing programs designed to place people who are unhoused or are guests in temporary shelters into permanent housing on the private market with temporary subsidies or permanent vouchers. These programs include Rising Up for transitional aged youth, Adult Rapid Rehousing, Flexible Pool Subsidy Program, and Emergency Housing Vouchers for returning citizens. Five Keys is contracted to provide individualized care management for participants who are placed into these programs through the coordinated entry system. These programs are complex partnerships between various organizations in San Francisco– including HSH, the Office of Economic and Workforce Development, the SF Department of Public Health, and multiple community-based agencies that provide housing location and rental subsidy services.

Five Keys Overview

Five Keys is a nonprofit organization that operates an extensive network of programs across California. With a presence in 14 counties and over 120 locations, Five Keys focuses on various initiatives aimed at empowering individuals and families to overcome poverty and inequity. The organization's programs encompass a wide range of services, including public charter schools, restorative justice programs in jails and prisons, shelters, permanent supportive housing, and the development of new housing and support programs. At Five Keys, the overarching objective is to uplift individuals and families by providing them with essential resources. This includes education, housing, employment, and the necessary tools to sustain their progress. By offering these fundamental elements, the organization aims to create positive and lasting change in communities, making them better places for everyone.

Our Core Competencies

A well qualified candidate has the capacity to communicate effectively, collaborate with others while building positive relationships, demonstrates strong problem solving skills, has a dynamic learning mindset, and remains committed to a high level of cultural and social awareness. A successful candidate will work well under pressure, observe appropriate boundaries and operate with a high degree of emotional intelligence.

What it’s really like to join our agency…

At Five Keys, culture matters. Culture is at the very core of everything we do and impact on a daily basis. We’ve made a commitment to building an inclusive culture that seeks collaboration over hierarchy to create empowered work teams. We serve vulnerable populations daily and we strive to approach everyone with compassion, patience and a trauma informed approach. We choose to push past discomfort to have difficult conversations to impact the greater good. This allows us the opportunity to collaboratively create an inclusive culture and transform the world around us.

BENEFITS

We offer very low monthly costs for medical, dental, and vision insurance, along with generous time off! Various pre-tax flexible spending accounts and retirement account 403(b) are available. We provide annual reimbursements up to $100 towards gym membership, smoking cessation, and weight loss programs. Annual athletic event participation and annual massages are reimbursed up to $50. Other Company-paid benefits, including free wellness-related apps, an Employee Assistance Program, and a comprehensive mental health care platform, are available to you and your dependents.

title: Investigator 3 (PCN 084063)
description:
Job Description

Division of Insurance is recruiting for an Investigator 3 to join our team.

This position is an Insurance Investigator in the 4-person Investigation Unit in the Anchorage office. The Investigation Unit investigates telephonic, oral and written complaints of insurance fraud in compliance with Alaska Statute. Under general direction of the Division of Insurance, Chief Investigator and Assistant Attorney General’s office this position provides investigative reports reflecting effective civil and/or criminal investigations. The Investigator 3 has standardized policies and procedures that affect investigations and the preparation of cases.

Our organization, mission and culture:
The mission of the Division of Insurance is to regulate the insurance industry to protect Alaskan consumers. The Division of Insurance is a small division that consists of 48 positions split between Anchorage and Juneau with the Director based in Anchorage and the Deputy Director based in Juneau. The Investigation section within the division fosters a positive, diverse and respectful environment. We encourage innovative ideas, personal growth and team participation.

The benefits of joining our team:
At the Division of Insurance, you will be joining a team of highly competent professionals who work together effectively and efficiently to support the division’s mission of protecting Alaskan consumers. You will be working in a friendly and supportive environment that fosters accountability, cooperation, respect for each other and professionalism. We offer training opportunities, and a comprehensive employee benefits package to include health insurance, retirement and paid holidays.

Where you will be working:
Currently located on the 15th floor of the Atwood Building, you will enjoy a panoramic view of downtown Anchorage, Mt. Susitna aka Sleeping Lady, and the Knik Arm. Great dining, shopping, the Park Strip, Anchorage Museum and Atwood Concert Hall are all within short walking distance from the office. Covered parking at the Linny Pacillo parking garage is provided free. When you come to work, you will be walking into a calm and respectful work environment where everyone knows your name.

To be successful in this position a candidate will need the following core competencies:

  • Adaptability: Adjusts planned work by gathering relevant information and applying critical thinking to address multiple demands and competing priorities in a changing environment.

  • Attention to Detail: Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail.

  • Compliance Inspection: Knowledge of the guidelines, regulations, and procedures associated with compliance inquiries, including application of compliance rules and criteria and ability to make appropriate decisions and issue citations, fines, or orders.

  • Information Management: Identifies a need for and knows where or how to gather information; organizes and maintains information or information management systems.

  • Interpersonal Skills: Shows understanding, friendliness, courtesy, tact, empathy, concern, and politeness to others; develops and maintains effective relationships with others; may include effectively dealing with individuals who are difficult, hostile, or distressed; relates well to people from varied backgrounds and different situations; is sensitive to cultural diversity, race, gender, disabilities, and other individual differences.

Special Notice:
This position requires the ability to qualify for a Special Commission Department of Public Safety. Ability to travel state-wide and outside Alaska and be willing to work irregular or unusual work hours during the course of an investigation. Background check by the Department of Public Safety may be conducted.

Minimum Qualifications

Any combination of education and/or experience that provides the applicant with competencies in

  • Accountability: Holds self and others accountable for measurable high-quality, timely, and cost-effective results. Determines objectives, sets priorities, and delegates work. Accepts responsibility for own actions and decisions. Complies with established control systems and rules.

  • Analytical Thinking/Problem Solving: uses a logical, systematic, sequential approach to address problems or opportunities or manage a situation by drawing on one’s knowledge and experience base and calling on other references and resources as necessary.

  • Integrity/Honesty: Contributes to maintaining the integrity of the organization; displays high standards of ethical conduct and understands the impact of violating these standards on an organization, self, and others; is trustworthy.

  • Investigation: Knowledge of the guidelines, regulations, and procedures associated with investigation, including interviewing, evidence detection, locating, gathering, and handling, and drawing appropriate factual inferences and conclusions. Provide oral or written reports of findings. Presenting evidence and providing testimony.

  • Law: Knowledge of State and federal laws, including legal and court procedures, regulations, guidelines, precedents, admissibility of evidence, case preparation, and/or settlements for applicable areas of law practiced or supported.

Equivalent to those typically gained by:
Any combination of preparatory post-secondary education and/or progressively responsible investigative work experience performing duties such as locating and gathering information, evidence and/or testimony to be used in civil or criminal proceedings, administrative actions, or governmentally regulated activities which included preparing reports in support of attorneys or agencies engaged in administrative adjudication, and/or detecting and verify suspected fraud, licensing violations, and other violations of state law.

Definitions:
“Competencies” means a combination of interrelated knowledge, skills, abilities, and behaviors that enable a person to act effectively in a job or situation.

“Typically gained by” means the prevalent, usual method of gaining the competencies expected for entry into the job.

“Training” and “education” in this guidance are synonyms for the process of acquiring knowledge and skills through instruction. It includes instruction through
formal and informal methods (such as classroom, on-line, self-study, and on-the-job), from accredited and unaccredited sources, and long-duration (such as a post-secondary degree) and short-duration (such as a seminar) programs.

“Progressively responsible” means indicating growth and/or advancement in complexity, difficulty, or level of responsibility.

Special Note:
Some positions in this class may require eligibility for commission as a Special Officer with the State of Alaska as a condition of hire.

Some positions require applicants pass a background investigation, which includes a criminal record check for conviction of felony or misdemeanor crimes, as a prerequisite to employment.

Some positions require incumbents possess an Alaska driver's license and operate a motor vehicle.

Additional Required Information

At time of application applicant(s) are requested to submit:

  1. Three (3) professional references that have had supervisory responsibility over you along with their daytime contact phone numbers;
  2. Copies of your three (3) most recent performance evaluations;
  3. Proof of successful completion of a recognized law enforcement academy; and
  4. Cover letter per instructions below.

Cover Letter Instructions:
Please include a cover letter (attached to your application) that illustrates your experience with the competencies listed in this job posting. If you do not have experience in each area, please say so. Explain why you are the best qualified for this position. Also, detail your Knowledge, Skills and Ability (KSA's) as they relate to the position description.

Education:
If post-secondary education is required to meet the minimum qualifications, you must fill in the Education section of the application. If you have not obtained a degree, please indicate the number of units completed. Copies of transcripts are required to verify educational credentials if used to meet the minimum qualifications for a position. Transcripts must be attached at the time the application is submitted.

Work Experience:
If using work experience in order to meet the minimum qualifications of the position and it is not already documented in your application, also provide the employer's name, your job title, dates of employment, and whether full-or part-time. Applications will be reviewed to determine if the responses are supported and minimum qualifications are clearly met. If they are not, the applicant may not advance to the interview and selection phase of the recruitment.

Multiple Vacancies:
This recruitment may be used for more than one (1) vacancy. The applicant pool acquired during this recruitment may be used for future vacancies for up to ninety (90) days after this recruitment closes. Interested applicants are encouraged to apply to each recruitment notice to ensure consideration for all vacancies.

title: Business Analyst, Senior
description:
Infor IQ is a new component of Infor Data Fabric. It builds an ontology over Infor’s CloudSuite ERP products — the entities, relationships, actions, business rules, and policies that describe how core business objects behave — so that people and AI agents can query it, reason over it, and act on it with results that are explainable and auditable.


This role decides what that ontology should say. You will translate ERP business processes into precise, testable requirements, validate that the resulting model reflects how the business actually works, prototype proposed experiences to remove design risk early, and track the competitive landscape. You will work closely with product management, engineering, UX, and domain experts.


· Translate ERP business processes, including order-to-cash, procure-to-pay, plan-to-produce, and related industry variants, into ontology requirements that define entities, relationships, permitted actions, rules, and policies.


· Write structured, testable specifications for technical design and implementation, including end-to-end use cases, acceptance criteria, traceability, and documented decisions.


· Build working prototypes with AI tooling to support UX design, gather stakeholder feedback, and reduce design risk before engineering investment.


· Conduct competitive and market analysis across semantic layer, knowledge graph, and metadata catalog solutions, and translate findings into roadmap input.


· Validate ontology outputs by reviewing schema-to-ontology mappings, data dictionaries, enumerations, and relationships against source data and documented ERP behavior.


· Partner with application development and content development teams to create ontology content for enterprise applications, including domain models, vocabularies, and rule sets.


· Facilitate workshops with domain experts, demonstrate working software, prepare written briefings for executive and engineering audiences, and support backlog grooming with product management and engineering.


· Experience as a business analyst, product analyst, functional consultant, or product owner supporting enterprise software, ERP, or enterprise data platforms.


· Experience writing specifications, use cases, acceptance criteria, and documentation that support engineering design and implementation.


· Functional knowledge of at least one ERP domain, including documents, statuses, workflows, and business process behavior.


· Data modeling knowledge, including conceptual, logical, and physical models; keys; cardinality; normalization; schema review; and SQL.


· Experience building domain-model or ontology content for enterprise applications.


· Experience with business process automation, including governance, approvals, escalations, observability, and human-in-the-loop controls.



· Knowledge graph or semantic web experience, such as RDF, OWL, SPARQL, SHACL, or formal conceptual modeling.


· Background in analytics, business intelligence, data catalog, master data management, or data governance.


· Experience with analytical models, KPIs, reports, dashboards, or related data products.


· Multi-tenant SaaS product experience.


· Experience with Palantir Foundry, Microsoft Fabric IQ, or similar ontology and process automation products.


· Experience with data lake, lakehouse, or data transformation tooling such as dbt.


· Experience working in issue-tracking and collaborative documentation tools.

title: Bakım & Onarım Çalışanı
description:
Rol Hakkında

Bakım & Onarım Çalışanı olarak, üretim tesisimizdeki makine ve ekipmanların kesintisiz, güvenli ve verimli bir şekilde çalışmasını sağlamaktan sorumlu olacaksınız. Bu rol, koruyucu ve önleyici bakım faaliyetlerinin yürütülmesini, arızalara zamanında müdahale edilmesini ve üretim sürekliliğinin desteklenmesini amaçlamaktadır.

Temel Sorumluluklar

  • Vardiya süresince üretim hattındaki makine ve ekipmanların periyodik bakım ve onarım faaliyetlerini gerçekleştirmek (Saha içi / On-site).
  • Arıza durumlarında hızlı ve etkili müdahalelerle duruş sürelerini en aza indirmek.
  • Bakım ve onarım süreçlerinde iş sağlığı, güvenliği ve çevre (EHS) standartlarına tam uyum sağlamak.
  • Ekipman performansını artırmaya yönelik iyileştirme ve revizyon çalışmalarına destek vermek.
  • Yedek parça takibini yapmak ve kullanılan malzemelerin düzenli kaydını tutmak.

Gerekli Nitelikler

  • Meslek Yüksekokulları veya Teknik Liselerin Elektrik, Elektronik, Makine, Mekatronik veya Bakım Onarım bölümlerinden mezun olmak.
  • Üretim tesislerinde veya endüstriyel ortamda bakım/onarım alanında deneyim sahibi olmak.
  • Vardiyalı çalışma düzenine ve esnek çalışma saatlerine uyum sağlayabilmek.

Başarılı Olmak İçin İhtiyacınız Olan Beceriler

  • Problem çözme ve teknik arıza tespit yeteneğine sahip olmak.
  • Takım çalışmasına yatkın olmak ve güçlü iletişim becerileri sergilemek.

Neler Sunuyoruz?

Sizi bekleyen harika yan haklara kısa bir bakış:

  • Finansal ve Sağlık Yan Hakları: Sağlık sigortasının yanı sıra Sosyal Yardım, Gıda, Bayram, Servis, Yemek ve Yakacak ödeneklerini içeren çeşitli yardımlar sunuyoruz.
  • İzinler: Kıdemle birlikte artan, en az 16 günlük Yıllık İznin tadını çıkarın; ayrıca önemli hayat olayları için özel ücretli izinler de sağlıyoruz.
  • Sürekli Gelişim: Üretim çalışanları için performans yönetim sistemi ve çeşitli şirket içi eğitimlerle gelişiminize yatırım yapıyoruz.
  • Kurumsal Sosyal Sorumluluk: Sivil Toplum Kuruluşlarını (STK) desteklemek amacıyla gönüllülük faaliyetlerine katılma fırsatları sunuyoruz.

Neden Avery Dennison'a Katılmalısınız?

We are a global materials science and digital identification solutions company with locations in over 50 countries, and approximately 35,000 employees worldwide. As a science and innovation company, we believe that diverse teams are stronger teams. We are committed to fostering a culture of curiosity and courage, where you can grow your career with a company that has innovation in its DNA. Founded on creating real-world impact to enable a better future, we strive to provide an open, collaborative culture where diversity of thought is encouraged and respected. Hear from our employees about what it's like working at Avery Dennison. Learn more at www.averydennison.com.

Fırsat Eşitliği Sunan İşveren

Avery Dennison fırsat eşitliği sunan bir işverendir. Bütün nitelikli adaylar; ırk, renk, din, cinsiyet, ulusal köken, cinsel yönelim, cinsiyet kimliği, engellilik durumu, korunan gazilik statüsü veya korunan diğer herhangi bir statüye bakılmaksızın işe alımda değerlendirmeye alınır. Engellilik durumunuz nedeniyle online başvuru sürecimizi kullanamıyorsanız, uygun bir düzenleme (accommodation) talebinde bulunmak için lütfen bizimle iletişime geçin: Requestaccomodation@eu.averydennison.com. EMEA bölgesinde Elevate, Unite ve Mental Health grubumuz gibi aktif Çalışan Kaynak Grupları (ERG'ler) aracılığıyla kapsayıcı bir kültürü destekliyoruz. Çeşitlilik, Hakkaniyet ve Kapsayıcılık (DE&I) yaklaşımımız hakkında daha fazla bilgi edinmek için lütfen DE&I sayfamızı ziyaret edin.

Ücret Şeffaflığı Beyanı

Yukarıdaki işe alım temel maaş aralığı, Avery Dennison'ın bu ilan tarihi itibarıyla bu pozisyon için ödemeyi makul ölçüde beklediği tutarı temsil etmektedir. Gerçek maaşlar bu aralık içinde değişebilir ve bazı durumlarda adayın ilgili becerileri, deneyimi, eğitimi ve konumu ile pozisyonun gerektirdiği ve adayın havuzuna bağlı olarak değişebilecek iş kapsamı, karmaşıklığı, sorumlulukları ve düzenli/gerekli seyahatler dahil ancak bunlarla sınırlı olmamak üzere çeşitli faktörlere bağlı olarak aralığın üstünde veya altında olabilir. title: Personal Operations Assistant
description:
Steel City represents more than just a location on the map, it’s the story of the American Dream, to build something that you’re proud of. We all have a story, we all love our family, our hometown and our sports teams. It’s what connects us and binds us together. It’s our mission to tell those stories through our clothing.


We're looking for a part-time Personal Operations Assistant who is extremely resourceful, organized, and loves figuring things

out and getting things done.


This is not a traditional Executive Assistant role. You won’t spend your day managing a calendar, sitting in meetings, or organizing an inbox. Instead, you’ll be handed problems, projects, and loose ends — and own them through completion. One day that might mean finding and vetting a contractor for a property. Another might be researching a vendor, getting three quotes, handling a return, resolving an issue with a service provider, scheduling a repair, researching options for a purchase, or following up on something that’s been sitting unfinished. The goal is simple: take things off the owner’s plate and close the loop.


What You’ll Do

• Research and vet vendors, contractors, products, services, and solutions

• Contact vendors, request quotes, compare options, and make recommendations

• Follow up persistently until projects are completed

• Schedule and coordinate appointments, repairs, deliveries, and services

• Handle returns, warranties, order issues, and customer-service problems

• Research solutions to personal and business problems

• Coordinate occasional household and property projects

• Assist with travel, reservations, purchases, and other personal logistics

• Help with miscellaneous business projects and vendor coordination

• Maintain a simple running list of open projects and make sure nothing falls through the cracks

PURPOSE STATEMENT:

Plan, direct and implement activity therapy programs as a component of the patient’s treatment plan.

Responsibilities

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

  • Complete activity assessment through patient observation and patient/family interview, obtaining information on the patient’s needs, skills, interests and limitations for the development and implementation of the treatment plan.
  • Plan, organize, direct and implement the activities within the treatment program to facility patient progress with treatment goals.
  • Plan and implement an activities program including but not limited to therapeutic leisure skills and activities, leisure education and leisure awareness.
  • Facilitate and lead activity sessions to improve patient mental and physical well-being.
  • Instruct patients in activities and techniques, such are sports, dance, music, art or relaxation techniques designed to meet their specific needs.
  • Develop treatment plans and implement activity interventions that meet patient needs and interests and helps the patient achieve his/her treatment goals.
  • Engage patients in therapeutic activities, such as exercise, games and community outings.
  • Help patients learn social skills needed to become or remain independent.
  • Modify activities to suit the needs of specific groups.
  • Demonstrate a positive, empathetic and professional attitude towards customers always. When patient needs are not met, acknowledge and work to resolve complaints. Recognize that patient safety is a top priority.

OTHER FUNCTIONS:

title: Human-Centered Design Specialist IV - Technical Design
description:
Overview

LMI is seeking an experienced Human-Centered Design (HCD) Specialist IV - Technical Design to support the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) portfolio. This role will apply human-centered design methods to the design and modernization of technical products, platforms, workflows, dashboards, and digital experiences supporting VA stakeholders and end users.

The successful candidate will combine strong HCD expertise with technical fluency, enabling them to understand business and user needs, work effectively with technical teams, and translate research findings into designs that can be implemented within enterprise technology environments. This individual will lead design efforts for solutions such as Microsoft Power Platform applications and dashboards, SharePoint experiences, data visualization products, workflow tools, and other digital solutions.

This is a design-focused role rather than a software development position. The HCD Specialist will develop the user experience, information architecture, workflows, wireframes, prototypes, and design specifications and partner closely with developers and technical teams for implementation.

As a Level IV individual contributor, this position is expected to independently lead complex HCD workstreams, solve ambiguous design challenges, develop advanced design solutions, and deliver high-quality work with limited oversight. The individual will also collaborate with LMI's broader HCD community of practice to promote consistent methods, standards, and lessons learned

LMI is a new breed of digital solutions provider dedicated to accelerating government impact with innovation and speed. Investing in technology and prototypes ahead of need, LMI brings commercial-grade platforms and mission-ready AI to federal agencies at commercial speed.

Leveraging our mission-ready technology and solutions, proven expertise in federal deployment, and strategic relationships, we enhance outcomes for the government, efficiently and effectively. With a focus on agility and collaboration, LMI serves the defense, space, healthcare, and energy sectors—helping agencies navigate complexity and outpace change. Headquartered in Tysons, Virginia, LMI is committed to delivering impactful results that strengthen missions and drive lasting value.

Responsibilities

Human-Centered Technical Design

  • Lead end-to-end HCD activities for new technical solutions, major enhancements, and redesign efforts.
  • Translate stakeholder and user needs into intuitive, usable, accessible, and technically feasible digital experiences.
  • Design experiences for solutions that may include Microsoft Power Platform applications and dashboards, SharePoint sites and solutions, analytics products, workflow tools, and other enterprise digital platforms.
  • Develop information architectures, navigation structures, user flows, task flows, process flows, and interaction models.
  • Create low-, medium-, and high-fidelity wireframes, mockups, clickable prototypes, and design concepts.
  • Develop clear design specifications and developer handoff materials that enable technical teams to implement approved designs.
  • Partner with developers, solution architects, analysts, product owners, and technical leads to understand platform capabilities and constraints and ensure designs are feasible for implementation.
  • Review implemented solutions against approved designs and user experience requirements and recommend refinements when appropriate.

HCD Discovery and Research

  • Plan and conduct stakeholder interviews, user interviews, discovery sessions, contextual inquiry, workshops, usability testing, and other qualitative research activities.
  • Identify user needs, pain points, goals, workflows, constraints, and opportunities through structured HCD research.
  • Synthesize qualitative findings into themes, insights, design principles, user needs, and actionable recommendations.
  • Develop personas, journey maps, experience maps, service blueprints, workflows, and other HCD artifacts as appropriate.
  • Validate design concepts through stakeholder feedback, prototype testing, and usability testing.
  • Iterate designs based on research findings, technical considerations, accessibility requirements, and user feedback.

Magnify Reports and HCD Documentation

  • Contribute to and, when assigned, lead development of Magnify Reports, the formal HCD deliverable produced for each SBIR contract.
  • Translate research and design activities into clear documentation of stakeholder needs, user insights, findings, opportunities, recommendations, and proposed design approaches.
  • Create executive-ready presentations and visual artifacts that communicate HCD findings and design recommendations to VA and LMI stakeholders.
  • Maintain clear documentation connecting research findings to design decisions.

Accessibility and Inclusive Design

  • Incorporate Section 508, WCAG, accessibility, and inclusive-design principles throughout the design process.
  • Design experiences that account for users with varying levels of technical proficiency, accessibility needs, roles, and work environments.
  • Partner with development and testing teams to identify potential accessibility concerns early in the solution lifecycle.

Collaboration and HCD Practice

  • Work collaboratively across multidisciplinary teams that may include developers, analysts, data scientists, program evaluators, healthcare subject matter experts, product owners, and program leadership.
  • Facilitate collaborative design sessions, design reviews, and working sessions with technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Clearly communicate design rationale, research findings, tradeoffs, and recommendations.
  • Participate in LMI's HCD community of practice, sharing methods, templates, design approaches, lessons learned, and reusable assets.
  • Promote practical application of HCD throughout technical delivery without serving as a formal people manager.
  • Work within Agile, Scrum, Kanban, or hybrid delivery environments and incorporate HCD activities into iterative development cycles.

Qualifications

Required

  • Bachelor's degree in Human-Centered Design, Human-Computer Interaction, Interaction Design, UX Design, Information Design, Psychology, Information Systems, or a related field.
  • 7+ years of experience in human-centered design, UX design, product design, service design, interaction design, or a related discipline.
  • Demonstrated experience independently leading complex digital product or enterprise-technology design efforts.
  • Strong experience conducting stakeholder and user research and translating findings into actionable design recommendations.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop wireframes, user flows, information architectures, journey maps, interactive prototypes, and detailed design specifications.
  • Proficiency with modern design and prototyping tools such as Figma, Adobe XD, Sketch, Axure, Miro, or comparable tools.
  • Experience working collaboratively with software developers, architects, analysts, and technical teams.
  • Technical fluency sufficient to design solutions within enterprise platforms and communicate effectively with development teams.
  • Understanding of Microsoft Power Platform, SharePoint, enterprise dashboards, data visualization, workflow systems, or comparable technologies.
  • Knowledge of Section 508, WCAG, accessibility, and inclusive-design principles.
  • Excellent stakeholder interviewing, facilitation, presentation, and communication skills.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to operate independently in ambiguous environments.
  • Ability to manage and prioritize multiple concurrent design and research activities.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a Public Trust clearance.

Desired

  • Master's degree in Human-Centered Design, Human-Computer Interaction, UX Design, Design, Psychology, Information Systems, or a related field.
  • Portfolio demonstrating HCD methodology, UX research, wireframes, prototypes, enterprise application design, dashboard design, or other digital product work.
  • Prior experience supporting the Department of Veterans Affairs, Veterans Health Administration, or other federal healthcare organizations.
  • Experience designing Power Platform, Power BI, SharePoint, or other Microsoft 365-based experiences.
  • Experience supporting federal digital modernization or enterprise technology programs.
  • Experience with service design, systems thinking, Lean UX, Design Thinking, or Agile product development.
  • Experience developing formal research reports, executive-level recommendations, or HCD deliverables for government clients.
  • Relevant HCD, UX, accessibility, Agile, or Microsoft certifications.

Target salary range: $100,000 - $150,000.

Individual salaries are determined by various factors including, but not limited to location, internal equity, business considerations, client contract requirements, and candidate qualifications, such as education, experience, skills, and security clearances.

The Development Coordinator plays an integral role in creating an exceptional donor experience and supporting the school’s efforts to cultivate a culture of generosity and mission partnership.
